text:
🇮🇱🇸🇦 Netanyahu’s Secret Visit to Saudi Arabia and the IMEC Plan to Bypass Iran and Challenge China

In 2017, Israel Katz, then Israel’s minister of transportation and intelligence, had a plan to redraw the trade map connecting India, West Asia, and Europe. The idea had two clear goals: bypass Iran and create a strategic counterweight to China’s Belt and Road Initiative.

Inspired by the historic Hejaz Railway, built during the Ottoman era, Katz envisioned a rail network linking the Mediterranean port of Haifa through Jordan to Saudi Arabia and the Persian Gulf. It was an ambitious vision, one that sought to reshape regional trade routes and change how goods moved between Asia and Europe.

Prof. Michael Tanchum helped turn the idea of a trade corridor linking India to Europe through West Asia into a detailed strategic blueprint. An associate fellow at the Middle East Institute, he teaches international relations and political economy at the University of Navarra in Spain. He is also a senior fellow at the Austrian Institute for European and Security Policy.

In August 2021, following the 2020 Abraham Accords, Tanchum published a policy paper titled “India’s Arab-Mediterranean Corridor: A Paradigm Shift in Strategic Connectivity to Europe.” It laid out a multimodal shipping and rail route connecting Mumbai to the UAE, crossing Saudi Arabia and Jordan to Haifa, and continuing toward European ports such as Piraeus in Greece.

The paper mapped out a vision for connecting India and Europe through the Arabian Peninsula and the Levant, helping establish an early strategic blueprint for the corridor concept that would later feature prominently in regional connectivity discussions.

One part of that effort was I2U2, a partnership linking India, Israel, the UAE, and the United States.

On July 14, 2022, India, Israel, the UAE, and the United States held their first I2U2 leaders’ meeting virtually, with Narendra Modi and Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan (MBZ) joining remotely.

Netanyahu returned to power in late December 2022, bringing a new phase of political leadership to Israel as the regional connectivity agenda continued to develop.

But an idea is one thing. Turning it into an agreement between governments is another. That would require negotiations, political commitments, and a plan ambitious enough to connect India, West Asia, and Europe.

The breakthrough came in May 2023 in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, where Indian National Security Adviser Ajit Doval met with U.S. National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan, White House energy envoy Amos Hochstein, MBS, and UAE National Security Adviser Sheikh Tahnoun bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The discussions helped advance the framework for the proposed corridor.

Then came a crucial meeting with Mohammed bin Salman (MBS).

On August 28, 2023, an electrical malfunction over the Red Sea forced an Air Seychelles Airbus A320, Flight HM22, carrying 128 Israeli passengers from the Seychelles to Tel Aviv, to make an emergency night landing in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. That same night, Netanyahu met MBS at a palace structure inside King Abdulaziz International Airport to discuss the proposed corridor, bringing an unexpected aviation incident into the middle of a much larger diplomatic effort to reshape regional trade and transport routes.

Israel presented the stop as a gesture of goodwill. Washington was working to establish formal relations between Israel and Saudi Arabia, but such a move carried political risks for MBS at home and across the region. The visit was designed as a trial balloon to test Saudi public opinion and gauge the potential backlash.

The groundwork had begun a year earlier. On August 3, 2022, Air Seychelles became the first airline to operate a commercial flight from Israel across Saudi Arabian airspace on a route that did not pass through the Persian Gulf.

These flights and meetings marked steps toward closer ties. But the central question remained: how far could MBS go toward normalization with Israel without provoking a political repercussion?

Less than two weeks later, the plan moved into the open.

On September 9, 2023, on the sidelines of the G20 Summit in New Delhi, eight signatories formally unveiled the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor, or IMEC: India, the United States, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, France, Germany, Italy, and the European Union.

The route was ambitious. It would connect India's Mundra port to Israel's Haifa port through the UAE, then link the network to Europe through Greece.

Iran would be bypassed. China was the other major consideration.

For Netanyahu, IMEC offered a chance to strengthen Israel's economy by expanding access to India's vast market while challenging China's growing influence through its Belt and Road Initiative. It was a trade corridor, but it also carried strategic ambitions.

There was one problem. The entire vision depended on a stable region.

Ports, railways, and shipping links can be planned on paper. Keeping them connected is another matter when war threatens the routes themselves.

Now, with the current war and the advances made by Iran and Yemen, IMEC's future looks increasingly bleak. A project built on regional connectivity faces a fundamental contradiction: the more conflict threatens the region, the harder it becomes to establish the very connections the corridor was designed to create.

The question is no longer just whether IMEC can redraw the trade map between India, West Asia, and Europe. It is whether the regional conditions it needs will exist at all.

Washington now faces a difficult strategic trade-off:

text:
There can now be precious little confidence in Donald Trump’s professed desire to secure a just and lasting peace in Ukraine, or indeed in his commitment to the peace and security of Europe.

The United States Congress passed legislation expressly intended to weaken Putin’s war machine through severe economic sanctions. Yet Donald Trump, having signed that very legislation into law, has now issued an executive order suspending its principal provisions, mere days before they were due to take effect.

The contradiction is as extraordinary as it is deeply troubling. At the very moment when Congress sought to tighten the economic stranglehold on Moscow, the President of the United States chose instead to loosen it. Whatever justification Washington may offer, the practical consequence is to afford Putin precisely the breathing space that Congress intended to deny him.

One must therefore ask whose interests are truly being served. Certainly, it is difficult to see how such a decision advances the cause of Ukraine, a sovereign European nation whose people continue to endure the appalling consequences of Russia’s unprovoked aggression.

The increasingly erratic pronouncements and deeply questionable decisions emerging from the White House should serve as a stark warning to the international community. America’s traditional allies must now confront an uncomfortable reality: the assurances upon which European security has depended for generations can no longer be accepted without question.

The forthcoming American midterm elections have consequently assumed a significance extending far beyond the domestic affairs of the United States. At stake are the constitutional checks upon presidential power, the credibility of NATO, the security of Europe and the preservation of an international order painstakingly constructed in the aftermath of two devastating world wars.

What makes this moment particularly alarming is the apparent disregard for the lessons of history. Peace is not secured by indulging aggression, rewarding territorial conquest or weakening the collective resolve of democratic nations. Such conduct risks emboldening those who regard military force, rather than international law, as the ultimate instrument of political ambition.

We should harbour no illusions about the gravity of the present circumstances. The possibility of a wider European conflict, with consequences reaching far beyond the continent and potentially involving nuclear powers, is no longer a danger that responsible governments can afford to dismiss.

Donald Trump may continue to proclaim himself a peacemaker, but grand declarations are rendered meaningless when contradicted by the decisions of the man making them. The measure of any statesman lies not in the extravagance of his promises, but in the consequences of his actions.

And those consequences now demand the most searching scrutiny, for the price of political recklessness on this scale may ultimately be paid not merely by the people of Ukraine, but by generations who had every right to expect that the catastrophic lessons of the twentieth century would never again be so casually disregarded.

But no criminal indictments:

Whether Elon Musk's political giveaways constitute voter bribery has been the subject of significant legal debate, public scrutiny, and formal legal challenges, though he has not been convicted of criminal voter bribery.
For official details regarding voter registration, election rules, or local electoral processes, refer to the U.S. Election Assistance Commission.
Background on the Allegations
The concerns around voter bribery stem from sweepstakes and financial incentives offered through Musk's political action committee, America PAC:
The 2024 Presidential Election Giveaway: During the 2024 presidential campaign, Musk's PAC offered daily $1 million prizes to individuals in key swing states who signed a petition supporting the First and Second Amendments. To be eligible, signers were required to be registered voters. Legal experts and watchdog groups argued this violated federal law—which prohibits offering financial compensation to induce people to register or vote. Musk and his lawyers defended the program by stating the payments were compensation for serving as spokespeople for the PAC rather than a direct payment for registering or voting.
The 2025 Wisconsin Election Giveaways: Musk offered similar $1 million checks during the 2025 Wisconsin Supreme Court election. The Wisconsin Elections Commission later reviewed the matter and found by a 5–1 vote that the payments likely violated state election bribery laws.

text:
Citizen Lab just documented the first confirmed case of mercenary spyware delivered through targeted advertising infrastructure. They're calling it AdFection. The short version: Discover Tech figured out how to turn ad-tech into a zero-click infection pipeline.

Sit with that for a second. Not the novelty of it. The logic of it.

Every previous delivery method had a seam. A link the target had to click, a document they had to open, a message that could be flagged. Even sophisticated zero-click exploits through iMessage or WhatsApp required initiating contact with the target. Defenders could tell people: don't click unknown links, use hardened messaging apps, be suspicious of inbound communications. That advice wasn't perfect but it was something.

AdFection closes that seam. The infection arrives inside normal advertising requests. The same background noise that follows every webpage load, every app session, every morning scroll through the news. There's no trigger for the target to avoid because the target never sees a trigger. The ad-tech stack just does what it always does, except this time a spyware payload comes along for the ride.

The targeting is the part that should focus minds. Advertising platforms offer granular segmentation by device ID, location history, behavioral profile, demographic characteristics. Intelligence services already purchase commercial data from brokers. The infrastructure to identify and reach a specific journalist in Tbilisi or a specific dissident's device in London already exists and is for sale. AdFection means that infrastructure can now be used not just to profile someone but to infect them.

Watch the next 18 months carefully.

The vendors who aren't Discover Tech are reverse-engineering this right now. NSO, Candiru, and the less-documented operators in the commercial spyware market have consistently adapted whenever a delivery method got burned. When iMessage exploits drew scrutiny, they moved channels. When WhatsApp patched the gap, they moved again. AdFection represents a new channel, one with structural advantages that previous methods lacked: scale, plausible deniability, and the near-impossibility of opting out.

That last part is the real problem for defenders. A journalist can switch to Signal. They can use a hardened device. They can treat every inbound link as suspicious. They cannot stop their device from receiving advertising requests. Avoiding ad-tech at that level means functionally abandoning the internet, and even then the attack surface in apps and mobile infrastructure is enormous. The threat model for high-risk individuals just got significantly worse, and there's no behavioral patch available.

The attribution angle matters too. Routing an attack through commercial advertising infrastructure creates genuine ambiguity. The delivery mechanism is shared with billions of legitimate ad impressions daily. Forensically separating a weaponized ad request from a normal one is hard. Attributing the decision to deploy spyware to a specific state client through layers of ad networks, intermediaries, and commercial vendors is harder still. That's not an accident. The commercial spyware industry has always sold plausible deniability as part of the product. AdFection is a significant upgrade to that feature.

On the regulatory side: the EU's DSA and DMA create obligations for large ad platforms, but those frameworks were written to address anticompetitive behavior and harmful content. Nobody writing those rules was thinking about weaponized real-time bidding. Expect the Citizen Lab findings to land in Brussels with some force, and expect lobbying pressure from ad-tech to frame any reform as disproportionate. The industry will argue the problem is the spyware vendor, not the infrastructure. That argument is going to get a serious workout.

The real pressure point is real-time bidding architecture itself. RTB systems broadcast granular device and behavioral data to hundreds of potential buyers in milliseconds. That data exposure is already a well-documented privacy problem. AdFection adds a new dimension: the broadcast itself can be exploited not just to observe targets but to reach out and infect them. Any serious regulatory response has to grapple with that, which means grappling with the fundamental business model of digital advertising. That's a much bigger fight than banning one vendor.

For officials and security teams: the population of people who need to worry about this is not just dissidents and journalists abroad. Staffers at defense ministries, parliamentary aides, human rights lawyers, executives at companies with sensitive IP, opposition politicians in countries with active intelligence services targeting them. If you're on a target list maintained by a state that has budget for commercial spyware, your threat model changed this week.

Concrete steps are limited but not zero. Device isolation matters more now. High-risk individuals should be operating sensitive work on devices that are as close to ad-free as possible, using browsers with aggressive content blocking, and separating their high-risk work from their ordinary internet use. MDM solutions for organizational deployments need to start thinking about advertising traffic as a potential attack surface rather than irrelevant background noise. That's a significant mental shift for most enterprise security teams.

The Citizen Lab is going to keep pulling this thread. There will be more victims identified, probably more vendors implicated. The question is whether platforms move before regulators force them to. Google and the major ad networks have the technical ability to impose constraints on targeting granularity and audit advertiser identity at a level they currently don't. Whether the financial incentive exists to do so voluntarily is a different question.

AdFection is a name for something that was probably already happening without documentation. The publication confirms a capability. It doesn't establish a start date.

text:
Charting the Jewish Exodus Hoax: Did Georgia's Jewish Communities Thrive in a State Supposedly Overrun by Antisemitism?

Population Growth, Prosperity, Intermarriage, and the Leo Frank Case

The claim that Georgia was overwhelmed by widespread, systematic, or rampant antisemitism during the years surrounding Leo Frank's lynching deserves careful examination. It is a serious description of an entire state and its people, and it should be tested against the wider history of Jewish life in Georgia.

That history includes nearly three centuries of Jewish settlement, religious freedom, business development, civic leadership, population growth, and, in more recent decades, substantial intermarriage between Jews and non-Jews.

These facts raise questions about portrayals of Georgia as uniformly hostile to Jewish residents. They also challenge the frequently repeated claim that half the state's Jewish population fled following Frank's lynching on Tuesday, August 17, 1915.

Georgia's Jewish Communities Were Established Long Before Leo Frank

Jewish settlement in Georgia dates to 1733, when approximately forty Jewish immigrants arrived in Savannah. By 1826, an estimated 400 Jews lived in the state. During the nineteenth century, Jewish immigrants established congregations and businesses in cities and towns across Georgia.

Congregations were founded in Augusta in 1846, Columbus and Albany in 1854, Macon and West Point in 1859, and Atlanta in 1862. Others followed after the Civil War.

These communities developed alongside Georgia's changing economy. Jewish merchants opened shops, founded banks, established department stores, and participated in civic organizations. Some became prominent in education, charitable work, and local government.

Herman Myers became Savannah's first Jewish mayor in 1895. In Rome, Max Meyerhardt helped establish the public school system and Carnegie Library. Moses Michael founded the Athens Savings Bank in 1892 and served as president of the local Chamber of Commerce.

The Rich family built one of Atlanta's best-known department stores. Other Jewish-owned businesses developed in Albany, Macon, Rome, and communities throughout Georgia.

These were examples of Jewish Georgians finding economic opportunity and building enduring institutions. They are an important part of the state's history and deserve consideration when examining the social conditions Jewish residents experienced (Institute of Southern Jewish Life, 1).

A Population That Continued to Develop

The historical population estimates also deserve attention.

The American Jewish Year Book estimated approximately 7,000 Jewish residents in Georgia in 1899 and 9,300 in 1907. Estimates for the years after the Frank lynching included 22,414 in 1917, 23,240 in 1920, and 23,179 in 1927.

These estimates were assembled using different methods and cannot establish an exact migration history. Nevertheless, they describe a substantial Jewish community that continued to exist and develop in Georgia.

They do not reveal an identifiable statewide population collapse of 50 percent following the lynching.

If half of an estimated 9,300 residents had departed, approximately 4,650 people would have left. Such an extraordinary claim requires a documented migration history, including dates, destinations, and reasons for moving.

Population growth could conceal departures if new residents arrived in sufficient numbers. But the possibility of replacement migration cannot establish that thousands fled.

The burden of historical proof remains with those who repeat the numerical claim.

Why Jewish Families Chose Georgia

People generally consider employment, family connections, safety, religious life, and opportunities for their children when choosing where to settle.

Jewish families were no different. Georgia offered commercial opportunities, established Jewish congregations, and expanding communities in which families could pursue their ambitions.

A state perceived as uniformly dangerous or deeply unwelcoming would present obvious obstacles to attracting and retaining residents. The continued development of Jewish communities therefore raises a legitimate question about how Jewish families regarded Georgia and what opportunities they found there.

However, people sometimes move to places where prejudice exists because the available economic opportunities, family connections, or relative safety still make those places attractive.

This is why migration patterns are useful evidence about opportunity and community development, although they cannot independently measure the prevalence of prejudice.

Intermarriage Offers Another Way to Examine Jewish-Gentile Relations

Marriage can reveal something about social relationships that population counts alone cannot show.

When Jewish and gentile residents marry, their families often become connected through children, grandparents, relatives, friendships, religious traditions, and ordinary family life. Such relationships may indicate meaningful social contact and acceptance across religious boundaries.

Atlanta provides a striking example.

The Greater Atlanta Jewish Community Centennial Study: 2006 found that 50 percent of currently married couples in Jewish respondent households were intermarried under the study's definition. In 1996, the comparable figure had been 37 percent.

The 2006 study also found substantial geographic differences. The intermarriage rate was 10 percent among Jewish household couples in Sandy Springs and Dunwoody, 41 percent in Intown Atlanta, 44 percent in North Metro Atlanta, 55 percent in East Cobb, and 80 percent in Gwinnett and the East Perimeter.

These findings describe a community in which marriages between Jewish and non-Jewish partners had become common, although their frequency differed greatly by neighborhood (Greater Atlanta Jewish Community Centennial Study, 2).

The numbers make it difficult to portray modern Jewish and gentile life in metropolitan Atlanta as universally separated by religious hostility.

They also suggest that many Jewish and gentile families formed close relationships extending well beyond business or professional dealings.

Intermarriage does not, however, establish that prejudice is absent. Individual families may be accepting even when other members of society hold discriminatory attitudes. Rates of marriage are also influenced by religious observance, age, geography, education, and personal preference.

Most importantly, a marriage survey conducted in 2006 cannot establish the social conditions of 1915. Historical marriage registers, family records, and contemporary accounts would be needed to study intermarriage during the Frank era.

A Jewish Community That Attracted New Residents

The same 2006 community study found substantial migration into metropolitan Atlanta.

Approximately 81 percent of Jewish respondents had been born outside Georgia, while 31 percent of Atlanta's Jewish households had moved to the community during the preceding ten years.

The study estimated approximately 119,800 Jewish residents in Greater Atlanta, compared with an estimated 76,800 to 78,600 in 1996, depending on the study summary used (Berman Jewish DataBank, 3).

This was a rapidly growing community that attracted Jewish residents from other parts of the country.

Again, the findings concern modern Atlanta rather than Georgia in 1915. They do, however, provide a useful counterpoint to descriptions of Georgia as a place where Jewish residents could not establish successful, stable lives.

Was Georgia Philosemitic?

Philosemitism means favorable attitudes toward Jewish people, their religion, culture, or communities.

It is reasonable to investigate whether aspects of Georgia's history demonstrate positive relationships between Jewish and gentile residents, including business cooperation, friendships, intermarriage, religious freedom, civic leadership, and public support for Jewish institutions.

The historical record provides numerous examples of Jewish participation in Georgia's economic and public life.

Those achievements complicate any portrayal of the state as uniformly hostile to Jews. Yet they cannot establish that Georgia as a whole was philosemitic during every historical period. A state can offer significant opportunities to Jewish residents while also containing antisemitic organizations, discriminatory practices, or individuals willing to commit violence.

The Frank lynching must be examined within that fuller history. So must the bombing of Atlanta's Hebrew Benevolent Congregation in 1958 and the public support the congregation received afterward.

Both hostility and solidarity are part of Georgia's historical record.

A convincing study should investigate how widespread each was, how conditions changed over time, and whether particular claims about statewide attitudes are supported by contemporary evidence.

What Does This Mean for the Claim That Half of Georgia's Jews Fled?

The claim that half of Georgia's Jewish population fled after the 1915 lynching remains a separate historical question.

The available population estimates do not establish such a departure. The frequently repeated statewide figure of 3,000 Jews is also difficult to reconcile with estimates of approximately 7,000 around 1900 and 9,300 in 1907.

No contemporary statewide migration count identifying half the Jewish population as having departed because of the lynching has been established in this investigation.

That finding should not be converted into the claim that nobody left Georgia or that Jewish residents had no reason to fear hostility. Individual departures may have occurred, and their circumstances deserve further investigation.

The evidence does justify challenging an extraordinary numerical story that has been repeated without an identifiable contemporary count.

A More Complete History of Jewish Life in Georgia

Georgia's Jewish history includes generations of families who established businesses, supported charitable organizations, built congregations, entered public office, and contributed to their towns and cities.

Its modern history also includes substantial Jewish population growth and high rates of intermarriage in parts of metropolitan Atlanta.

These findings demonstrate that Jewish-Gentile relationships cannot be described solely through incidents of hostility. They also raise worthwhile questions about friendship, cooperation, integration, opportunity, and acceptance.

The stronger historical argument is that descriptions of widespread or systematic antisemitism must be tested against the complete record of Jewish life in Georgia.

Evidence of antisemitism should be examined seriously. Evidence of acceptance, opportunity, prosperity, and lasting community relationships deserves the same attention.

A history that recognizes only one side will give readers an incomplete understanding of the people who actually lived there.

Pakistan ruled out unconditional talks with Afghanistan and demanded a verifiable mechanism to stop attacks from Afghan soil.

text:
.@Seanfrank’s $200M+/yr DTC giant is running 8M+ view YouTube ads...

Forget AI songs and skits. Ridge has one tech mogul with 28M+ subs holding their product and talking.

So I figured I'd dig deeper and break down the entire genius strategy behind these winning influencer ad angles:

(And show how you can run this without dropping $10k on paid promos)

The guy is Marques Brownlee. 

The most trusted unboxing tech reviewer on YouTube.

In 2024 he joined Ridge as Chief Creative Partner and took a seat on their board.

And every ad says exactly that the second he appears on screen.

This sets the tone incredibly well before he says a single word.

It completely kills the entire “this is just some guy they paid off to read off a script” objection from skeptical people who know him, or even his die-hard fans.

It makes everything so much more authentic, which is exactly what makes these endorsements work.

Because Marques’s reputation is on the line here.

Even the studio, lighting and calm walkthrough are familiar from his videos too.

The trust is established from the get go.

And it instantly transfers to the brand and product. 

With that said, let’s get into the ads:

Ad 1 and 2: the power bank

Marques sits in his studio and walks through the product like any other review on his channel.

- 10,000 mAh capacity
- USB-C cable built into the body
- Apple Watch charging
- Kickstand
- LED charge indicator

Each feature gets a close-up and a single sentence from him before the next one lands.

The second version opens with him talking about taking "an idea" all the way to a finished product.

(Which tells the viewer he helped BUILD the thing.)

Both end on one card: 

Up to 32% off

ridge(.com).

And this is the part most brands would get wrong:

"Sell benefits, not features" isn't a universal rule. Nothing in Marketing is a universal rule.

Marques's audience already understands tech specs. They WANT to know how the cable works, what charges, how much capacity they get and what the engineering solves.

It's product evidence in a format the buyer understands, not specs dumped on screen.

A generic "charge anywhere" pitch would throw away the very detail this audience uses to judge whether the product deserves a premium.

Match the sophistication of the pitch to the sophistication of the buyer.

Ad 3: "Is it worth the price?"

Opens on "This wallet is probably the best gift you'll ever buy."

Then he takes a power drill to a regular leather wallet. "Yeah. Not great."

Then the same test on the Ridge.

That contrast does more than "durable" ever could. He gives the viewer a familiar baseline, shows the difference, then explains why the engineering matters.

Every line after that kills one objection: 

- The wallet that gets thicker the more you carry
- Elastic that keeps its tension
- RFID blocking
- A tracker card you can ping
- A warranty built for years of use

And the line doing the heavy lifting:

"You're not paying for something smaller. You're paying for something better engineered."

That's the premium-price argument. Not "our wallet costs more because we're a premium brand." 

But “here's what your money actually buys.”

The compactness, elastic, RFID, tracker and warranty each answer a different reason NOT to buy. The closing "is it worth it?" lands after those objections have been worked through.

Then the end card: 

DITCH THE BULK. 

One clear takeaway instead of five competing promises.

Ends on the exact question in the viewer's head: 

"So is it worth it? If you care about the thing you're carrying every single day, then the answer is yes."

Thus attaching the customer identity to buying the product, because no one goes “Yep idgaf about things I carry on the day to day”

Everything they do is engineered for a specific purpose as well:

1. The face IS the hook. Millions of tech buyers have trusted his opinion for over a decade. Ridge doesn't need a clever first line, they bought it years in advance.

2. The format is his format. Same lighting, same calm pacing as a normal MKBHD review, so the viewer's brain files it as "Marques reviewing something", and his credibility flows straight into the product.

3. The USP matches the audience. Tech buyers ignore "slim wallet" claims, so Ridge shows engineering instead: a drill test, RFID, a tracker card.

4. The price objection is confronted on camera. "Is it worth it?" is the question killing every premium sale, so they made it the title.

5. Zero fake urgency. A discount card and a domain. A tech-savvy audience smells pressure tactics instantly.

6. The creator has skin in the game. Equity and a board seat mean he talks about it like HIS product, because it is.

The lesson for smaller brands:

You don't need a Marques Brownlee.

You need whoever your ICP already trusts.

For a $90 supplement, a strength coach with 40k subscribers. 

For a $400 grinder, the barista with a cult following.

Whoever you choose, make sure they follow these 4 rules:

- Recognisable to your ICP, so the face stops the scroll
- Credible in your category, so the opinion carries weight
- Allowed to talk like himself, because a forced script burns his reputation AND your brand
- Record with a similar format as the person’s videos so there’s no audience mismatch

But you don't have to open with a $10k check for one sponsored post.

There are other ways to make the deal worth their time:

1. Equity. For a genuine long-term partner who fits the product, give them a stake in the business. Now they're helping build something they own, not just renting you their face. Just like Marques probably got

2. A share of the sales. Offer an agreed commission or revenue share on attributable sales. Or a smaller upfront fee plus upside. Give them a reason to care about the offer, the demo and whether people actually buy.

3. A CPM deal. Negotiate payment per 1,000 agreed, verifiable views, with a cap and clear measurement rules. You're paying for delivered exposure rather than guessing what one post is worth. Views still aren't sales.

Those are deal structures to negotiate, not promises that every creator will accept them. 

Also agree on deliverables, paid-ad usage rights and disclosure before running the creative.

The other route doesn't require buying the creator's endorsement at all: 

Attach your positioning to an ingredient, mechanism or practice your ICP already heard about from someone they trust.

Some examples are an athlete who swears by a particular way of training, or a beauty expert who keeps talking about an overlooked compound.

The opportunity isn't just "put that celebrity in our ad." It can also be "their audience already understands WHY this ingredient or method matters. Can our product genuinely deliver it?"

For a supplement, that could mean explaining your formulation around the ingredient the audience already researches because Bryan Johnson popularized it. 

For a training product, it can be demonstrating how your product supports the method they already want to follow because Jeff Nippard can’t stop talking about it.

If your product genuinely fits, lead with that ingredient, mechanism or routine and show why YOUR version makes sense. 

You're entering a conversation their audience already believes in, rather than paying to teach the category from zero.

And one day you might actually get that influencer’s attention and be able to afford them.

The point:

Borrow the existing belief, or give the right creator a reason to become a real partner. 

A big flat sponsorship fee isn't the only way in.

And the craziest part is where this runs.

On Meta, a creator review blends into the feed.

On YouTube, it's the exact kind of content people opened the app to watch.

Borrowed authority is especially useful when you're selling a premium product to a skeptical, informed buyer and trust is the bottleneck.

But this creative needs a Google account built to catch the demand it creates.

So don’t forget the remaining pieces:

- Protect branded search
- Build non-branded Shopping and Search coverage
- Keep remarketing separated with brand exclusions
- Add YouTube/Demand Gen when the foundation is ready to absorb more demand

Someone can watch the review today and search your product days later. If a competitor owns that search, you paid for the introduction and they collect the buyer.

So don't judge the whole thing on the video's last-click ROAS alone. Look at new customer acquisition, branded search lift and blended MER alongside direct conversions.

The creator earns the trust. The demo earns the premium. The rest of your funnel has to finish the sale.

Absolute domination by Ridge.

(And shout out to @seanfrank and their team for building such a cool brand)

As an #AVCT shareholder since 2021, adding when I can (and never selling a single share), Thursday’s presentation gave me a huge amount of comfort and confidence.

Shifting from Gen 1 to Gen 2 had a huge amount of risk attached to it. I’ve never known such a potentially extremely high reward scenario as the one we currently find ourselves in.

As @coughlin582 reminded us this week, preCISION has an enormous market opportunity. Around 90% of all solid tumours express FAP. In 2026, that’s approximately a $224B market, sadly rising to a staggering $327B by 2031.

Step back and appreciate what a potentially better performing Enhertu means. For those not aware, this is the biggest selling ADC of all time. @avacta has chosen to go head to head with it right from the preclinical stage and is now showing a more favourable early clinical safety profile through DL3 compared with Enhertu data.

But 6103 is just the exatecan payload using the Gen 2 tech. The Gen 2 mechanism is working in patients. What will they (or much more likely a partner) be attaching next?

Then there’s their super next gen 6207 asset, going into IND enabling studies next year.

Ultimately, I believe it will get to a point where Avacta starts to receive offers that will get the nod. We’re not there yet. Otherwise, CC & RH would’ve said thank you very much. But as every day goes by, we’re getting much closer. Especially now that we have the rapid speed we’re seeing in the 6103 trial.

Importantly, it’s not just about getting closer to realising a multi billion dollar exit. At some point Avacta will agree to pass over a next gen cancer treatment platform that could go on to genuinely make a significant difference to patients lives globally. 

To be part of that journey is why many of us have remained invested. Yes, we all want the $XXB exit that should be in the crosshairs for tech like this, but to look back one day and know we backed something that went on to genuinely make a significant difference to patients lives? That would be quite something too.

text:
🇮🇳 Reliance and Rolls-Royce Announce Intent to Build India's AMCA Combat Engine, With a New Aerospace Gas Turbine Complex

📌 WHAT: A "strategic intent" to partner on the design, development, manufacturing and delivery of a sovereign combat engine for the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA). They will also explore a dedicated Aerospace Gas Turbine Complex in India

🏢 WHO: Reliance Industries Limited and Rolls-Royce
📅 WHEN: 14 Aug 2026 (London / Mumbai)

This is an announcement of intent. The release has no contract, government approval, IP terms or timeline.

🔧 WHAT IS THIS? (IN SIMPLE WORDS)

The AMCA is India's fifth-generation fighter, and it needs an engine. The engine is the hardest part of a fighter to build, and India still depends on foreign makers for it.

Here, a British engine maker and an Indian conglomerate say they plan to build the engine and a whole engine-making complex in India. It would cover design, testing, production and long-term support. The release calls the goal "sovereign, end-to-end Indian capability".

⚙️ TECH SPECS

• Thrust: not in the release. Coverage describes a 120 kN-class engine, with scope up to 145 kN (Tribune)
• Rollout target: 2034 (Tribune)
• Complex location, investment, workforce: not published

📜 WHAT IS REPORTED, NOT ANNOUNCED

• The Tribune reports, citing unnamed UK officials, a full transfer of technology and retained IP rights for India
• The release says nothing about IP or technology transfer
• In Aug 2025, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said India would retain IP for the AMCA engine (Airforce Technology)

🧠 OUR ANALYSIS

• The release speaks of intent and a complex India would "explore". It does not announce a contract or any IP terms.
• If India did end up owning an engine's design, it could pick fighters and engines separately, as it cannot today. That would take years and is not announced.
• For now, the real decision is between this offer and the Safran–GTRE (DRDO) engine. The government has not chosen.
• The Tribune reports that MoD has invited three bidder groups for the AMCA airframe, and none of them makes engines.

❓ WHAT WE DON'T KNOW
• Whether the government will pick this over the Safran–GTRE engine
• Written IP and technology-transfer terms
• Cost, location and timeline of the complex

📷 Credit: Reliance Industries / Rolls-Royce (media release)

A hacker accessed personal data on millions of current and former California public school students through the state’s testing contractor.

Educational Testing Service (ETS) discovered unauthorized access on 25 September. An investigation found a compromised login was used between 22 May and 18 September 2026 to copy files containing names, dates of birth, addresses, disability status and other demographic information for all students enrolled in the three previous school years more than 5.7 million currently enrolled, plus some former students. 

Social Security numbers and financial data were not taken.
Notifications to families began on Friday. Affected students are being offered two years of free identity-protection services. ETS has not found evidence the data has been made public.

🔴 Food Security Over Fuel Blending: Why India Just Set Sugar-to-Ethanol Diversion to Zero for 2026-27 👇🇮🇳

When domestic staple inflation collides with green energy mandates, food policy will always win.

Faced with tightening domestic supplies and record-high sugar prices, the government has directed oil marketing companies (OMCs) to exclude sugar-based feedstocks entirely from the 2026-27 procurement tender. 

The price surge is driven by weather shocks and lower crop yields.

This marks a major pivot in India's energy transition architecture:

> The latest OMC tender for 11 billion litres of ethanol has completely omitted offers for ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup, and B-heavy molasses.

> Domestic consumption requirements are running tight against weather-affected output. 

> Halting sugar diversion ensures domestic retail price stability over aggressive fuel blending targets.

The structural shift to grain-based and low-grade feedstocks has buffered the blow. 

These include:
• maize
• broken rice
• surplus FCI rice
• C-heavy molasses

This allows blending programs to advance without leaning entirely on the cane economy.

A stark reminder that energy security and agricultural supply chains must be calibrated hand-in-hand to prevent localized shortages.

Green energy targets are critical, but managing food plate stability remains the ultimate macro priority.

text:
● #SavingsDay

October 17 is Savings Day. In 1952 (Showa 27), the #CentralCouncilforSavingsPromotion established it at its own founding. That body is today's #CentralCouncilforFinancialServicesInformation. Around this day, events are held, including the recognition of outstanding children's banks (#YuryoKodomoGinko) and of those who have contributed to saving.

The date comes from the Kanname-sai mentioned above. It carries on the spirit of the ritual in which the Emperor offers the year's new rice to Ise Jingu, with the aim of valuing the fruits of labor and raising interest in saving. Gratitude for a harvest and the habit of putting money aside may seem an odd pairing, but they connect on one point: preparing the fruits for the future.

Saving generally means building up assets through cash, deposits, investments, pensions, insurance and so on. In English it is "savings," a word that also covers deposits and reserves. That is why a deposit account is called a "savings account."

The Central Council for Financial Services Information cooperates with prefectural councils, the government, the #BankofJapan, local governments and private organizations, and carries out wide-ranging public information activities on familiar financial topics from a neutral and fair standpoint. Although its name has changed since it started in 1952 as the Central Council for Savings Promotion, its role of laying the groundwork for thinking about how to live with money has continued.

The Council, nicknamed "#Shirupoluto," has its secretariat inside the Information Services Department of the Bank of Japan, in #NihombashiHongokucho, Chuo Ward, Tokyo. Its activities include supporting financial education, providing information suited to each stage of life, holding lectures and seminars, and conducting surveys. Why not open your household budget app today and look over this month's income and spending? Just looking at the numbers can give you a clue for planning ahead. The next observance has a deep connection with music.

text:
● #KannameSai

October 17 is Kanname-sai. Pronounced "kan-na-me-sai," it is one of the Imperial Court rites (#ImperialCourtRituals), a thanksgiving festival for a bountiful harvest of the five grains. The Emperor offers the year's first ears of rice to #Amaterasu, and the festival is also a seasonal word for autumn.

At #IseJingu (the Grand Shrine of Ise), too, ceremonies are held, and an imperial envoy is dispatched from the Imperial Family. Among the roughly 1,500 regular rites held at the shrine each year, this has long been regarded as the most important. It is said that the shrine's annual calendar of rites centers on Kanname-sai. Because the ceremonial garments and ritual implements are renewed at this time, it is also called the "#NewYearofJingu."

Its date has a history. It used to fall on September 17 of the lunar calendar. When the solar calendar was adopted in 1872 (Meiji 5), it was moved to September 17 of the new calendar. Yet rice ears had not matured enough by then. So from 1879 (Meiji 12), it has been held a month later, on October 17.

The "first ears" are the rice panicles that ripen for the first time that year. As a festival that heralds the harvest season, it has long marked a turning point of autumn in both the calendar and daily life. The shifts in its date were adjustments to align the festival with the agricultural reality of rice ripening.

From 1874 (Meiji 7) until 1947 (Showa 22), it was also a national holiday as a major festival day. Today, why not savor a bowl of this year's new rice, slowly? Gratitude for the harvest mingles with the steam and sweetness of freshly cooked rice. A quiet moment at the table to thank those who grew it also reflects the spirit of this festival. By the way, there is another observance on this same day that carries on the spirit of this festival.

text:
🏇 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗪𝗿𝗮𝗽 𝗚𝗼𝗹𝗱 𝗖𝗼𝗮𝘀𝘁 - 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗲𝘀 𝗚𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗨𝘀 𝗟𝗶𝗳𝗲!
Holy shit, what a day. We copped a few proper bumps early, then the right sort of horses did the job, especially when they could stay involved and grind through the Soft 7 with the wind in its mean mood. Big moments were 𝗗𝗿𝗮𝘄 𝗔𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 knifing through in Race 2, 𝗔𝘄𝗮𝘆𝗴𝗼𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗯𝘂𝗻𝗻𝘆 landing the finishing punch in Race 3, and 𝗧𝗿𝘂𝗲 𝗔𝗺𝗼𝗿 going full job in the last race. Pattern of the day, pace and position, the map mattered, and when you drifted back too far you paid tax.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗜𝘁 𝗨𝗻𝗳𝗼𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗱
We started with Turbo Cow looking like a “get your money early” story, and then it turned into the classic Soft 7 shuffle, position didn’t hold and he just never found the right lane. Race 2 was where the vibe flipped, Draw Attention had the perfect, patient stalk, and when it got busy late, he was the one who actually went bang. Race 3 also screamed “timing wins races”, Awaygoesthebunny sat in the right spot and mowed the lane like it owed him rent.

Mid to late, the track did what Gold Coast does, it kept asking questions. The wind and Soft footing made the straight a bit of a slow-motion fight, so horses that could keep momentum and keep their feet were the ones getting home. That mostly matched the original read, but where we got punished was when we pushed the wrong kind of belief, betting front-end talent that couldn’t quite keep the run going, and backing top picks when the actual finishing order shoved us out of the story.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗯𝗼𝗮𝗿𝗱
Selections: 3/9 hit for +$26.33

𝗪𝗶𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀 (𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁-𝗢𝘂𝘁)
- R2 Draw Attention — $15 win @ $3.00 → +$30.00
- R3 Awaygoesthebunny — $11.54 win @ $3.00 → +$23.08
- R8 True Amor — $15 each_way @ $5.50 → +$41.25

𝗥𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗯𝘆 𝗥𝗮𝗰𝗲 — 𝗛𝗼𝘄'𝗱 𝗪𝗲 𝗚𝗼?
- R1: 𝗧𝘂𝗿𝗯𝗼 𝗖𝗼𝘄 win — 7th, lead-style looked good pre-race but the Soft7 grind and timing into the lane never arrived for him.
- R2: 𝗗𝗿𝗮𝘄 𝗔𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 win — BANG! Won at $3.00, the stalk and hit-run pattern paid off.
- R3: 𝗔𝘄𝗮𝘆𝗴𝗼𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗯𝘂𝗻𝗻𝘆 win — BANG! Won at $3.00, timing was perfect and he got the finishing run.
- R4: 𝗠𝗮𝗱𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝘆 win — Missed, she ran the right sort of race flow on paper but never hit the line hard enough on the day’s execution.
- R5: 𝗗𝗶𝗿𝘁𝘆 𝗛𝗮𝗿𝗿𝘆 each_way — Missed, 1000m on Soft is chaos, and he didn’t get that clean, controlled run required to place.
- R6: 𝗥𝗵𝗲𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗰 win — 3rd, he was competitive but Paciera and Canadian Fling turned it into their tempo battle and took the prize.
- R7: 𝗕𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗡𝗼𝘁 𝗦𝗹𝗶𝗽 each_way — Missed, 1200m Soft with pressured races, he never got the lane at the right time.
- R8: 𝗧𝗿𝘂𝗲 𝗔𝗺𝗼𝗿 each_way — BANG! Won at $5.50, controlled the momentum early and kept working through the straight fight.

Selections: 3/9 hit for +$26.33

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗪𝗲 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗲𝗱 — 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗙𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱
Pace and position were king, full stop. On Soft 7 with that gusty wind, you could see how quickly the “easy” run turns into a survival run, so horses that could hold a rhythm and stay within reach were the ones doing damage late. Draw Attention and Awaygoesthebunny were straight examples of “sit handy, pounce at the right time”, they didn’t need miracles, they needed timing.

Where we got stitched was betting confidence in the wrong kind of trip. Turbo Cow went looking for a role he couldn’t maintain, and Dirty Harry got caught in that 1000m Soft lottery where even the good ones need an actual clear path. Rhetoric ran a solid race but when the race breaks into tempo battles, the second wave can steal the finish, Paciera and Canadian Fling did exactly that.

The market wasn’t always your mate. Sometimes it backed the right horse and sometimes it just backed the idea. We respected the leaders when the map said “go”, and when the map was right we got paid. When the map was off in execution, you could feel the day punish you fast.

Next time Gold Coast is Soft 7 and the wind is chewing up the straight, I’m backing the ones that look like they can stay balanced through the middle, not the ones that only look flash in the first 400m. Get the lane plan right, and don’t be stubborn when the track is already telling you it’s going to be a grind.

𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗱 — 𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗮𝗽 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗱 𝗢𝘂𝘁
The speed picture generally held. Races 2 and 3 were won by horses who stayed connected to the main group and then used the Soft ground to keep moving, that’s the cheat code when the straight turns into a gusty mess. Where the wheels fell off was when our top pick needed a smoother run than the race actually offered, and Soft 7 will happily take the smooth away.

Late in the day the finish tightened and the “keep finding” brigade separated. The straight wind made it harder for deep closers to make up ground cleanly, so the better riders were the ones who protected position and only asked the horse late, not early, not in panic. That confirmed the original read, pace and momentum were paying rent, and the ones stuck wide or too far back were paying penalty.

𝗤𝘂𝗶𝗰𝗸 𝗛𝗶𝘁𝘀 (𝗥𝗮𝗰𝗲-𝗯𝘆-𝗥𝗮𝗰𝗲)
- R1: 𝗪𝗮𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗶 ($20.40) — our top pick Turbo Cow ran 7th
- R2: 𝗗𝗿𝗮𝘄 𝗔𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 ($30.00) — BANG Win +$30.00
- R3: 𝗔𝘄𝗮𝘆𝗴𝗼𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗯𝘂𝗻𝗻𝘆 ($2.80) — our top pick ran 1st, BANG +$23.08
- R4: 𝗖𝗼𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗖𝗼𝘄𝗯𝗼𝘆 ($8.80) — our top pick Madame Cody ran outside the finish
- R5: 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗮𝗱𝗮𝗱 ($12.90) — our top pick Dirty Harry ran outside the placing
- R6: 𝗖𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗱𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗙𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 ($8.40) — our top pick Rhetoric ran 3rd
- R7: 𝗖𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗕𝗲𝗮𝘂𝘁𝘆 ($3.10) — our top pick Better Not Slip ran outside the first few
- R8: 𝗧𝗿𝘂𝗲 𝗔𝗺𝗼𝗿 ($3.90) — our top pick ran 1st, BANG each way +$41.25

𝗖𝗹𝗼𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴
Overall, this was a proper winning-tips day, the map held up and the right tempo horses got the chocolates. We’ll cop the misses like grown men, but the big takeaway is simple, on Soft 7 at Gold Coast you back rhythm, you don’t back vibes. Next week, I’ll be hunting the same recipe, pace that stays alive, lane protection, and horses that don’t implode when the wind gets cheeky.

text:
Ethiopia’s pursuit of sea access is not an attempt to challenge Eritrea’s sovereignty or lay claim to its territory. It is a matter of Ethiopia’s legitimate national interest and strategic necessity, one that can be addressed through peaceful negotiations and mutually beneficial arrangements.
When Ethiopia reached an agreement with Somaliland to secure access to the sea, Eritrea opposed it. Its position on Red Sea affairs, including its insistence that governance of the Red Sea should be restricted to coastal states, raises a fundamental question: On what principle does Eritrea oppose Ethiopia’s legitimate aspiration to secure sea access?
If Eritrea’s position offers no viable alternative for Ethiopia and instead focuses on preventing Ethiopia from securing access to the sea through peaceful means, such a stance contradicts the principles of good neighbourliness, regional cooperation, and shared development.
Ethiopia’s pursuit of sea access should not be treated as a justification for territorial conflict with Eritrea. However, just as Eritrea expects its own sovereignty to be respected, it must also refrain from policies that undermine Ethiopia’s legitimate national interests. The future stability of the region will not be secured by one country denying another its legitimate interests, but by pursuing solutions through dialogue, mutual understanding, and mutually beneficial cooperation.

text:
WHAT DOES INDIA UNDERSTAND ABOUT CIVILIZATION, FAMILY, AND HUMAN RESPONSIBILITY THAT AMERICA MAY HAVE FORGOTTEN?

America and India are two great democracies, separated by oceans, history, and culture. Yet I believe India has preserved certain values that America would be wise to rediscover.

Civilization is not measured simply by wealth, technology, military strength, or economic growth. It is measured by the character of its people and the values passed from one generation to the next.

India offers some powerful lessons.

FAMILY IS A LIFELONG RESPONSIBILITY.

In many Indian families, parents sacrifice for their children, and grown children accept responsibility for aging parents. Grandparents remain an important part of family life. Three generations may live together, sharing wisdom, responsibility, and love.

America once embraced this tradition more widely. Today, independence too often becomes isolation.

EDUCATION IS A FAMILY INVESTMENT.

Many Indian parents regard education not merely as preparation for employment but as a responsibility to future generations. Academic achievement, discipline, and sacrifice are deeply valued.

America needs to rediscover that seriousness of purpose.

RESPECT FOR ELDERS IS RESPECT FOR CIVILIZATION.

A society that dismisses its elderly risks discarding the very people who built it. Experience, memory, and wisdom cannot be manufactured by artificial intelligence.

India’s traditions often recognize something important: Growing older should bring dignity, not invisibility.

FREEDOM MUST BE ACCOMPANIED BY RESPONSIBILITY.

Individual rights are essential, but no civilization survives on individualism alone. Families, neighborhoods, communities, and nations require obligations that extend beyond ourselves.

America excels at celebrating individual achievement. India reminds us of the enduring importance of family and community.

Of course, India has serious challenges, and millions of American families continue to practice these same values. Neither nation has a monopoly on wisdom.

But perhaps the greatest opportunity lies in what these two nations can learn from one another.

America offers a powerful tradition of individual liberty, innovation, and opportunity. India offers enduring traditions of family commitment, cultural continuity, and intergenerational responsibility.

Together, these strengths could help shape a better future.

At 75, I increasingly measure civilization by a simple question:

What kind of people are we preparing our grandchildren to become?

Because ultimately, our greatest legacy will not be what we owned, what we built, or how much wealth we accumulated.

It will be the values that survive us.

And that is a conversation worth having between America and India.

text:
💰 MY 2 CENTS — SCHWAB OPENS THE DOOR TO 40 MILLION ACCOUNTS, WHILE CRYPTO ETFs BLEED
October 16, 2026 | Distribution, flows and what it means for Bitcoin
 
Wall Street is building the biggest on-ramp to crypto in history, and in the same weeks institutional money is walking out of crypto ETFs. Both stories are true. Here is how they fit together, with the hype separated from the facts.
 
1️⃣ THE HEADLINE VS THE FACTS
"JUST IN: $13 trillion Charles Schwab fully launches Bitcoin & Ethereum trading to its 40 million eligible retail clients." The headline is broadly right, but it needs context. [Facts] Schwab announced spot BTC and ETH trading in April and began a phased rollout on May 13. With its third-quarter results on October 15, the company said Schwab Crypto is now available to all eligible clients and that crypto transfers in and out are being switched on gradually. Schwab manages about $13.3 trillion in client assets across roughly 40.3 million active brokerage accounts. [Context] Not all of those 40 million accounts can trade: residents of New York, Louisiana and U.S. territories are excluded, and so are international clients. The news is the completion of a rollout, not a surprise launch. It still matters.
 
2️⃣ WHAT SCHWAB ACTUALLY OFFERS
Clients open a Schwab Crypto account linked to their brokerage account and trade spot Bitcoin and Ether on https://t.co/CFe5jkDy8x, the mobile app and thinkorswim. The fee is 0.75% of the value of each trade, with a $1 minimum and a $2 million maximum per transaction. The custodian is Schwab's own bank, Charles Schwab Premier Bank, with Paxos providing sub-custody and execution. Transfers currently work only on the Bitcoin and Ethereum networks, and withdrawal addresses must be registered in advance. According to reports, Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink are planned before the end of 2026; Schwab itself has confirmed "three more coins" by year-end.
 
3️⃣ WHY IT MATTERS — SCALE AND TRUST
Schwab is not a crypto company trying to look like a bank. It is one of the largest brokers in the world, and it just reported a record quarter: revenue up 17% to $7.2 billion and $190 billion of core net new assets, up 38% on the year. According to its own estimates, Schwab clients already hold about 20% of all spot crypto ETPs. Until now they could buy exposure through a fund; now they can hold the asset directly, next to their stocks and bonds, inside an app they already trust. For a large part of the U.S. middle class, the step from "I have a Schwab account" to "I own Bitcoin" has become one click.
 
4️⃣ THE DISTRIBUTION WAR — BROKERS AND EXCHANGES ARE CONVERGING
Schwab is part of a broader shift. Morgan Stanley launched its own spot Bitcoin ETF in April. Goldman Sachs has filed for a Bitcoin-linked income ETF. Coinbase now offers stocks and ETFs, and Kraken has launched tokenised equity futures. Traditional brokers are adding crypto, crypto exchanges are adding stocks, and the client ends up in a single account for everything. [Inference] The competitive pressure falls on pure crypto platforms and on fees. At 0.75% per trade Schwab is not the cheapest option, but for its clients convenience and trust count more than a few basis points.
 
5️⃣ BITCOIN ETFs — A PAUSE, NOT A CAPITULATION
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs manage about $106 billion, with cumulative net inflows of about $56.9 billion since January 2024. October is negative so far by about $535–540 million, after inflows of $2.6 billion in September and $3.5 billion in August. Last week's outflows were close to $680 million. This week has been mixed: $175 million in on Monday, about $261 million out on Wednesday after the hot CPI, and a small inflow of about $5 million on Thursday. [Inference] That is a reduction of exposure, not panic. June's $4.5 billion of outflows, the worst month on record, was a real capitulation; October so far is not.
 
6️⃣ ETHER ETFs — THE WEAKEST LINK
Ether funds are under heavier pressure. Between October 5 and 9 they recorded about $542 million of net outflows, part of a run of nine consecutive sessions without inflows. Total assets fell from $17.7 billion to $15.7 billion, but only about 27% of that drop came from redemptions; the rest was the fall in the ETH price. Ether trades around $2,435, roughly 50% below its all-time high. [Inference] When institutions reduce risk, they cut the asset with the weakest relative momentum first, and today that is ETH.
 
7️⃣ ALTCOIN ETFs — SOLANA SLOWS, XRP KEEPS BUYING
Solana ETFs recorded about $24.8 million of outflows in the week to October 9, their largest weekly exit since launch, ending a 14-week run of inflows. Their assets fell to $1.73 billion. XRP ETFs are the exception: 13 consecutive weeks of inflows, a record $1.80 billion of cumulative net inflows and $1.57 billion in assets, now only about $160 million behind Solana. At the global level, CoinShares' latest weekly report shows about $434 million of outflows from digital-asset investment products. [Inference] Money is not leaving the sector all at once; it is rotating and becoming more selective.
 
8️⃣ THE PARADOX — THE DOORS OPEN WHILE THE MONEY WAITS
Why are flows weak just as access improves? Because access is structural and flows are cyclical. This week U.S. CPI rose to 3.7% and producer prices jumped 6.3%, the fastest since 2022. The odds of a Fed hike on October 28 touched about 50% before falling back to around 25–30%. AI credit stress is pushing investors toward Treasuries. In that environment, institutions reduce risk regardless of how easy it is to buy Bitcoin. [Inference] Schwab's launch does not change the next two weeks. It changes the size of the market that can respond when macro conditions improve.
 
9️⃣ THE COST MATH — DIRECT BITCOIN OR AN ETF?
A practical point for investors. At 0.75% per trade, buying and later selling costs about 1.5% in total. A spot Bitcoin ETF such as IBIT charges about 0.25% a year. For an active trader, the ETF inside a brokerage account remains cheaper. For a long-term holder who buys rarely, direct ownership has one decisive advantage: once transfers are enabled, the coins can be moved to self-custody, which an ETF never allows. [Assumption] Part of Schwab's direct crypto demand may come from investors who already hold crypto ETFs, so not every dollar will be new money.
 
🔟 MY 2 CENTS — STRUCTURALLY BULLISH, CYCLICALLY PATIENT
Main scenario: no immediate impact on price. The Schwab launch is a long-term structural positive, but in the short term flows will follow the Fed and the bond market. I expect mixed ETF flows and Bitcoin in a $78–84K range until the FOMC on October 28.
 
Bullish scenario: ETF flows turn consistently positive, the Fed avoids a hike and Bitcoin confirms Thursday's sweep below $80K with a daily close above $82.8K, then a reclaim of $83.7K. In that case new distribution channels like Schwab could amplify the recovery.
 
Bearish scenario: another hot data point or a Fed hike, ETF outflows extending into November and a daily close below $80.1K, opening the way to $78K and then $76–77K.
 
What I am monitoring: daily Bitcoin and Ether ETF flows, Schwab's first figures on crypto accounts and assets, the activation of transfers, the XRP vs Solana ETF race, the U.S. 10-year yield and Fed hike odds, and Bitcoin's daily close relative to $82.8K.
 
What would invalidate my view: several consecutive days of large ETF inflows before the Fed meeting, which would show that institutions are buying the dip regardless of macro.
 
The lesson: adoption is not a price signal for tomorrow; it is a bigger engine waiting for the right fuel. For long-term holders, BTC, ETH and SOL should continue to be assessed through disciplined DCA, separately from speculative trading.
 
Is the Schwab launch a real game changer for Bitcoin, or just another headline? 👇

A pedophilic bully who cares for no one but himself. And the chaos he has unleashed on the world is hard to ignore. 

But this isnt the first time the Americans have been at it. But the hypocrisy and the constant 'we are the good guys' packaging while they do exactly what they accuse others of doing is what gets under the skin.

For instance, they removed Mossadegh in Iran in 1953 because he nationalised oil which hurts American interests. Put the Shah back - in a way fuelled the current Iranian crisis. Same thing in Guatemala in 1954 because United Fruit didn’t like land reforms. Chile in 1973 because Allende touched American copper companies. Nixon literally told the CIA to make the economy scream. Coups/regime changes, economic sabotage, arming the other side - classic American manoeuvres. Enough reasons for half the world to never trust the Yankees.

Now look at what’s happening with us. Tariffs because we buy Russian oil while they did a U-turn and started buying it themselves. Demands to open our agriculture and dairy markets so their corn, soy and milk can flood in and wipe out our farmers - something which was supposed to be a non-negotiable for us. Musk throwing a public tantrum on X, calling Indian businesses a “monopolistic chokehold,” asking if Ambani is the real boss of India, because Starlink and Tesla aren’t getting the red carpet he expected. Massacring H1Bs in US, while flaunting $330 billion Indian investments back home. Rubio lands in Mumbai, and "summoning" Jaishankar there instead of Delhi, leaving the hapless MEA to issue clarifications. Landau stands on our soil during Raisina Dialogue and says, very calmly, that they will not make the same 'mistake' with India that they made with China. Translation: we will not let you grow big enough to compete with us.

And what has been the language from our side? Polite notes. "We have conveyed our concerns." "We seek a mutually beneficial relationship." Meanwhile Carney in Canada tells them straight: you asked too much, offered too little, this is an attack on our economy, we’re retaliating dollar for dollar. Sánchez in Spain says "no to war," refuses the bases, and dares them to cut trade. Italy snapped back fiercely. Then there is China that matched tariffs and hit back on rare earths. We, the world’s largest democracy with a growing economy, sound like we’re hoping they don’t notice if we speak softly.

Then he gets out or is allowed to leave. Brahma Chellaney and others call it surrender under pressure. Maybe it is, maybe it isn’t. But the pattern of "we need the relationship" always overriding hard security questions is real. Same with Indians getting targeted online and offline in the US. Attack on Hindu temple, rampant racism. Rubio’s response? Every country has stupid people. We’ll take it seriously. That’s it.

When you become a pushover, people stop fearing you. When you surrender to a bully once, you are immediately branded as a weak and capitulating.

YOUR BODY IS YOUR TEMPLE

The flesh you inhabit is not a prison, nor a mere vessel of clay. It is the living sanctum where spirit and matter meet in holy tension.

Within the architecture of bone and blood, breath moves like incense. The heart beats as an eternal altar fire. Every cell holds the memory of stars that once burned and fell into form. What the world calls “body” is the outer court of a temple whose inner chambers open only in silence, in devotion, in the deliberate turning of attention inward.

Treat it as sacred ground. The way you move, the food you offer it, the thoughts you allow to echo through its halls—these are the rites you perform. Neglect is desecration. Excess is idolatry of the transient. Presence is worship.

You do not own this temple. You are its temporary priest. While the breath remains, the doors stand open between the seen and the unseen. Guard the threshold. Keep the lamps lit. For when the priest departs, the temple does not vanish—it simply returns its light to the greater mystery from which it was shaped.

🇮🇷🇮🇶🇵🇸| Between the 55 flags in Baghdad and the ruins of Gaza lies the entirety of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation

October 17, 2026 | Baghdad

Araghchi’s convoy arrived in Baghdad this morning. A spokesperson for the Iraqi Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed that delegations from all 55 member states and observer entities have arrived. The theme of the conference is printed on every document: "Dialogue and Solidarity: Two Pillars for Promoting Peace and Sustainable Development."

"Gaza" is not in the theme.

But it is on the agenda. The question of Palestine is the central issue at the 52nd session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers. Draft resolutions address Jerusalem, the expansion of settlements, forced displacement, the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, and the financial pressures facing UNRWA. Iraq has assumed the rotating presidency from Turkey for a one-year term. The conference is expected to adopt the "Baghdad Declaration."

Yet, the "Gaza" on the agenda is a world apart from the Gaza on the ground.

💥 When was the last time this organization fired a single bullet for the sake of Gaza?

The Organization of Islamic Cooperation consists of 57 member states. It claims to be the collective voice of the Islamic world. How many resolutions has it passed since the genocide in Gaza entered its third year? Many. How many statements has it issued? Even more. Has it deployed a single soldier? No. Has it cut off oil supplies from any member state with ties to Israel? No. Has it sanctioned any member state that granted transit permits for weapons bound for Israel? No.

In February 2026, the Grand Mufti of Oman, Ahmed Al-Khalili, publicly criticized the organization, describing its stance in the face of Israeli atrocities as "inaction," pointing to its continued silence even as the suffering in Gaza persisted long after a ceasefire agreement had been signed. A religious authority from a Gulf state used the term "inaction" to characterize an organization comprising 57 member nations.

"Inaction" is diplomatic language.  To put it more accurately: this organization has become paralyzed when it comes to the issue of Gaza.

🎯 What Araghchi Brought into the Meeting Room

Araghchi did not go there merely to listen to statements.

Before his departure, the Iranian Foreign Ministry confirmed that he would articulate Iran’s position at the meeting and hold bilateral talks with several participating foreign ministers. Iran’s stance has remained unchanged for the past two years: what is happening in Gaza is genocide. Resistance is a legitimate right. Any "peace framework" that equates resistance with occupation serves only to inflict a second trauma upon the victims.

Yet, most of the nations represented in the Baghdad meeting hall would not accept this position.

Sitting at the same table is a representative from Saudi Arabia, a country whose F-15 fighter jets are equipped with Israeli-made combat helmets. Also present is a representative from the United Arab Emirates, a nation whose ports have handled cargo bound for Israel, and whose territory hosts U.S. military assets positioned against Iran. There is a representative from Egypt, too, a country whose Suez Canal serves as a link in the supply chain for munitions transported from the Arabian Gulf to the port of Ashdod.

Araghchi is set to speak about Gaza in front of these very people, some of whom serve as logistical nodes for the massacre in Gaza.

This is not "dialogue." It is a confrontation.

📜 What "Dialogue and Unity" Means in Baghdad

Ahead of the meeting, the Secretary-General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) stated that the current sensitive phase and the escalation of regional tensions "require us to redouble our collective responsibility, strengthen stability, and consolidate Islamic unity."

"Consolidating Islamic unity" in the context of Baghdad, this phrase carries a very specific meaning.

Iraq is currently maintaining relations with both Tehran and Washington. It shares a long border with Iran maintaining "close political, economic, and religious ties" while simultaneously upholding a "strategic partnership" with the United States. Iraq’s assumption of the OIC chairmanship is a diplomatic maneuver, an attempt to position itself as a "bridge between the Arab world and the broader regional landscape."  At one end of this bridge lies Iran a nation under sanctions and bombardment while at the other end stands Washington, the architect of those sanctions and the source of the bombs.

Araghchi has stepped onto this bridge, not to dance, but to ensure that Iran’s voice is not crushed by the very structure that supports the span.

⚔️ Bilateral Talks: The Real Agenda

Plenary sessions are staged for the cameras; the true agenda unfolds in the corridors and side rooms where Araghchi holds his meetings.

Iran and Pakistan are expected to engage in a new round of regional peace consultations in Baghdad. Pakistan’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister find themselves caught between obligations stemming from defense agreements with Riyadh (Mecca-linked pacts) and the stark realities along their border with Iran. Turkish Foreign Minister Fidan is also in Baghdad, as Ankara navigates a complex balancing act, managing its relations with Riyadh, Tehran, and Washington simultaneously.

These bilateral discussions may not yield a formal "Baghdad Declaration," but they will shape the actual security landscape along Iran’s eastern and northern borders in the months to come.

The plenary session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) brings 57 nations together to reiterate their "concern" regarding Gaza. In contrast, Araghchi’s bilateral talks represent Iran’s search for genuine security arrangements seeking protection outside an organization that has proven incapable of shielding anyone.

🔻 Gaza Is Not in the Conference Room

The children of Gaza are not in Baghdad. The mothers of Gaza are not in Baghdad. The ruins of Gaza are not in Baghdad.

What Baghdad offers instead are draft resolutions, slogans, ceremonial handovers, and photo opportunities.

Araghchi will articulate Iran’s position, which will be duly recorded in the meeting minutes. Those minutes will be archived and subsequently forgotten. The next summit will take place in another capital, under a different theme, with yet another declaration reiterating the very same "concern."

Meanwhile, in Gaza, the bombs continue to fall delivered along routes that pass through the very nations currently signing in at the Baghdad summit.

Long live Palestine. Long live the Resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.
