text:
Grace, Survival, and Resilience: Giving Thanks for the Life of Chief Kola Karim, the Agbaoye of Ibadanland

​By Dare Adelekan 

​In the journey of life, wealth, status, and titles can shield a person from many of society's storms, but they offer no immunity against the unpredictable forces of nature and mechanics. Recently, the Nigerian business community and the traditional landscape of Yorubaland were thrown into a moment of profound anxiety, quickly replaced by immense thanksgiving, following a terrifying mid-air incident involving a private aircraft linked to the renowned industrialist and Agbaoye of Ibadanland, Mr. Kola Karim. To God be the glory, the harrowing event ended in praise rather than tragedy, reminding everyone of the fragility of life and the supreme grace of the Almighty.

​A Close Shave in the Skies of Abuja

​The incident, which sent shockwaves through the aviation and public sectors, occurred when an aircraft connected to the Shoreline Energy boss experienced a rare and dangerous structural failure—losing its door mid-flight shortly after taking off from Abuja en route to Lagos. Flying thousands of feet in the air, a situation of that magnitude spells instant disaster in standard aviation terms. Yet, through extraordinary pilot professionalism, quick-thinking crew coordination, and divine intervention, the flight managed to squawk a Mayday call and execute a safe emergency landing back at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport. 
​When news broke of the miraculous survival of those on board, sympathizers and well-wishers across the country let out a collective sigh of relief. Indeed, we must thank God for preserving his life and the lives of everyone on board.

​A Pillar of Industry and Tradition

​Beyond his corporate identity as a titan in energy, infrastructure, and international business as the head of Shoreline Energy International, Chief Kola Karim holds a revered traditional stool as the Agbaoye of Ibadanland. He is a leader who blends modern corporate sagacity with deep-rooted cultural heritage. 
​As Agbaoye, he is not only a prominent ambassador of Ibadan kingdom's rich values of resilience, bravery, and integrity, but he is also a key contributor to national economic development. Men of his caliber carry immense responsibilities—employing hundreds, driving investments, and shaping key sectors of the African economy. Losing such a dynamic figure would have created a monumental vacuum, making his miraculous survival a blessing not just to his immediate family, but to the nation at large.

​Conclusion

​The miraculous escape from the jaws of tragedy serves as a poignant reminder to stay humble and always return all glory to God, who holds the breath of all men in His hands. As the Agbaoye of Ibadanland continues his invaluable service to humanity, commerce, and tradition, this brush with mortality only reinforces the depth of grace surrounding his life. We join family, friends, associates, and the good people of Ibadanland in shouting a resounding Alhamdulillahi / E se Olohun for sparing his life. May his days be long, and may divine protection continually envelop him and his endeavors.@kolaKarim

text:
"With thee is the fountain of life."  Psalm 36:9 

There are times in our spiritual experience when human counsel or sympathy, or religious ordinances, fail to comfort or help us. Why does our gracious God permit this? Perhaps it is because we have been living too much without him, and he therefore takes away everything upon which we have been in the habit of depending, that he may drive us to himself. 

It is a blessed thing to live at the fountain head. 

While our skin-bottles are full, we are content, like Hagar and Ishmael, to go into the wilderness; but when those are dry, nothing will serve us but "Thou God seest me." We are like the prodigal, we love the swine-troughs and forget our Father's house. 

Remember, we can make swine-troughs and husks even out of the forms of religion; they are blessed things, but we may put them in God's place, and then they are of no value. Anything becomes an idol when it keeps us away from God: even the brazen serpent is to be despised as "Nehushtan," if we worship it instead of God. 

Genesis 6:6

[6] And the LORD regretted that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him to his heart.

Job 13:23

    [23] How many are my iniquities and my sins?
        Make me know my transgression and my sin.

The prodigal was never safer than when he was driven to his father's bosom, because he could find sustenance nowhere else. Our Lord favours us with a famine in the land that it may make us seek after himself the more. The best position for a Christian is living wholly and directly on God's grace—still abiding where he stood at first—"Having nothing, and yet possessing all things." 

Revelation 3:3

[3] Remember, then, what you received and heard. Keep it, and repent. If you will not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come against you.

Let us never for a moment think that our standing is in our sanctification, our mortification, our graces, or our feelings, but know that because Christ offered a full atonement, therefore we are saved; for we are complete in him. Having nothing of our own to trust to, but resting upon the merits of Jesus—his passion and holy life furnish us with the only sure ground of confidence. 

Proverbs 17:9

    [9] 
    Whoever covers an offense seeks love,
        but he who repeats a matter separates close friends.

Psalm 97:11

    [11] Light is sown for the righteous,
        and joy for the upright in heart.

Psalm 100:1

    [1] Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth!

Beloved, when we are brought to a thirsting condition, we are sure to turn to the fountain of life with eagerness.

Philippians 3:3

[3] For we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God and glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh—

The Distant Republic:

A historical epic set in Mexico and the American Southwest, 1835–1848

* warning - AI generated content.  Viewer discretion is advised *

Mexico views its northern territories as an inseparable part of its national inheritance, even as it is obvious they are unable to administer, populate, and defend them.

The United States sees the same territory through a different lens: a vast expanse of agricultural land, mineral resources, Pacific ports, commercial corridors, and communities that might be integrated into an expanding continental economy.
American leaders believe their institutions, capital, transportation networks, and migration could develop the region. Mexico cannot.

The dramatic irony is that American officials cannot understand why Mexico refuses to sell territory that it struggles to govern, while Mexican officials cannot understand why Americans believe administrative weakness should make national territory negotiable.

In the White House:
POLK: How much revenue do these provinces return to Mexico?
ADVISER: Little that reaches the national treasury, Mr. President.
POLK: And what does it cost them to maintain the garrisons?
ADVISER: More than they can reliably pay.
POLK: Can they protect the settlements?
ADVISER: Not consistently.
POLK: Can they govern California from Mexico City?
ADVISER: Not as they would wish.
POLK: Then explain something to me. We offer them money they desperately need, for territory they cannot properly govern, defend, or develop. Why will they not sell?
BUCHANAN: Because, Mr. President, they do not consider it a question of money.
POLK: Everything has a price.
BUCHANAN: Not to a nation that believes selling its land is admitting it has ceased to be a nation.

Cut away to conversation in Mexico:
MINISTER: They offer enough money to retire debts, equip the army, and restore the treasury.
ISABEL: And what do they ask in return?
MINISTER: California. New Mexico. Recognition of their boundary in Texas.
ISABEL: Then they are not offering to rescue Mexico. They are offering to purchase our weakness.
MINISTER: Can we defend these territories?
ISABEL: Not with the resources we possess.
MINISTER: Then what are we defending?
ISABEL: The proposition that a nation's sovereignty does not depend upon the wealth of its neighbor.

text:
Friendship Park: Bringing Kurdish Identity to a Public Space in Minnesota

By Jihan Brifki — Writing for Kurdish Identity Voice

In Moorhead, Minnesota, Friendship Park celebrates a connection that reaches across continents: the friendship between Moorhead and Zakho, Kurdistan. Featuring the Kurdish flag, signage naming Zakho, Kurdistan, and a friendship proclamation displayed in Kurdish and English, the park gives our community a visible place in the city’s public life.

For me, seeing this project come to life is deeply meaningful. It reflects the relationships I have worked to build and my commitment to sharing Kurdish identity, culture and history with a wider audience.

Building a Friendship Across Borders

The project grew out of my efforts to strengthen ties between Moorhead and Zakho. Through numerous online meetings with Moorhead Mayor Shelly Carlson, Dan Mahli and Guhdar Sheekhoo, head of the Zakho Independent Administration, we worked to turn a shared interest in friendship into a lasting relationship.

The two cities signed an official friendship proclamation. Educational cooperation followed: on July 2, 2025, President Downs of Minnesota State University Moorhead signed a memorandum of understanding with the University of Zakho.

These developments helped build the relationship that Friendship Park now celebrates.

From an Idea to a Public Place

I worked with Moorhead’s parks director for nearly a year to help bring the idea to life. Special credit goes to Sean Bradenburg for considering the proposal and helping secure the support of the parks board and city leaders.

Moorhead opened Friendship Park this year, creating a space that honors the growing bond between the two communities.

I have led and coordinated efforts between the cities, but this friendship has grown through shared learning and mutual support. Its value extends beyond financial contributions. One example of the practical support connected to our work is a 40-foot container of donated medical equipment, valued at more than $1 million, that we sent to Kurdistan.

A Place for Kurdish Identity

The name Friendship Park reflects the proclamation between Moorhead and Zakho. For the Kurdish community, the presence of the Kurdish flag and our language in a public space carries particular significance.

To our knowledge, this is the first park in the United States dedicated to a city in Kurdistan to feature both the Kurdish flag and Kurdish-language signage. That understanding makes the recognition especially meaningful to us.

Visitors can encounter the name of Zakho, see the Kurdish flag and read the friendship proclamation in Kurdish and English. Each element offers an opportunity to learn about a people, a language and a history they may not previously have known.

The Beginning of a Larger Vision

The park marks the beginning of a broader effort to introduce Kurdish culture and history through a welcoming community space.

We want people to enjoy the park while discovering more about Kurdish heritage. As this work develops, we hope to create further opportunities to share our story, encourage cultural understanding and advocate for the Kurdish people.

Growing up in America has given me opportunities to speak on behalf of my community and build meaningful relationships for Kurdistan. I have always loved advocating for my people.

Seeing that work reflected in a public place—where our language is visible, our flag is represented and our history can become part of a wider conversation—is something I am deeply proud of.

Jihan Brifki writes for Kurdish Identity Voice about her role in building the friendship between Moorhead and Zakho and bringing Friendship Park to life.

WHAT IF WE HAVE BEEN ASKING THE WRONG QUESTION ABOUT GLIOBLASTOMA?

WHAT IF IMMUNOTHERAPY FAILS NOT BECAUSE T CELLS CANNOT FIGHT BUT BECAUSE TOO FEW EVER ENTER THE TUMOR?

Two UCLA studies reported October 13 offer a fascinating clinical and laboratory perspective!

In a phase 2 trial 63 patients with recurrent glioblastoma received nivolumab plus ipilimumab or nivolumab alone or placebo before surgery!

Median survival was approximately 13 and a half months with the combination compared with roughly 9 months with nivolumab alone!

Five patients receiving both drugs became long term survivors!

THE MOST IMPORTANT CLUE?

Tumors containing more T cells were associated with longer survival!

But why do so many glioblastomas remain almost empty of cancer fighting T cells?

A second UCLA team developed a more realistic experimental brain tumor model!

It reproduced the immune cold environment seen in patients!

Very few T cells entered!

Myeloid cells dominated!

And checkpoint blockade failed to control the tumors!

Together these studies suggest an extraordinary possibility!

Perhaps we must first GET IMMUNE CELLS INTO THE TUMOR before asking checkpoint inhibitors to reactivate them!

As a hematologist oncologist I find the patient implications profound!

Robert Prins and Timothy Cloughesy have spent years investigating brain tumor immunity and resistance!

Their work now raises five questions!

FIRST!

Can we identify the patients whose tumors already contain enough T cells to benefit from dual checkpoint blockade?

SECOND!

Can vaccines or engineered immune cells turn immune cold glioblastoma into immune hot disease?

THIRD!

Can targeting suppressive myeloid cells improve T cell entry and persistence?

FOURTH!

Could early MRI changes reflect useful immune inflammation rather than tumor progression?

FIFTH!

Can blood and tumor biomarkers predict benefit without exposing everyone to dual immunotherapy toxicity?

MY NEXT EXPERIMENT!

Test combinations in patient matched tumor models and then prospectively validate immune biomarkers in carefully designed trials!

These findings are promising but the trial was small and survival comparisons do not establish a new standard of care!

THE NEXT BREAKTHROUGH MAY NOT BE A STRONGER IMMUNE DRUG!

IT MAY BE LEARNING HOW TO OPEN THE DOOR TO THE BRAIN TUMOR!

What would you target first to make glioblastoma vulnerable to immunity?

text:
Value-Focused Plays: British Champions Day

Two-Year-Old Conditions
🏇3-CONFUCIUS 18
Massive price on $2.4m Ballydoyle colt Confucius who has dodged no one and takes a marked drop in class after a race in which I had no idea why they would add blinkers and then ask him to take back to last. He had not run in two months, so perhaps they were just giving him a racecourse gallop. Expecting a more forward run with the move back to Moore and a mid-pack draw. Should be in the mix and wouldn’t be shocked with a big effort and possible win.

G1 Long Distance Cup
🏇7-QUEENSTOWN 11
Simply love the way this horse has come into this race, improving as the season has plugged along, while taking on a field of horses with ample questions to answer. Is Gregory going to back up his big comeback? Can Highwayman be as effective over 2mi? Has the season been too busy for Caballo de Mar? In the end, this 6yo makes his 4th start of the season and should be ready to fire his best at a nice value—especially when allowed to run his own race and not be a pacemaker for Scandinavia. He will be forward, but not forced to use any more petrol than required.

G1 Sprint Stakes
🏇12-DIVISION 10/1
Division was best in the G1 Prix Maurice de Gheest and a return to that form with a bit more luck and maturity begets a very good run here over a track he’s proven he likes. He also provides a ton more value than his odds-on stablemate.

G1 Fillies & Mares Stakes
🏇10-LILT 8/1
Granted, 12f is a big question mark for this daughter of 8-10f specialist and BC F&M Turf champ Dank, but I do think Lilt deserves a chance here to be the ‘now filly’ for Haggas. Nearly a duplicate in markings of her star mother, her strong finish in the G2 Blandford over 10f hints that maybe 12f will suit and Lope de Vega infused enough stamina to do so. Really looking forward to seeing how this plays out because she could be improving at the right time against a couple logical favorites—Kalpana & Minnie Hauk—who will be bet enthusiastically.

G1 Queen Elizabeth II Stakes
🏇9-RAYIF 15/2
Rayif is still improving and has targeted this race since his run in the Marois, where I tipped him, as well. I think he’s sitting on another step forward and is simply not as stylish a player to punters as Gstaad & Talk of New York and his numbers stack up right against them. Graffard gets all my respect. Additionally, in my mind, I always feel like the French do well, compared to the summer ground they tackle during Royal Ascot.

G1 Champion Stakes 
🏇1-ALMAQAM 10/1
Not sure what Almaqam has done wrong except win the Tatts Gold Cup, nearly win the Juddmonte, come back too soon and still run respectably as a tired horse in the Irish Champion and return to the course, distance & race day at which he ran a blinder last year to be third—and he’s an improved animal now. Squarely the value of the race and I love the inside post for his style.

Balmoral Handicap
🏇18-HICKORY 11/1
Hickory offers solid value here if you get him before everyone else figures out that he should love the move back to a mile, as well as to Saffie, who is riding with a lot of confidence. A horse who lives up to his name and should have something to say about this race.

text:
🇮🇷🇶🇦|Tehran Unconvinced by Qatar’s “Explanation”

Brigadier General Bagherzadeh of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) made a statement that captures Tehran’s dwindling patience with Doha far more precisely than any standard diplomatic rhetoric:

“Qatar’s statement regarding the Iranian pilots is entirely unconvincing. The dispatch of a second expert team implies that the first team uncovered certain facts, facts that, at the very least, failed to reassure or persuade our experts, standing in stark contrast to the claims and assertions put forward by the Qatari authorities.”

💥 What This Statement Implies

The mention of a “second expert team” is the crucial detail.

If Qatar’s explanation were credible, a single expert team would have sufficed. That team would have returned with a report confirming that “the Qatari account aligns with the facts,” and the matter would have been closed.

Instead, the first team returned with “certain facts,” facts that do not align with Qatar’s narrative. Iran remains unconvinced, prompting Tehran to send a second team.

This is not merely a diplomatic friction; it is a contest over the truth. Qatar attempted to offer an explanation, which Iran rejected sending further personnel to dismantle it.

🎯 What Is Qatar Trying to Conceal?

The incident involving Iranian pilots in Qatar must be viewed against the backdrop of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, which has been ongoing since February 2026.

Qatar hosts one of the largest U.S. military installations in the Middle East: Al Udeid Air Base, which also serves as the forward headquarters for U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM). This U.S. military presence is being utilized in the war against Iran; the runways at Al Udeid have facilitated the operations of U.S. bombers, aerial tankers, and reconnaissance aircraft.

Simultaneously, Qatar positions itself as a regional mediator. It facilitated talks between the U.S. and Ansarallah in Muscat in September 2026 and has acted as an intermediary in Gaza-related negotiations. It strives to maintain an open channel between Tehran and Washington.

However, the roles of a regional mediator and a host to U.S. military bases cannot coexist indefinitely.  If the explanation provided by Qatar regarding the incident involving an Iranian pilot proves untenable, Tehran has reason to ask: whom is Doha protecting?

📜 What does "not reassuring" mean?

Bagherzadeh’s exact words were that the Qatari account was "not reassuring" and "did not convince them."

In diplomatic parlance, "not reassuring" is a weighty term. It goes beyond merely saying, "We still have questions." It implies: "We suspect you are hiding something."

While Iran has not explicitly accused Qatar of lying, the very act of dispatching a second expert team serves as a formal declaration of distrust.

Had Doha’s explanation been complete, honest, and verifiable, there would have been no need for a second team. The fact that a second team was sent suggests that what the first team observed contradicts what Doha has claimed.

⚔️ Qatar’s dual stance

During the conflict, the Emir of Qatar, Tamim, stated that Qatar would "not get involved in the war," while simultaneously warning that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz would be devastating for global energy markets. Qatar has also previously accused Iran of a "blatant violation of sovereignty" against its territory and called for enhanced maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz.

Even as it accuses Iran of aggression, Qatar permits the United States to maintain military bases on its soil, bases used for operations against Iran. While advocating for security in the Strait, it refuses to join any military actions directed at Iran. It acts as a mediator, yet simultaneously provides a base for Washington.

The incident involving the Iranian pilot has brought this Qatari duality into sharp focus. Doha can no longer rely on the vague defense that "we are mediators." Tehran demands verifiable facts, not diplomatic rhetoric.

🔻 The significance of the second expert team

There is a detail in Bagherzadeh’s remarks that has not received sufficient attention: he did not say the first expert team "failed." Instead, he stated that the first team "had already established certain facts."

This implies that Iran is already in possession of something—be it a timeline, a piece of testimony, a document, or a technical assessment.  These findings are inconsistent with Doha’s account. The mandate of the second expert panel was not to conduct an “investigation from scratch,” but rather to take the facts established by the first panel and use them to verify, probe, and expose the truth.

Tehran did not escalate this into an overt diplomatic crisis. It did not recall its ambassador, expel Qatari diplomats, or single out Doha by name during meetings of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.

Yet, it dispatched a second expert panel. This move alone speaks more clearly than any public statement: Iran does not believe Qatar’s version of events regarding the Iranian pilots.

Long live Iran. Long live the Resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

The Rise Of The Far Right In Europe: Capitalism's Useful Ally And The Tasks Of Communists 
by Nikos Mottas
“The growing influence of nationalist and far-right forces across Europe is neither accidental nor a development occurring outside the capitalist system.

It is closely connected with the needs of capitalist power itself, at a time when imperialist rivalries are intensifying, preparations for war are accelerating and the established bourgeois parties are finding it increasingly difficult to secure popular consent for their policies. The rise of the Alternative for Germany (AfD), France's National Rally and Britain's Reform UK, alongside the experience of Giorgia Meloni's government in Italy, points to significant changes in Europe's political landscape. 

Far from representing a genuine challenge to capitalist domination, these forces offer additional political options to sections of the bourgeoisie seeking to adapt to the changing international situation. Capitalism does not merely create the social discontent exploited by the far right. It also provides the political conditions in which nationalist and reactionary forces can channel that discontent away from the struggle against capitalist power. 

The sharpening competition between the United States and China, the confrontation between NATO and Russia, and the struggle over markets, energy resources and trade routes are aggravating contradictions within the Euro-Atlantic bloc itself. Different sections of European capital have competing interests concerning relations with Washington, Moscow and Beijing, the future of the European Union, military expenditure and the consequences of sanctions and economic confrontation. 

These disagreements inevitably find expression in the political systems of the capitalist states.”

POMPEO BLASTS FRANCE AND GERMANY FOR LETTING EUROPE’S DEFENSE COLLAPSE 🇺🇸🇫🇷🇩🇪🇵🇱🇺🇦🇷🇺

Former U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo has delivered a harsh assessment of Europe’s security failures, accusing major European powers of spending years relying on Washington while neglecting their own military preparedness.

In particular, Pompeo singled out France and Germany for criticism, arguing that both countries failed to take deterrence seriously. He offered a more favorable assessment of Poland and the Baltic states, but maintained that European governments collectively underestimated the danger posed by Russia.

His accusation was blunt: Europeans effectively took a holiday while expecting America to handle the difficult work of defending the continent.

Pompeo believes the consequences are now visible in Ukraine, where Russia’s full-scale invasion has entered its fifth year.

Drawing on his visits to Kyiv, he claimed that Russian forces are losing approximately 1,000 personnel every day through deaths and injuries. Those figures reflect his assessment rather than independently verified battlefield totals.

For Pompeo, however, the problem extends beyond Ukraine. He warned that adversaries interpret insufficient military preparation as weakness and may exploit opportunities when European governments appear unwilling to defend themselves.

He also credited Donald Trump with forcing NATO members to confront their defense responsibilities, arguing that pressure from Washington, combined with the threat posed by Vladimir Putin, has finally pushed Europe toward taking its own security more seriously.

Pompeo does not believe NATO must collapse. His argument is that the alliance can survive if its European members invest sufficiently in their armed forces, accept a greater share of the burden and demonstrate that they are prepared to defend their own populations.

His criticism leaves European governments facing an uncomfortable question: after years of relying heavily on American military power, have they done enough to ensure they could respond effectively if Washington were unwilling or unable to lead?

For Pompeo, Europe’s future security depends on what its governments are prepared to do themselves, rather than what they continue expecting the United States to provide.

Our historic doors opened to a new generation of curious minds, and it was a special pleasure to welcome the fifth-grade Warriors of First Baptist Christian School! Accompanied by Rebecca Smith Cobo, educator and ministry leader at First Baptist Stuart, these bright young visitors brought wonderful energy and curiosity  to our little pioneer church.

As part of First Baptist Christian School’s “Warrior Life” program, students are encouraged to grow beyond the classroom through experiences that bring together academics, Christian faith, and community involvement.

Their visit to The 1895 Church of Stuart offered an opportunity to connect these values with local history and discover how faith, perseverance, and a strong sense of community shaped the lives of our early pioneers.

Built in 1895, when Stuart was still known as Potsdam, our little church has witnessed more than 130 years of local history.

During their visit, we briefly traveled back to the pioneering days of our community, exploring how early settlers lived, worked, worshiped, and built a town along the St. Lucie River.

We talked about the important role churches played in pioneer communities—not only as places of worship, but also as centers of social life, fellowship, education, and community gatherings.

In those early days, churches helped bring families together, strengthen relationships, and create a sense of belonging in a developing settlement.

The students also learned about Dade County pine, the remarkably durable native lumber used to construct many of the area's earliest buildings, including our historic church. Standing among the original wooden walls, they had an opportunity to see and touch the very materials that pioneer craftsmen worked with more than a century ago.

Our journey through history also included the arrival of Henry Flagler's Florida East Coast Railway in 1894, the pioneers who helped establish Potsdam, and the story of how the little settlement eventually became known as Stuart.

And the history lesson didn't end at our church!

Gary Zingo, an Army veteran, tram driver, and knowledgeable downtown Stuart history tour guide, continued the students' journey into the past.

There is something especially meaningful about watching young people discover history within the walls of a building that has stood for more than 130 years. 

After all, today's young Warriors are tomorrow's guardians of our community's heritage

❤️ Our heartfelt thanks to Rebecca Smith Cobo, the fifth-grade Warriors of First Baptist Christian School, and Gary Zingo for being part of this memorable day! We loved sharing our little church and its stories with you, and we hope to welcome you back again!

How to Host Mystery Discussions that Spark Clues
#cozymystery #dogs #cats
The best mystery discussion begins just after someone says, “I never saw that coming.” That delighted groan is an invitation to compare clues, defend a favorite suspect, and revisit the tiny detail everyone missed. If you are learning **how to host mystery discussions**, think less about running a formal class and more about setting a friendly table for readers who enjoy a good puzzle.

Cozy mystery readers bring different pleasures to the page. One person loves the alibi chart. Another is there for the small-town bakery, the quirky neighbor, or the animal sidekick with better instincts than the sheriff. A great gathering makes room for all of it, including readers who solved the case by chapter three and readers who were happily fooled until the final reveal.

## Start with a Mystery Worth Talking About

The best book club choice is not always the most complicated mystery. Pick a story with enough possible suspects, motives, and clues to give readers something concrete to discuss. A book with a memorable setting, a lively amateur sleuth, and a satisfying solution tends to work especially well because the conversation can move beyond “Who did it?”

For a relaxed first meeting, choose a standalone or the first book in a series. Readers are more comfortable joining in when they do not fear they have missed six earlier adventures. If your group already knows one another well, a later installment can be fun, particularly when members enjoy tracking how familiar characters have changed.

Consider the group’s comfort level, too. A classic puzzle may suit readers who want to examine every clue. A lighter cozy mystery is often better for a mixed gathering of longtime mystery fans, casual readers, and guests who mainly came to enjoy good company. Neither choice is more serious than the other. The goal is a conversation people want to return to.

## Set the Ground Rules Before the First Clue

Mystery readers have strong feelings about spoilers, and for good reason. One careless mention of a culprit can take the fizz out of a carefully built plot. Before the meeting, tell everyone whether the discussion assumes the book has been finished. If not, choose a clear stopping point and limit questions to that section.

Even in a finished-book discussion, begin with a spoiler warning. Give anyone who is still reading a chance to step away from the main plot talk or simply listen without being surprised by the ending. It is a small kindness that makes a club feel welcoming rather than competitive.

A few simple agreements help: let people finish their thought, disagree with theories rather than with people, and avoid treating the fastest reader as the winner. A mystery discussion is not a courtroom. It is closer to neighbors swapping stories on a porch while the dog watches everyone very carefully.

## How to Host Mystery Discussions Without Turning Them Into a Quiz

A page of rigid questions can make a book club feel like homework. Instead, prepare a handful of open prompts that invite readers to follow whatever thread interests them. Start broad, then become more specific as people warm up.

Ask what readers noticed first about the setting and whether it helped them trust the sleuth. Talk about which suspect seemed most convincing, not only who seemed guilty. Ask whether the clues felt fair once the solution was revealed. Those questions allow both plot-focused readers and character-focused readers to take part.

You can also ask about the sleuth’s methods. Did the main character have a useful skill, local knowledge, or a personal connection that opened doors? Did that advantage make the investigation believable? In a series such as the Doc and Daisy Mysteries, veterinary experience and canine observations can create a playful conversation about what animals notice that people overlook.

When the group goes quiet, return to a specific scene. “What did you make of the missing recipe card?” is easier to answer than “What did everyone think?” Concrete details give shy readers a safe way in.

### Questions That Encourage Better Theories

Good mystery questions do not demand one correct response. They make room for evidence, intuition, and a little friendly second-guessing. Try prompts such as these:

- Which clue seemed ordinary at first but mattered later?
- Who had the strongest motive, and who had the best opportunity?
- When did you change your mind about a character?
- Did the ending feel earned? Why or why not?
- What role did the town, workplace, or family history play in the crime?
- If you were the sleuth, what would you investigate next?

Do not feel obliged to use every question. Two lively prompts can produce a better hour than twenty hurried ones. Follow the energy in the room, especially when readers begin building on one another’s observations.

## Give Everyone a Way Into the Case

Some guests arrive with notes tucked inside their book. Others finished the story in the parking lot and are hoping nobody asks about chapter numbers. Both belong at the table.

At the beginning, invite each person to share one word for their reading experience: surprised, suspicious, charmed, frustrated, delighted. This takes less than five minutes and immediately reveals where the conversation might go. It also lets quieter members speak before the more enthusiastic detectives take over.

If one person is dominating, gently redirect with a question for the group. “I’d love to hear a different theory,” works better than calling someone out. If the room is reserved, use a quick pair discussion before opening the topic to everyone. People often find their voice after testing an idea with one other reader.

It helps to remember that solving the mystery early is not the only form of participation. A reader who notices the emotional stakes, questions an assumption about a suspect, or points out a wonderfully odd detail is contributing to the case.

## Add a Little Atmosphere, Not a Production

A themed meeting can be delightful, but it should never become another burden for the host. The book is the main event. A pot of coffee, tea, sparkling water, and a simple snack are plenty.

If you enjoy a touch of fun, borrow one small detail from the story. A Florida-set mystery might inspire citrus cookies. A library mystery could call for bookmarks at each place setting. An animal-loving group might bring a photo of a beloved pet or donate a small item to a local shelter. Keep it optional and easy.

You might place a few index cards on the table for anonymous questions or theories. This works well when guests do not know one another, and it can produce wonderfully bold guesses. Read a card aloud between topics and let the group decide whether the writer is onto something or has been distracted by a red herring.

## Know When to Leave a Clue Unexamined

Hosts sometimes feel responsible for covering every character, every twist, and every loose end. Resist that urge. A conversation with room to breathe is better than a rushed tour through your notes.

If the group becomes fascinated by whether a certain character was treated fairly, let that topic develop. If readers are laughing over the town gossip or debating whether the sleuth should have called the police sooner, that is real engagement. You can always save an unused question for next month.

Near the end, ask one final question that carries the discussion beyond the solution: Would you read another book with this sleuth? The answer often tells you more about a mystery than a score out of five. Readers may forgive a far-fetched moment if they want to spend another afternoon in that town with those characters.

Before everyone leaves, announce the next selection or invite suggestions. A small mystery club grows through consistency, not perfection. Offer a warm welcome, protect the surprises, and give every reader a chance to share the clue that caught their eye. Soon enough, your gathering may become the kind of place where people arrive early, theories ready, and perhaps a little suspicious of whoever brought the cookies.

The most remarkable feature of these two volumes is the proposed capacity of a living organism to undergo extraordinary alterations of sensation, volition, memory, bodily representation, and physical influence while preserving an underlying continuity of identity. In Collyer's terminology, this capacity depends upon an elusive nervo-vital principle, whose concentration, displacement, exhaustion, and renewal supposedly govern the passage from ordinary consciousness into somnambulism, ecstasy, anaesthesia, and other exalted conditions. In Hare's investigations, the corresponding problem acquires an astonishing instrumental character: whether an intelligence independent of an observer's ordinary sensory faculties might communicate its intentions through the measurable displacement of matter.

The consequences of bringing these authors into the same investigation are particularly revealing.

Collyer's Exalted States supplies a peculiar vocabulary of nervous reservoirs, vital photography, inherited impressions, cerebral exaltation, electro-biological transmission, atmospheric inhalation, nervous vibration, and voluntary metamorphosis. His account of the brain assumes that impressions may outlast conscious recollection and reappear under exceptional physiological conditions. His examples encompass dormant linguistic knowledge, heightened somnambulistic faculties, peculiar congenital representations, responsive inorganic substances, and the remarkable influence he attributes to concentrated faith.

His chapter on vital photography is especially extraordinary. Here the word photography extends beyond the conventional formation of an optical image. It describes the supposed inscription of experience into nervous organization, occasionally attaining a degree of physical expression. Reported maternal impressions, bodily markings, animal resemblances, and stigmata become parts of one speculative physiology of image transmission. These reports furnish a remarkable historical archive of alleged hereditary metamorphosis, although the extraordinary causal mechanisms Collyer proposes are not established by the anecdotes.

The positive atavistic dimension of the work appears most clearly in its discussions of dormant capacities. An apparently forgotten language, a lost impression of childhood, or a faculty absent from waking consciousness may re-emerge in an altered state. His experimental apparatus translates alleged manifestations into mechanical displacements: rotating alphabetic disks, oscillating levers, balances, weighted pulleys, wheeled platforms, and arrangements intended to exclude ordinary muscular pressure. His Plate III supplies a particularly striking example. The extraordinary physiological and experimental investigations of Dr. Robert H. Collyer (1873) and Dr. Robert Hare (1855) preserve two remarkably elaborate nineteenth-century systems of invisible agency, nervous transformation, molecular activity, cerebral exaltation, organic metamorphosis, and the alleged interaction of material and spiritual existence. Their combined intellectual significance emerges from an unusual convergence of medical experimentation, electrochemical philosophy, anomalous mechanics, comparative antiquity, biblical cosmography, and speculative theories of the vital principle. Within these investigations, the living organism appears as an exceptionally responsive configuration of sensory faculties, electrical activity, nervous excitation, retained impressions, muscular volition, and transformative developmental processes, while the external world becomes the proposed theatre of forces whose operations extend beyond immediately visible mechanical phenomena.

Collyer's Exalted States of the Nervous System introduces an extensive physiological investigation of consciousness under extraordinary conditions. Anaesthesia, somnambulism, trance, ecstatic insensibility, cerebral congestion, visual fixation, nervous exhaustion, magnetic induction, respiratory excitation, and the restoration of dormant faculties are interpreted through his proposed nervo-vital principle. 

The resulting model attributes exceptional importance to the concentration, redistribution, and expenditure of nervous activity, particularly where ordinary sensory relationships appear suspended or radically altered. 

His comparisons between inhalational anaesthesia, mesmerism, concentrated attention, and natural sleep establish a striking historical theory of state-dependent cerebral transformation. 

Especially important are the reports of forgotten languages reappearing during illness, unusual intellectual accomplishments during somnambulism, and memories apparently inaccessible to waking consciousness. These accounts invite a specialized investigation of positive anamnetic atavism, latent cerebral impressions, mnemonic reactivation, and the extraordinary phenomenology of recovered capacities.

Among Collyer's most singular contributions is his theory of vital photography, an ambitious attempt to account for the persistence and physical expression of nervous impressions. He considers the brain an extraordinarily sensitive recipient of experiential images and proposes that powerful impressions may influence the wider organization of living tissue. His examples include devotional stigmata, alleged maternal impressions, unusual congenital formations, animal resemblances, and bodily responses attributed to intense mental conviction. These materials belong to a historically important literature of psychosomatic morphology, teratology, cerebral imagery, reproductive speculation, and the relationship between imagination and physical embodiment. Their accompanying anatomical and physiological theories also expose the nineteenth-century search for causal correspondences between transient mental events and comparatively permanent organic structures.

The chapters concerning the creative function extend these questions into embryological development, anatomical differentiation, crystallographic analogies, and the successive transformations of animal life. Collyer's treatment of the developing ovum, the progressive formation of organs, and the metamorphosis of insects supplies a particularly rich foundation for examining what may be termed morphogenetic amplitude: the magnitude of structural transformation occurring between successive conditions of a living organism. His discussion of the punctum saliens, the initiating vital point, further connects embryological speculation with older natural-philosophical inquiries into the organization of matter and the emergence of articulated living forms.

The historical range of Collyer's investigations is equally remarkable. 

Ancient Egyptian initiation, the mysteries of Trophonius, Greek narcotic preparations, mandragorean anaesthesia, the mineral substance called Memphetis, medieval soporific sponges, Chinese medical traditions, and the pneumatic experiments of Humphry Davy enter a comprehensive account of induced insensibility. 

Particularly unusual is the association of ancient ritual preparations with surgical pharmacology, revealing an extensive field for investigating the transmission of obscure medicinal procedures through Greek, Latin, medieval, and early-modern literature. 

Collyer's documentary treatment of the nineteenth-century anaesthesia controversy also preserves valuable testimony concerning Horace Wells, William T. G. Morton, Charles T. Jackson, James Young Simpson, and the disputed chronology of inhalational discoveries.

Robert Hare's Experimental Investigation of the Spirit Manifestations introduces an entirely different experimental architecture. 

His elaborate spiritoscopic instruments, alphabetic indicators, rotating disks, pulley systems, spring balances, water-filled vessels, mechanical isolators, and weighted levers embody an attempt to subject purported invisible agency to physical measurement. 

The distinctive importance of these instruments lies in their translation of alleged extraordinary effects into observable displacements, symbolic communication, and calculable mechanical forces. Particularly striking are Hare's experiments involving the spring balance and unequal lever arms, through which a reported alteration of three pounds in the balance indication becomes an inferred eighteen-pound applied force. 

Such arrangements provide rare historical material for studying experimental control, instrumental sensitivity, static equilibrium, physical measurement, and nineteenth-century efforts to investigate extraordinary manifestations.

Hare's apparatus also introduces a curious form of mechanical information processing. His revolving alphabetic disks convert physical movement into readable characters, creating an unusual analogy with telegraphic communication. 

Visual screens, spherical supports, modified fulcrums, and arrangements intended to interrupt ordinary muscular influence reveal the experimental strategies employed to distinguish intentional mechanical interference from supposedly independent physical action. 

The resulting investigations occupy a distinctive position in the history of experimental spiritualism, anomalous instrumentation, mechanical communication, and the interpretation of phenomena attributed to invisible intelligences.

An especially important and comparatively neglected component of Hare's volume is its advanced discussion of electrical and molecular philosophy. 

His investigations of electro-ethereal polarization, ethereo-ponderable atomic constitution, electrical induction, galvanic reaction, molecular polarity, surface conduction, Leyden-jar discharge, magnetic effects, and electrical deflagration preserve a substantial technical vocabulary rarely associated with spiritualist literature. 

The discussions involving Faraday, Franklin, Ampère, and Mossotti situate Hare within major nineteenth-century controversies concerning the constitution of matter, the transmission of electrical action, and the theoretical relationship between ponderable substances and hypothetical ethereal media.

 These passages furnish an independent historical pathway into pre-electromagnetic-field theories of subtle matter, microscopic polarization, oscillatory electrical behaviour, and the proposed unification of seemingly dissimilar physical effects.

Beyond the laboratory, Hare develops an elaborate cosmography of post-mortem existence. 

Communications attributed to surviving intelligences describe graded celestial spheres, spiritual birth, continuing intellectual advancement, affinities between persons, rarefied forms of nourishment, and supposed agencies capable of operating upon terrestrial matter. These descriptions constitute an unusual system of progressive supernatural anthropology, in which personal identity, cognition, moral development, and the acquisition of knowledge are represented as continuing through successive conditions of existence. 

Their conceptual structure invites detailed comparison with biblical eschatology, ancient philosophical accounts of the soul, Swedenborgian cosmography, Neoplatonic gradations of being, and historical theories of spiritual substance.

Of particular significance is the fundamental disagreement between the two authors. 

Collyer frequently interprets extraordinary manifestations through the nervous capacities of embodied human beings, including cerebral imagery, concentrated volition, and the supposed projection of the vital principle. Hare increasingly attributes certain manifestations to independent surviving intelligences and constructs mechanical experiments intended to support that conclusion. 

Their conflicting interpretations preserve an exceptional historical problem concerning the identification of causal agency, the nature of consciousness, the persistence of personal identity, and the evidential relationship between observation and invisible explanation.

The combined works consequently establish an unusually extensive field for the investigation of;

positive atavistic phenomenology,

high-amplitude metamorphic transitions, 

ethereo-ponderable dynamics, 

electro-biological correspondences,

pneumatic physiology,

somatic image inscription, 

instrumental metaphysics,

latent cognitive organization,

molecular force transmission, 

& the dimensional gradation of conscious existence.

 These analytical categories extend the original historical terminology into a comparative framework for examining extraordinary transformations without confusing nineteenth-century theoretical constructions with subsequently established physical mechanisms.

Taken together, the volumes preserve a remarkable archive of obscure scientific language, experimental ingenuity, unconventional medical observation, anomalous physical testimony, philosophical speculation, and supernatural cosmography.

 Their most consequential scholarly contribution lies in the exceptional richness of the questions they preserve: how sensory awareness changes under unusual physiological conditions; how impressions become inaccessible and subsequently recoverable; how living organisms acquire their differentiated forms; how mechanical instruments register and transmit information; how electrical theories develop from observations of invisible action; and how nineteenth-century investigators attempted to describe the ultimate relations of matter, vitality, consciousness, and spiritual existence.

The resulting historical study offers a foundation for renewed investigation into the extraordinary boundaries of the living organism, the hidden constitution of physical processes, and the complex intellectual heritage through which natural philosophers, physicians, chemists, and investigators of spiritual phenomena sought to comprehend the transformations and continuities of existence.

text:
Evan Spiegel was 23 and working out of his dad's house when Mark Zuckerberg offered $3 billion in cash for Snapchat. He said no.

Seven years earlier, Zuckerberg had said no to Yahoo's $1 billion.

In the video below, Spiegel tells Steven Bartlett why he and co-founder Bobby Murphy walked away.

"I wish I could say it was wisdom. Bobby and I loved what we were doing."

They started Snapchat at Stanford in 2011. Their first investors put in $485,000.

In 2013 Facebook was building its own copy, called Poke. Zuckerberg met them in Santa Monica with an offer.

Snapchat had been valued at $800 million. Facebook had paid $1 billion for Instagram.

Earlier, investors had let each founder sell $10 million of stock. With that in the bank, they could afford to say no.

Then Facebook copied them. In 2016 Instagram launched Stories, a feature Snapchat invented.

Snap went public in 2017 at about $24 billion. At its peak it was worth around $130 billion. Today it's about $9 billion.

Spiegel says he never doubted the decision. "Not even a moment."

Yahoo offered Zuckerberg $1 billion.
Zuckerberg offered Spiegel $3 billion.

Would you have taken $3 billion at 23, or kept the app?

If you'd share this with a friend, save it first, then follow for more like it.

Guru Nanga Tales: The Second Pitch (1/3)

Twisted Ben called at 6:10 in the morning, Walnut Creek time, which he considers polite, since it was 9:10 in Toronto. He had read that Redwood Materials would run a Rivian factory on old Rivian batteries. Two questions. Is it a pick. What is the ticker.

Guru Nanga, legs straight out, nimbu pani not yet poured, took the second question first. There is no ticker. Ben said then it is not a pick, it is gossip. The Guru said a pick is a judgment about a company. A ticker is a convenience for people who want to be wrong faster.

Here is why it is a pick. It starts with a lunch.

In 2003 a Stanford graduate named JB Straubel sat down with Elon Musk to pitch an unmanned hydrogen airplane. Musk had no interest. Straubel, at the same table, switched to an electric sports car built from laptop cells. Musk wrote a check. Musk has since said that without that lunch Tesla would not exist, basically. Ben, that is the whole résumé. The rest is footnotes.

People read a track record as a list of wins. Wrong. It is what a man does in the ninety seconds after his idea dies. The airplane died before the food came. The car was born before the bill.

Footnotes. Employee number five at Tesla in 2004. CTO from 2005 to 2019. The first Roadster pack, nearly seven thousand laptop cells, 244 miles. In 2009 a lawsuit was settled and five men, him among them, were declared co-founders. The only founder I know whose founding was settled out of court. In 2023 a proxy adviser called him not independent enough for Tesla's board. The shareholders elected him anyway. Independence is like table tennis. The people who discuss it most have the least.

In 2017, still at Tesla, he started a battery recycler in Carson City, and later admitted he had started it almost too early. Ben said he knew the feeling. Ben's roof also started early.

Redwood takes in more than 20 gigawatt-hours of dead batteries a year, about 250,000 cars' worth, and says it collects most of the packs leaving North American roads. Revenue in 2024: about 200 million dollars. In 2023 the Department of Energy offered it a two-billion-dollar loan. In 2024 it walked away; the costs and conditions, it decided, outweighed the money. text:
The Spiritual Consequences of Mortal Sin: A Catholic Reflection on Repentance and Grace

Sin wounds our relationship with God and weakens our spiritual life. In particular, sins against chastity remind us of the dignity of the human person and the call to honor our bodies as temples of the Holy Spirit. As St. Paul teaches in 1 Corinthians 6:18–20, we are called to flee sexual immorality and glorify God in our bodies.

Catholic spiritual tradition sometimes uses the image of a foul odor to describe the ugliness of sin and the beauty of holiness. Stories attributed to certain saints and priests speak of a spiritual “stench” associated with grave sin. However, such accounts should be treated carefully unless their authenticity can be established. The Church’s central teaching is clear: sin damages our communion with God, while repentance opens our hearts to His mercy.

Mortal Sin and the Need for Conversion

The Catholic Church teaches that mortal sin involves three conditions: grave matter, full knowledge, and deliberate consent. When these conditions are all present, mortal sin destroys charity in the heart and separates a person from sanctifying grace. Nevertheless, no sinner should despair, because God continually calls every person to repentance and reconciliation.

The effects of sin are not limited to sexual misconduct. Pride, greed, dishonesty, hatred, infidelity, and other serious offenses can also damage our relationship with God and with others. We must examine our consciences honestly, resist temptation, and seek the Lord’s help to grow in virtue.

St. Paul reminds us in Romans 6:23 that sin leads to death, while God offers eternal life through Jesus Christ. This is a call to conversion, not an invitation to judge or condemn others. We should be vigilant about our own spiritual lives and extend compassion to those who struggle.

The Sacrament of Confession: A Path to Healing

The Sacrament of Reconciliation is a precious gift through which repentant sinners receive God’s forgiveness and are restored to communion with Him. Through sincere contrition, confession, absolution, and a firm purpose of amendment, we receive the grace to begin again and resist future temptations.

As Jesus teaches in Matthew 26:41, “Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation.” Prayer, frequent reception of the sacraments, reading Scripture, and practicing works of mercy help us remain close to Christ.

We should also remember that illness, financial difficulties, family conflicts, and accidents are not reliable signs that a person is living in sin or experiencing demonic influence. We must never assume that someone is being punished by God because of their suffering.

Become the Fragrance of Christ

In 2 Corinthians 2:15, St. Paul describes believers as “the good odour of Christ.” This beautiful image invites us to make Christ’s presence known through holiness, charity, humility, and faithful service.

The Blessed Virgin Mary leads us toward her Son, while the saints encourage us through their examples of repentance and fidelity. Their witness reminds us that holiness is not the absence of every struggle but a continual turning toward God.

Let us therefore examine our consciences, repent sincerely, seek the grace of Confession, and strive to live in a state of grace. Rather than becoming consumed by fear of evil, let us place our trust in Jesus Christ, who is stronger than sin and whose mercy is always available to the repentant heart.

Choose repentance. Choose grace. Choose holiness. Let your life become a fragrance of Christ’s love in the world.

text:
The left has reacted in their usual and entirely predictable way to Tesla's new flying car. And once again, the explanation is to be found in the Frankfurt School.

Max Horkheimer and Theodor Adorno treated modern technology as the triumph of instrumental reason: the reduction of the world to what can be measured, controlled and made useful. Anything that cannot be justified as efficient or socially necessary is already suspect. 

Herbert Marcuse went further still: advanced industrial society, he argued, integrates people by delivering comforts and spectacles that leave the underlying relations of power untouched. A car that flips for the sake of flipping fails both tests. It is not optimised for transport and it does not expose or overturn domination. It is therefore waste - an affirmative culture that offers intensity without politics.

It is, however, not just the critical theorists - the same instinct appears in older forms too. Rousseau’s suspicion of luxury survives in the idea that ostentation is a moral problem rather than a private choice. Marxist traditions treat concentrations of capital and engineering talent as socially produced and therefore socially accountable; spent on a private demonstration rather than a state-defined need, the expenditure is read as appropriation.

Contemporary environmentalism supplies the immediate language of carbon and opportunity cost, but the deeper move is the same: once every resource is a claim on a shared budget, private technical play becomes difficult to defend. The demand that a new device name its social purpose before it is allowed to exist is a that of a central planner. It assumes the relevant ends are already known. Free-market traditions reject that premise; they treat many valuable uses as discoveries that appear after the thing exists. The left’s tradition treats unplanned exuberance as a category error.

A machine built to do something astonishing, by a private firm, before its practical uses are fully enumerated, violates the requirement that technology be instrumental, collective, sober and pre-justified. The joyless outrage is entirely political.

text:
I analysed all the responses from this post and from the original BFBS Forces news post.  This is what the people say!  

BRITISH FAMILIES MUST SACRIFICE MORE FOR DEFENCE — BUT WHY ARE THEY ALWAYS FIRST IN LINE TO PAY?

The head of the British Army warns that Britain must prepare for sacrifices, while Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch declares that she would begin by cutting welfare spending to put more money into defence.

And judging by the furious public reaction, the political establishment has a much bigger problem than military preparedness.

It has lost the trust of many of the very people it expects to defend the country.

The comments beneath the Forces News report are overwhelmingly hostile. The language is frequently crude, but the underlying objections deserve serious consideration.

People are asking why they should be expected to fight and potentially die in foreign conflicts while they believe successive governments have failed to secure Britain's borders, protect their communities and put British interests first.

Others point to the financial sacrifices families are already making through rising household bills and the cost of everyday essentials.

Then along comes Kemi Badenoch with her solution: cut welfare spending.

But whose welfare, Mrs Badenoch?

The disabled? The chronically ill? Pensioners? Low-income working families? Or those genuinely unable to support themselves?

Before proposing cuts that could affect vulnerable British citizens, perhaps she should explain why the political establishment has tolerated billions in annual asylum expenditure and failed to implement immigration reforms that could substantially reduce the burden on taxpayers.

The figures deserve examination.

In 2024–25, the Home Office spent approximately £4 billion supporting asylum seekers, including £2.1 billion on hotel accommodation alone.

Meanwhile, Britain's defence expenditure is projected at £71 billion for 2026–27.

No serious person should pretend that abolishing asylum expenditure would automatically fund the entire Armed Forces. Nor can the costs of immigration enforcement and deportations simply be ignored.

But billions of pounds are being spent in areas where substantial savings could be pursued. Even the Government has identified scope to reduce asylum costs by at least £1 billion annually.

Why, then, is cutting welfare the first answer Badenoch offers when asked how Britain should fund its defence?

Restore Britain has already published proposals to reverse mass immigration, deport illegal migrants, overhaul access to benefits for foreign nationals, replace costly asylum hotels and put British national interests at the centre of government policy.

Its published plans also target the longer-term fiscal pressures associated with immigration, including future eligibility for welfare and demands on taxpayer-funded services.

If implemented effectively, such reforms could release substantial resources over time, some of which could be directed towards rebuilding Britain's military.

The precise net savings must be established after accounting for enforcement costs, implementation, lost tax revenue and other economic effects. But that is an argument for proper costing, not for refusing to examine the potential.

The important political distinction is that Restore Britain's approach seeks savings from changing immigration and asylum policy before demanding further sacrifices from vulnerable British households.

That is a fundamentally different starting point from announcing welfare cuts without identifying who will lose support.

And this controversy is about much more than money.

The public response suggests a profound crisis of confidence in Britain's political leadership.

For years, politicians have made decisions concerning immigration, national security, foreign intervention and international obligations while large sections of the population have felt increasingly ignored.

Now those same institutions are warning that ordinary Britons must be prepared to make further sacrifices, potentially including the lives of their sons and daughters.

Sacrifices for whom? For what? And decided by whom?

Britain must have strong, properly funded and capable Armed Forces. Our soldiers deserve respect, modern equipment, competent leadership and the resources necessary to defend the country.

Restore Britain explicitly supports rebuilding and rearming our military.

But there is a fundamental difference between defending Britain and automatically supporting every overseas conflict or international military commitment that politicians consider strategically desirable.

Military alliances can serve Britain's interests. Foreign deployments may sometimes be necessary. But each commitment must be justified by its contribution to British national security, not simply by appeals to international obligation or political credibility.

It is entirely reasonable for the public to question why its sons and daughters should be put in danger, particularly when the necessity and objectives of a potential war have not been clearly explained.

Nor should politicians dismiss public resistance as a lack of patriotism.

Patriotism is not unquestioning obedience to government. It is loyalty to one's country and a determination that its people, security and future should come first.

If political leaders want public support for greater defence expenditure, they must first demonstrate that existing public money is being spent responsibly.

They must explain why savings cannot be made through immigration reform, asylum reform, reducing unnecessary expenditure and reassessing foreign commitments before support for British citizens is placed on the chopping block.

And if they want the British people to contemplate war, they must be equally clear about the threat, the national interest, the alternatives and the potential human cost.

The establishment cannot continually ask ordinary families to pay more, endure more and risk more while failing to address their concerns about what is happening in their own country.

General Walker is right that Britain needs a frank national conversation.

But that conversation must include uncomfortable questions about the political decisions that have brought Britain to this point.

A strong nation needs a strong military. It also needs secure borders, sustainable public finances, public trust and a government that understands whom it serves.

Before asking British families to sacrifice still more, the political establishment should demonstrate that it is prepared to change its own priorities.

Defend Britain. Rebuild Britain. Put British interests first.

text:
🏇🏇🏇
The HORSES that changed history known as Tianma, Fergana, Akhal-Teke, Heavenly Horses or Turkmen Horse

The war fought for these horses stands as one of the greatest military logistics operations in Chinese history.

The cause of war: The Great Xiongnu (Hun) Threat
In the 2nd century BC, the Han Dynasty of China (under Emperor Wu) was struggling against the Xiongnu (Hun) raids, who possessed master riding skills. China’s local horses were short, so they could not compete with the fast horse riders of the stepps. Chinese diplomat Zhang Qian, during his exploratory mission to the Western Regions, discovered a magnificent horse breed in the Fergana Valley (Dayuan Kingdom), a region stretching across modern Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan. These horses were the direct ancestors of today's Akhal-Teke horses.

Why Heavenly Horses and Sweating Blood?
Mesmerized upon seeing them, the Chinese named these creatures Tianma (Heavenly or Celestial Horses) for two major reasons:
1. Sweating blood: Ancient Chinese records noted that these horses appeared to bleed from their skins when running. Modern science reveals this was caused by a microscopic parasite unique to local rivers, which lived just beneath the thin skin and caused minor bleeding when mixed with sweat. However, the Chinese interpreted this as a sign of divine power and nobility.
2. Mystical belief: Emperor Wu believed these horses would not only defeat the Huns but also served as divine entities destined to carry him to the Land of the Immortals

The priceless horses and the outbreak of war
Emperor Wu sent an embassy with gold and a massive golden horse statue to the King of Fergana to purchase breeding stock. Knowing the strategic military value of his horses, the King rejected the offer. To make matters worse, Chinese envoys were ambushed and looted on their return journey. Infuriated, the Emperor sent an army under General Li Guangli to invade Fergana in 104 BC.

Crossing the deserts and the siege
- The first campaign (104 BC): The Chinese army was decimated by hunger and thirst while crossing the brutal Taklamakan Desert. Reaching Fergana exhausted, they were easily defeated by local forces and forced to retreat.
- The second campaign (102 BC): Emperor Wu refused to yield. He launched one of the largest logistical operations in ancient history, mobilizing 60,000 to 100,000 soldiers along with thousands of camels and supply trains. The Chinese army successfully besieged the capital of Fergana and cut off its water supply.

The legacy: Birth of the Silk Road 
Fearing total destroyed, Fergana nobility assassinated their own king and made a deal with China. Approximately 3,000 Celestial Horses, including top breeding stallions, were handed over. With these horses, China gained absolute military supremacy against the Huns. More importantly, this military campaign deeply extended Chinese influence into Central Asia, securing the trade routes and officially birthing the historic Silk Road.

The breed alive today: The Turkmen heritage
This legendary lineage did not vanish into history. The Turkmen nomadic culture preserved these horses with religious devotion, keeping the bloodline pure for over to millennia. Today, the legendary Heavenly Horses that China marched armies across deserts to capture are officially known as the Akhal-Teke, the national pride and living treasure of Turkmenistan.
Sources: Sartupaev and S. Kudabaev – The Heritage of Akhal-Teke Horses and Central Asian History, Records of the Grand Historian by Sima Qian

text:
ZELENSKYY WAS ASKED WHO HIS HERO IS. HIS ANSWER SAYS EVERYTHING. 🇺🇦❤️

For nearly five years, Volodymyr Zelenskyy has lived with the responsibilities of leading a country at war. But in a deeply personal exchange with Reuters, the Ukrainian president revealed what he misses most about the life he left behind.

Asked whether he missed being an actor, Zelenskyy replied:

“I miss being a good father.”

The conversation then turned to his children.

When they were younger, what did he tell them?

“I love you.”

And now that they are older?

“I miss you.”

Three words that capture the personal cost of a presidency consumed by war. Behind the speeches, negotiations and constant demands of leadership is a father who misses spending time with his children.

Then came a question about heroism.

“Are you a hero?”

“No.”

When asked whom he considers his heroes, Zelenskyy answered:

“My children, our army, and the Ukrainian people. I am part of our nation. I think our nation is absolutely heroic.”

He was given the opportunity to describe himself as a hero. Instead, he spoke about his family, the soldiers defending Ukraine and the people enduring the war.

For all the attention surrounding Zelenskyy as a wartime president, this exchange offered a much more personal glimpse of the man behind the office.

And perhaps the most moving words were not about courage or leadership at all.

“I miss you.”

text:
One question that gets asked more and more frequently is why France seems to do comparatively so much better than the UK with its defence forces. There is not one single, simple answer. France does not do better under every aspect, to start with. But the one macroscopic problem I will always come back to is that the UK does NOT do strategic planning of military capability. 
The UK NEVER has an agreed, long term vision. The UK by design does NOT give its Parliament a real understanding and control of Defence aims and means. 
Every successive government that comes and goes does its own thing; obfuscates its plans at leisure, and leaves the following one to do the same. 

Other countries are less prone to shock program cancellations and sudden erasure of entire capabilities. If other Countries, France being just one example, agree on the strategic rationale of one capability, they will indicatively stick to it. 

The UK will not. The UK holds absolutely nothing sacred (in terms of actual capability). I often hear cries about "sacred cows", but the UK does NOT have sacred cows. Not in terms of actual military capability. 
It has cosmetic obsessions such as the supremacy of the "Foot Regiment" that will bend the entire Army out of shape to hang on to this or that tiny, near-insignificant infantry battalion even at the cost of the Supports for fielding an actual brigade. 
It has the Red Arrows and a few other trinkets. 

Actual capabilities? No. It will happily gap or delete maritime patrol aircraft and AEW (utterly demented things to do from a strategic point of view). It will happily have its army down to 14 self propelled howitzers in total for years. 
It has happily given up IFVs altogether. 
It has dismantled the Navy. 

None of the UK "strategic" papers are ever worth the time they take to be read. 
They are only ever lists of the Dead, the Wounded, the Missing. Whatever makes it into the fancy and funding of the day carries on. 
What does not dies. What is in the middle lives on for years as a cat in a box, and no one is sure whether it is alive or dead. 

Defence in the UK starts getting less demented only when actual Parliamentary scrutiny of Defence is implemented. Something like the rolling Military Planning Law in France, so both sides of Parliament know what the fuck they are doing and have to vote on plans. So there is some actual continuity in planning and execution. So no side of the House gets to make empty statements without attaching an overt vote to a plan. 

UK Defence can never get healthier until the Defence Committee is a toothless body meant to be told lies and to hear about things months to years after they have happened. 
Commissions must discuss and approve plans BEFOREHAND, not offer commentary when it is too late. 

The entire handling of Defence in the UK is designed from the root up to ENSURE failure.
