You see a beautiful dog in a harness at the store and every part of you wants to say hello. For the person holding that leash, the kindest thing you can do is let the dog keep working.

Guide Dogs for the Blind puts it simply: please do not pet or talk to a guide dog, do not offer food or treats, and do not touch or steer the harness. It is fine to ask the person if you may meet their guide, and many handlers enjoy introducing their dogs when the time is right. Ask before offering a toy too, since guide dogs are only allowed to play with specific toys for their health and safety.

Guiding Eyes for the Blind explains why. While in harness, a guide dog is constantly navigating around obstacles, indicating curbs and stairs, and looking to its handler for direction. Even a momentary distraction could cause a person who is blind to run into a pole or miss a turn. That includes eye contact and giving the dog commands, because the dog should look only to its handler.

CNIB, the Canadian organization for people who are blind, puts it this way: harness on means hands off. Keep your own dog leashed and away from a working team. Never grab the leash or harness or try to steer the handler. If you want to help, ask first and speak directly to the person, not the dog, and give specific directions, because "over there" does not help.

Guide Dogs for the Blind also asks people not to call out directions, block a team's path, or honk a car horn to signal when it is safe to cross. The team is trained to travel safely on its own, and even well meant noise can be distracting, confusing and dangerous. If you see someone distracting a guide dog, CNIB suggests a polite reminder.

That same courtesy is a good habit around any working service dog team, including our own Odin and his handler Ski. Give the team space, talk to the person, and let the dog do its job.

Watch Dogs of Service from Iowa PBS on YouTube

text:
The State Grocery Store.

New York’s mayor, Zohran Mamdani, is opening city-owned grocery stores. Five of them, the first one next year. The city will cover the rent and the construction, and a basket of staples will be sold about 30% below market. A "public option," he calls it, for where the market has failed.

It sounds kind. Poland had these stores for over forty years. See the picture below. Let me tell you how it ends.

1. Every Pole knew the joke. A man walks into a shop: "No meat?" The clerk: "No, sir. Here is no fish. No meat is across the street."

2. A store that cannot go bankrupt has no reason to stock what you want. A private grocer who guesses wrong goes broke. A state store that guesses wrong gets a bigger budget. So the shelves follow the plan, not the customer.

3. A price below cost is not a gift. It is a queue. When staples sell for less than they cost, demand runs ahead of supply, and the shelf is empty by ten in the morning. A local shop owner has already predicted it: a handful of stores for eight million people will be jam-packed.

4. The city promises not to compete with local shops – discounts only on the basics. That is how it always begins. In 1947, Poland’s communists launched what they called the "battle for trade." Taxes, inspections and price rules squeezed the private shops one by one, until the state store was the only store left.

5. Scarcity creates a new kind of power: access. The clerk keeps the good meat under the counter for friends. The party elite had their own shops – Poles called them the shops behind the yellow curtains. The store built for equality produced the most unequal access of all.

6. And look at why food is expensive in New York in the first place: rents, rules, taxes, and shops closing because theft goes unpunished. The city that makes groceries expensive now offers to sell them to you itself – typical socialism: fighting the problems you create first.

7. You don’t need to read Hayek to understand this. You only need to have stood in a Polish queue at dawn, with a ration card in your pocket.

Nobody voted for the queues and the vinegar (the only thing that was often left in the shops – because you can’t consume that much of it without anything else). They voted for the promise, but they still got what necessarily follows.

And in every socialist city, the shop that has no meat is always just across the street.

text:
Holyrood: The Rise and Stall of so-called "Progressive Nationalism"
In the Scottish Parliament, the process took a different path but arrived at a strikingly similar destination. 

For years, the SNP successfully campaigned to the left of Westminster Labour, presenting Scotland as a naturally social-democratic nation opposed to Tory austerity. However, left-wing critics argue that Holyrood's leadership was equally captured by a technocratic elite.

The "Sticking Plaster" Strategy:
Corporate Courtship and Deregulation: Behind the progressive rhetoric, successive Holyrood administrations since 2015 in particular heavily courted multinational corporations. 

The outsourcing of Scotland's massive green energy potential, notably through the ScotWind leasing round, saw vast swathes of offshore wind rights sold off to private fossil fuel giants rather than being retained under a state-owned, public energy company.

Suppression of Radical Reform: Long-promised systemic changes, such as replacing the regressive Council Tax or enacting radical land reform to challenge Scotland’s highly concentrated private land ownership, were repeatedly delayed, watered down, or shelved by a leadership class wary of alienating business interests.

The Double Political Lock
The result across both nations is a profound sense of political disillusionment. Voters in Scotland and England are presented with two distinct parliaments, yet the core macroeconomic choices on offer remain tightly constrained by neoliberal boundaries. 

Just as in France, when the democratic channels within Westminster and Holyrood are seen as captured by a single managerial class, it inevitably pushes political expression out of the ballot box and into strikes and protests.

text:
Westminster: The Purge and the Professional Class
In the UK Parliament, the capture of the Labour Party is often viewed by traditional socialists as a multi-decade project to insulate the party from radical economic policy.

The Managerial Takeover: The parliamentary party shifted decisively away from trade unionists, miners, and working-class organisers toward a professional political class consisting of former corporate lawyers, think-tank directors, and public relations advisors.

Systemic De-selection and Purging: Whenever the traditional left re-emerged within the party apparatus, the institutional machinery responded with aggressive internal policing. Critics point to the systematic marginalisation, suspension, and de-selection of left-wing candidates and MPs to ensure the parliamentary intake remained strictly aligned with market-friendly orthodoxy.

The Economic Consensus: The structural result is a Westminster dynamic where both the government and the official opposition operate within a narrow economic framework that prioritises fiscal discipline, light-touch corporate regulation, and private-sector partnerships over structural wealth redistribution.

text:
the working-class left did not just give up; its institutional machinery the parties, the think tanks, and the policy rooms were systematically captured by a new class of professional, technocratic elites who actively purged radical elements.

This "hostile takeover" played out across the West through several highly strategic moves:

1. The Marginalisation of Organized Labour
For a century, the power of left-wing parties came directly from trade unions. The takeover required deliberately severing or weakening this umbilical cord.

In the UK, New Labour architects explicitly sought to reduce the voting power and financial influence of unions within party conferences to project a "business-friendly" image.

In France, the Socialists under Hollande increasingly ignored the demands of major unions like the CGT, passing the El Khomri labor laws via emergency constitutional decrees (Article 49.3) to completely bypass parliamentary and union opposition.

The Rise of the Professional Managerial Class
The leadership of left-wing parties shifted away from trade unionists, industrial workers, and community organisers. Instead, it was occupied by what sociologists call the Professional-Managerial Class (PMC)—lawyers, investment bankers, PR consultants, and career politicians who held degrees from elite universities. 

For this new leadership class, politics was not about class struggle; it was about "managing" the state efficiently. 

Emmanuel Macron’s rapid rise from a Rothschild investment banker to Hollande’s economic advisor, and finally to the presidency, is the textbook definition of this takeover.

The Institutional Purge of Left-Wing Intellectuals
To solidify control, the new centrist leadership systematically pushed out, marginalised, or de-selected politicians and thinkers who refused to accept free-market orthodoxy.

In the UK, this manifested as a decades-long internal civil war against the Bennite left, which temporarily broke out into the open during the Jeremy Corbyn era and was subsequently crushed and purged by the party apparatus.

In France, it led to the total fracturing of the Socialist Party, as left-wing factions (the frondeurs) tried and failed to stop Hollande's rightward shift, eventually forcing figures like Jean-Luc Mélenchon to leave the party entirely to build an external movement from scratch.

The Systemic Trajectory
The tragedy of this takeover, as traditional leftists argue, is that it effectively locked the working class out of the democratic process.

By capturing the only mainstream parties that were supposed to represent labor against capital, the technocratic elite created a closed loop where both major parties agreed on the most important thing: the inviolability of the free market.

This brings the conversation right back to the streets of Paris today. The intense anger and readiness to clash with police seen in the videos isn't just about high inflation or broken school buildings. It is the direct result of a public that feels the traditional democratic channels were stolen from them decades ago, leaving the street as the only place where their actual voices can be heard.

text:
14) ~David Liu, PhD~

• David Liu, a chemical biologist at the Broad Institute & Harvard University, & colleagues have developed a new type of CRISPR-Cas9-based tool

• It retains the ability to home in on a precise location in the genome, but instead of cutting the double helix, it brings to the target site an enzyme that converts a DNA base into a different one

• Many life-threatening diseases are caused by a change in a single nucleotide base in an individual’s DNA

• To fix such point mutations using the traditional CRISPR-Cas9 approach, scientists deliver the Cas9-guide RNA complex to cells along with a separate repair template that has the corrected sequence

• The Cas9 nuclease cuts the DNA, stimulating cellular repair mechanisms to install the template sequence

• But this process, called homology-directed repair (HDR), is usually inefficient & not as clean as one would want; for example, random insertions, deletions, or translocations are common at cut sites

• The new tool Liu has developed, called a base editor, uses a different approach

• Liu stresses that base editors aren’t better at gene editing than CRISPR-Cas9

• They're just a different tool that offer advantages when the goal is to install or correct a point mutation

• So how was the base editor developed?

• The first step was to cripple Cas9 so that it would not cut double-stranded DNA, but would still unzip the helix at the target location

• That was the easy part, as researchers had previously disabled the DNA-cutting activity of Cas9

• Using the crippled enzyme, Liu & colleagues created a Cas9-guide RNA complex & tethered to it an enzyme called cytidine deaminase, which converts a cytosine (C) to a thymine (T) through a series of chemical reactions

• That T is now paired with the wrong base on the opposite strand—a guanine (G) instead of an adenine (A)

• The crippled Cas9 still has the ability to nick the opposite strand at the site of the now mismatched bases

• As a result of the nick, the cell’s repair mechanism goes into action to “fix” the error—& converts the G to an A, so that it can pair with the new T

• In the end, a C-G base pair is changed to a T-A without making any other changes to the DNA

• Liu likens the use of base editors to “chemical surgery” directly on a target site in a cell’s genome

• The scientific community raced to take advantage of this new technology as soon as it was published

• “We reported our first base editor in mid-2016, & already there have been several dozen papers published from laboratories from around the world that have used it to edit bacteria, yeast, rice, corn, wheat, tomatoes, zebrafish, mice, frogs & even human embryos,” says Liu

• But Liu did not stop there

• The most common point mutations associated with human diseases have an A-T base pair where there should be a G-C base pair

• Unfortunately, there was no known enzyme able to convert A to G in DNA

• Liu’s team was able to create a new enzyme by painstakingly tweaking an enzyme in the bacteria Escherichia coli (e-coli)

• When the team put the new enzyme into their base editor, it became “a very efficient & clean machine to transform A-T base pairs into G-C base pairs in living cells,” says Liu

• When doing a side-by-side comparison between Cas9’s molecular scissors & the base editors, which are more like pencils that directly change one base to a different base, Liu says that base editors work much more efficiently & cleanly, producing far fewer undesired products

text:
I have so much respect for business owners like Hilda Baci. I remember a couple years back I bought coconut rice and fried chicken from her restaurant in lekki. 

Unfortunately I couldn’t eat it because it was so peppery and I absolutely hate spicy food. I was hungry and very disappointed that I wasted my money on it so I impulsively texted her on Instagram, sent her pictures of the food with my complaint about it being too spicy. 

I wasn’t even expecting her to see it or even respond 😅
Surprisingly, a couple hours later she saw my message, read it, apologized and offered me a replacement meal with zero strings attached.
That incident made me respect her even more 👏🙏

text:
30-SECOND PHOTOREAL FANTASY ACTION COMEDY. 9:16.
THE LAST FISH
Seven connected shots with intentional cuts. No dialogue or music.

REFERENCES
Image 1 defines the orange cat warrior: fur markings, face, scar, ear notch, armor and green scarf.
Image 2 defines the slim CRT traveler: television head, single antenna, petrol coat, clothing and boots.
Reference the characters only. Each sheet shows several views of ONE character. Exclude the studio backgrounds and panel arrangements.

CHARACTERS AND CONTINUITY
Exactly two characters.
The armored orange cat stands upright and reaches the traveler's knee.
The CRT traveler is tall and slender, with narrow shoulders, long limbs and a compact ivory television head. His convex screen stays pale blue-grey, without a face or symbols.
Each carries one sword in a scabbard at the left hip.
CRT carries one cream cloth bundle containing one cooked fish.

LOCATION AND OPENING
One straight weathered stone bridge leading to a distant castle gate. Low stone parapets and one flat-topped square stone pier beside the action. Dry paving, warm late-afternoon sunlight, quiet valley below.
CRT walks toward the gate, carrying the bundle in his LEFT hand.
Cat blocks his path, staring at the bundle. Keep their position relative to the gate consistent throughout the duel.

SHOT 1 [00:00–00:04]
Frontal full two-shot, gate behind CRT.
Cat draws his short sword with his RIGHT paw and plants his feet.
CRT stops, tilts his head, then draws his sword with his RIGHT hand. His left hand keeps the bundle behind his hip.
Wind, small armor rattles and blades leaving scabbards.

SHOT 2 [00:04–00:09]
Cut to a low side full two-shot.
Cat advances with two quick, clearly separated slashes.
CRT retreats two short steps, blocking each strike with his right-hand sword. Blades meet visibly, then separate.
Keep both bodies and their feet readable.
Two sharp metal contacts, boots scraping stone.

SHOT 3 [00:09–00:14]
Cut closer from the same side of the action axis.
Cat ducks beneath CRT's blade and makes one upward strike.
CRT blocks, recoils and bumps his LEFT hand against the square stone pier.
The bundle drops onto its flat top. Its loose cloth unfolds, exposing one grilled fish.
Both freeze mid-confrontation, then lower their blades.
Cloth lands softly. The fighting sounds stop.

SHOT 4 [00:14–00:18]
Cut to a low close two-shot beside the pier, fish visible between them.
Cat stares at the fish. His ears lift.
CRT looks from the fish to the cat, then slowly tilts his head.
One awkward pause.
Cat gives one small, demanding meow.
Neither attacks.

SHOT 5 [00:18–00:23]
Cut to a medium two-shot.
Their swords are now visibly secured in their original scabbards.
CRT breaks the cooked fish into two portions with his gloved hands over the open cloth.
He offers the larger portion.
Cat accepts with both paws, suddenly polite.
Soft cloth movement and a small armor creak.

SHOT 6 [00:23–00:27]
Cut to a low frontal two-shot.
They sit shoulder-to-leg on a low stone ledge beside the pier.
Cat holds the larger fish portion and leans comfortably against CRT's leg.
CRT looks down. Cat answers with a slow blink.
Hold their relaxed familiarity. This was an argument over lunch between old companions.

SHOT 7 [00:27–00:30]
Cut to a rear wide view along the bridge.
Both walk together toward the castle gate, swords sheathed.
Cat carries his fish with both paws.
CRT carries the smaller portion in the folded cloth in his LEFT hand.
Cat takes quick little steps beside CRT's long stride.
End while they are still walking. No fade or black frame.

CAMERA AND LOOK
Panavision 35mm film aesthetic, photographic fantasy, subtle grain, warm highlights and natural cool shadows.
Vertical compositions keep the small cat and tall traveler visible together.
Stable framing for blade contacts. Brief lateral tracking during Shot 2. No orbit or slow motion.
Detailed fur, scratched armor, worn coat fabric and aged stone. Believable balance and contact.

PERFORMANCE AND SOUND
Play the duel seriously, with no exaggerated facial comedy.
CRT reacts through posture and television-head angles.
Cat changes from fierce determination to quiet satisfaction.
Native synchronized sound: valley wind, birds, footsteps, armor, sword contact, cloth and one meow. No speech, narration or music.

AVOID
Extra characters, bulky CRT body, extra antennas, human face inside the screen, identity changes, extra limbs, swapped hands, duplicate props, blood, injury, changing bridge geometry, glowing effects, text, subtitles and logos.

text:
AI INFRASTRUCTURE — $NBIS vs $IREN vs $CIFR
BULL VS BEAR | EMMANUELINVEST — PART 1
AI DEMAND IS BOOMING. BUT WHO ACTUALLY MAKES MONEY FOR SHAREHOLDERS?
The AI infrastructure trade is entering a more demanding phase.
For much of the buildout, investors rewarded companies securing power, building data centres and announcing multibillion-dollar contracts.
But the recent sell-off has exposed a more difficult question.
How much of that growth will actually translate into cash flow and returns for shareholders?
Three companies illustrate the challenge:
▪ $NBIS — Nebius: Full-stack AI cloud
▪ $IREN — IREN: Power-connected infrastructure and GPU cloud
▪ $CIFR — Cipher: Contracted data-centre infrastructure
All three are exposed to the same AI buildout.
But their business models, financing requirements and paths to profitability are different.
And I don't think investors should value them in the same way.
NEBIUS $NBIS — THE AI CLOUD GROWTH BET
Nebius is building a full-stack AI cloud platform, combining GPU infrastructure with software and services for AI developers and enterprises.
Its growth has been extraordinary.
Q2 2026 — THE NUMBERS
▪ Group revenue: $582.3M (+454% YoY)
▪ AI cloud revenue: $574.9M (+514% YoY)
▪ AI cloud adjusted EBITDA: $285.7M
▪ AI cloud adjusted EBITDA margin: 49.7%
▪ Net loss from continuing operations: $190.4M
▪ Purchases of PPE and intangible assets: approximately $5.66B
▪ AI cloud annualised revenue run-rate: $3B
What stands out to me is the difference between operating performance and the cost of expansion.
Nebius is generating strong adjusted EBITDA from its AI cloud operations, but Q2 depreciation and amortisation reached approximately $259.7M.
And infrastructure spending remains enormous.
The company has also reported more than $40B in customer commitments, with over $9B in customer prepayments expected during 2026.
Those commitments improve demand visibility and help finance expansion.
But commitments, prepayments and annualised run-rate revenue are not the same as recognised revenue or free cash flow.
Then there's the Meta agreement.
Nebius announced a five-year AI infrastructure agreement worth up to approximately $27B.
▪ $12B in dedicated AI capacity, with delivery beginning in early 2027.
▪ Up to $15B in additional compute capacity, which Nebius intends to offer to third-party customers first, with Meta committed to purchasing remaining available capacity under the agreement.
The infrastructure will use NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform.
It's a major commercial opportunity, but the full $27B is a potential contract value, not revenue already earned.
🟢 THE BULL CASE
Nebius could become a major independent AI cloud platform.
Rapid revenue growth, strong customer demand and expanding GPU capacity provide a foundation for sustained growth.
Its software capabilities could also help differentiate the platform beyond simply renting computing power.
If utilisation remains strong as capacity scales, operating leverage could become increasingly attractive.
Customer commitments and prepayments provide greater visibility and support the financing of future infrastructure.
🔴 THE BEAR CASE
The business remains extremely capital-intensive.
GPU depreciation, construction costs, financing requirements and potential dilution could absorb much of the economic value created by revenue growth.
Even with strong adjusted EBITDA margins, the company must continue investing heavily to expand and eventually replace computing infrastructure.
Large contracts also introduce delivery obligations.
MY VIEW
I'm bullish on Nebius's long-term opportunity.
But the investment case shouldn't rest simply on extraordinary revenue growth or the size of its customer commitments.
The real test is whether Nebius can turn that demand into sustainable free cash flow and attractive returns on invested capital.
IREN $IREN — THE POWER-TO-COMPUTE BET
IREN has evolved from Bitcoin mining into a vertically integrated AI cloud infrastructure business.
Its advantage is access to power-connected data centres, combined with an expanding GPU cloud platform.
Its August 2026 results illustrate both the scale of the opportunity and how much execution still lies ahead.
THE NUMBERS
▪ Contracted annualised run-rate revenue for 2026 capacity: approximately $4B
▪ Operating annualised run-rate revenue as of August 26: approximately $1B
▪ FY26 recognised revenue: $707M
▪ FY26 AI Cloud revenue: $128.8M
▪ FY26 adjusted EBITDA: $245.7M
▪ New GPU financing: approximately $2.8B
▪ Recent customer prepayments: 45–55% of associated GPU capital expenditure
The most important distinction is between contracted demand and revenue already recognised.
IREN has secured substantial AI compute commitments, but much of the opportunity still depends on bringing capacity online.
Its $4B contracted annualised run-rate figure is not $4B of recognised annual revenue.
The company's FY26 AI Cloud revenue of $128.8M shows how early the transition remains relative to its contracted opportunity.
Customer prepayments and GPU financing help reduce the immediate funding burden.
But financing isn't free capital, and the company still needs to deliver the infrastructure.
🟢 THE BULL CASE
Power access is becoming increasingly valuable as AI infrastructure expands.
IREN has spent years developing power-connected sites that could support substantial AI compute demand.
Its growing customer base and contracted capacity provide a pathway to rapid revenue expansion.
Customer prepayments and GPU-backed financing also help fund deployments.
If capacity is commissioned successfully and utilisation remains strong, the business could scale quickly.
🔴 THE BEAR CASE
The transition from Bitcoin mining to AI cloud requires substantial investment and execution.
Capacity must be commissioned, GPUs installed and customer requirements satisfied before contracted demand fully converts into revenue.
Hardware depreciation, financing obligations, customer concentration and potential dilution remain important risks.
And as the GPU fleet expands, investors need to consider the ongoing cost of maintaining and replacing that infrastructure.
MY VIEW
I like IREN's combination of power access, commercial momentum and customer-supported financing.
But the investment case ultimately depends on converting contracted capacity into profitable revenue and sustainable cash generation.
The next phase isn't about announcing bigger contracts. It's about delivering capacity and proving the economics.
CIPHER $CIFR — THE CONTRACTED INFRASTRUCTURE BET
Cipher is taking a different approach to the AI buildout.
Rather than primarily selling GPU cloud services, its strategy increasingly focuses on developing and leasing large-scale data-centre infrastructure.
That distinction matters.
Long-term leases can provide greater revenue visibility without the same direct exposure to GPU replacement cycles faced by AI cloud operators.
But the economics depend heavily on construction execution and financing.
THE NUMBERS — SEPTEMBER 30, 2026
▪ Contracted HPC capacity: 700 MW
▪ Contracted revenue: $16.6B
▪ Weighted average lease term: 17.3 years
▪ Average annualised NOI: $843M
These are contracted portfolio measures, not revenue and cash flow already realised.
Cipher also extended its Barber Lake lease arrangement to 20 years, increasing contracted revenue at the facility to over $9B.
That strengthens long-term revenue visibility.
But the facilities still need to be completed and delivered.
And the financing deserves attention.
On October 16, Cipher issued $850M of 0% convertible senior notes due 2032, with an initial conversion price of approximately $15.31 per share.
It also completed an exchange of approximately $165.9M of existing convertible debt for 40.7 million shares.
Cipher spent approximately $89.7M on capped-call transactions designed to reduce potential dilution from the new notes, subject to a cap.
Zero coupon doesn't mean zero economic cost.
The debt exchange has already resulted in additional shares, while the new convertible notes introduce further potential dilution.
🟢 THE BULL CASE
Cipher's long-duration leases provide substantial visibility into future contracted revenue.
Its infrastructure-focused approach reduces direct exposure to GPU pricing, utilisation and replacement cycles compared with companies operating their own AI cloud platforms.
If construction stays on schedule and costs remain controlled, long-term rental income could generate attractive infrastructure returns.
The value of large-scale, power-connected data-centre capacity could also increase as AI demand expands.
🔴 THE BEAR CASE
Data centres require substantial capital before rental income begins.
Construction delays, cost overruns, financing obligations and dilution could weaken shareholder returns.
The recent debt-for-equity exchange illustrates how financing decisions can affect existing shareholders even when infrastructure demand remains strong.
And $16.6B of contracted revenue doesn't mean $16.6B of revenue already earned.
MY VIEW
I like the visibility provided by Cipher's long-term lease portfolio.
But I wouldn't judge the investment simply by the headline size of its contracts.
The real test is whether those leases generate attractive returns after construction, financing and dilution — and how much value ultimately reaches shareholders.
THREE COMPANIES. THREE DIFFERENT ECONOMIC MODELS.
This is where I think investors need to become more selective.
$NBIS — THE AI CLOUD PLATFORM
Can rapid revenue growth, GPU utilisation and software capabilities translate into sustainable free cash flow?
$IREN — POWER + GPU CLOUD
Can contracted compute demand become profitable operating cash flow as new capacity comes online?
$CIFR — CONTRACTED INFRASTRUCTURE
Can long-term data-centre leases generate attractive returns after construction, financing and dilution?
Nebius is betting on the economics of operating a full-stack AI cloud.
IREN is combining power access with GPU cloud capacity.
Cipher is increasingly focused on the economics of developing infrastructure that others use.
The question isn't simply which company grows fastest.
It's which business model generates the strongest returns relative to the capital and risks involved.
That's why investors need to distinguish between:
▪ Contract value and recognised revenue
▪ Run-rate targets and actual sales
▪ Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow
▪ Planned capacity and operational capacity
▪ Enterprise growth and value created per share
THE BIGGER BULL VS BEAR DEBATE
🟢 THE BULL CASE
AI demand continues to expand.
Power, compute and specialised data-centre capacity remain strategically important.
Companies that deliver reliable infrastructure at scale could benefit from long-term customer relationships, stronger utilisation and operating leverage.
The strongest operators may emerge with durable competitive advantages.
🔴 THE BEAR CASE
The infrastructure is expensive.
GPUs depreciate.
Construction takes time.
Debt creates fixed obligations.
Equity issuance can dilute existing shareholders.
And large contracts don't eliminate execution risk.
Even if these companies meet their growth targets, investors can still lose money if valuations already assume exceptional future returns.
That's why valuation cannot be separated from the growth story.
MY TAKEAWAY
I remain bullish on long-term AI infrastructure demand.
But I'm becoming more selective about the businesses delivering that capacity and how they're financed.
$NBIS offers rapid AI cloud growth, software capabilities and platform potential.
$IREN combines power access, contracted compute demand and customer-supported financing.
$CIFR offers exposure to long-duration data-centre infrastructure leases.
Each has a credible opportunity.
But none is automatically undervalued simply because its share price has fallen.
For me, the next phase of the AI trade comes down to five things:
Utilisation. Margins. Financing discipline. Free cash flow. Returns on invested capital.
The companies that build the most AI infrastructure won't necessarily create the most shareholder value.
I'd rather own an AI infrastructure business that converts demand into sustainable returns per share than chase one simply because its backlog and capital expenditure keep getting bigger.
AI demand is not the problem. The price of building that capacity — and the returns shareholders ultimately receive — are what matter now.
— EMMANUELINVEST

text:
What we consume in the media shapes our culture.

Our culture shapes our values, our ambitions, our morals, and ultimately, the kind of society we become.

This is why I think Nigeria needs a different kind of reality TV show.

Let me explain.

Shows like BBNaija and Love Island are incredibly entertaining. They attract millions of viewers, dominate conversations, influence trends, and command the attention of young people.

I’m not against entertainment. Far from it.

But I keep asking myself one question:

What if we could channel even a fraction of that attention into building things?

What if we created a reality show where young Nigerians don’t just compete for fame, but compete to build real businesses, solve real problems, and create products that people can actually use?

Imagine a house filled with young, ambitious builders.

Some come with ideas. Some are developers. Some understand design, marketing, business, or technology. They are brought together with one mission: turn ideas into real products.

And the entire journey is broadcast.

We watch them identify problems, validate ideas, interview potential customers, disagree on product decisions, build prototypes, develop MVPs, test assumptions, fail, learn, iterate, and eventually launch to the public.

We watch real people go from zero to one.

Imagine the audience learning alongside them. Imagine a young person in Ilorin, Kano, Aba, or a village somewhere in Nigeria watching the show and realising that they, too, can build something meaningful with the resources available to them.

Imagine watching a founder struggle to find product-market fit, then finally figure it out. Imagine experienced founders, business leaders, investors, and industry experts visiting the house to mentor the contestants, challenge their assumptions, and share lessons from their own journeys.

The audience wouldn’t just be entertained. They would be learning how to think, build, solve problems, and create value.

And here’s another interesting part.

The products built on the show wouldn’t just end when the cameras stop rolling. They would go to market. They would have real customers, real users, and a chance to become sustainable businesses.

The show could provide seed funding, mentorship, infrastructure, and a transparent investment structure for promising teams. Viewers could follow the products after launch and see what happens when the real work begins.

This would be entertainment that creates builders.

Think about the cultural impact.

Today, many young people see entrepreneurship as something distant. They see successful founders after the funding rounds, after the headlines, after the millions.

They rarely see the messy beginning: the uncertainty, the customer who refuses to pay, the product that fails, the team that disagrees, and the discipline required to keep going.

What if we made that journey mainstream?

What if building a startup became as exciting to watch as competing for a reality TV prize?

What if young people began discussing customer acquisition, product design, revenue, engineering, and innovation with the same enthusiasm they bring to entertainment?

What if our next generation of celebrities included people who built solutions to some of our biggest problems?

This is not about making every young Nigerian a tech founder. It is about expanding what young people believe is possible for themselves.

We need to make building aspirational.

China’s investment in science, engineering, industrial capacity, and innovation offers important lessons about what happens when a society deliberately builds the capabilities to create things rather than merely consume them. We should study what works and develop a model suited to our own realities.

And Nigeria already has the talent, creativity, entrepreneurial spirit, and stories to make something like this works..

Here are the 30 biggest relevant stories, prioritized by scale, impact, and recency:

Houthi missile strikes on Aden presidential palace and airport: On Thursday, missiles hit Al-Maashiq Presidential Palace, killing five and wounding 16 (including guards and staff); PM Shaya al-Zindani and officials survived (two bodyguards killed). On Friday, two missiles struck Aden International Airport grounds (no casualties reported; a Yemenia flight was preparing to depart). Houthis claimed targeting “Saudi military operations headquarters.”

Saudi-led coalition intercepts multiple threats: Intercepted a ballistic missile headed for Yanbu (key Red Sea oil hub), two cruise missiles over the Red Sea, and three drones in southern Saudi Arabia and Riyadh regions. Ongoing pattern of intercepts continues.

Riyadh airport toll and attacks detailed: Coalition stated Houthis launched 20 attacks on King Khalid International Airport in October alone, killing 17 and wounding 333. Airport remained closed into October 17; earlier weekend strikes (around Oct 10) were the deadliest in the kingdom in over a decade.

Saudi accuses Iran of arming/encouraging Houthis: Deputy minister Rayed Krimly and coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki blamed Iran for encouraging escalation and helping acquire advanced weapons (ballistic missiles, drones, explosive boats) via regional actors, violating UN resolutions. Houthis rejected Oman talks.

Iran denies role and offers mediation: Iranian Foreign Ministry rejected any involvement in Houthi operations against Saudi Arabia and reiterated readiness to mediate between the Houthis and Riyadh.

UN Security Council condemnation: UNSC condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and threats to Red Sea/Bab al-Mandeb shipping in the strongest terms.

Trump on Israeli help and Abraham Accords: Trump said Saudi Arabia should accept Israel’s “very helpful” offer of support against the Houthis and that Saudi joining the Abraham Accords is “maybe more than ever” possible. Saudi has not publicly confirmed accepting Israeli assistance.

MBS faces major crisis: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is dealing with one of the biggest challenges of his tenure—airport closures, disrupted investment events, remote work/school shifts in Riyadh, strained defenses, and limited ally responses (US, Pakistan, Turkey). Economic and Vision 2030 ambitions under pressure.

Yemen battlefield updates (“Dawn of Yemen”): Saudi-backed IRG forces continued operations against Houthis, claiming advances and high numbers of targeting operations. Houthis reported civilian casualties from Saudi strikes (unverified independently). Fighting around Taiz, Marib, Red Sea coast, and Bab al-Mandeb remains intense.

Houthi claims and warnings: Renewed warnings that Saudi airspace/airports are unsafe (excluding Mecca/Medina). Claims of strikes on Aramco facilities, airports, and other targets in response to Saudi actions.

Iran-US war and Hormuz tensions: Ongoing sporadic exchanges after the June MoU expired. Iranian officials insist ending war on all fronts (including Lebanon) is essential. CENTCOM highlighted Iranian economic pressure (frozen funds, limited seaborne trade). Reports of a tanker explosion after hitting a mine in Hormuz (IRGC claim).

Iranian economic and militia strain: CENTCOM noted IRGC funding pressures, with Iran-aligned militias reportedly withholding fighter payments to support the IRGC. Broader economic shortfalls cited across sectors.
Saudi oil infrastructure concerns: Yanbu targeted (intercepted); prior hits or threats to Aramco facilities, Jazan processing plant, and pipelines used to bypass Hormuz. Oil export routes under stress.

Travel advisories and disruptions: UK advised against all but essential travel to Saudi Arabia. Major flight cancellations and airport closures continue to affect commercial aviation and events.

Pakistan and regional reactions: Pakistan condemned attacks on civilian/economic infrastructure. Limited additional military support noted from partners.

OpenAI Saudi employee bugging case fallout: Ongoing coverage of Abdulrahman Alfozan’s arrest for planting a recording device in an OpenAI executive conference room. Silicon Valley anxiety rises over AI espionage; FBI prioritizes protecting AI technology. Alfozan linked to Saudi tech advising.

White House Superintelligence Task Force: New task force (chaired by DNI Jay Clayton) started a 120-day clock for a frontier AI risk report covering cybersecurity, biosecurity, and model control. Voluntary industry accords signed; focus shifting toward incident reporting.

Sanders’ superintelligence ban proposal: Sen. Bernie Sanders continues pushing a permanent ban on artificial superintelligence and a pause on advanced AI development, citing cybersecurity risks (following Altman comments).

Palantir surveillance controversies persist: UK East Midlands police unit dropped Palantir tech after a trial over ethics/privacy concerns. Broader European pushback on data sovereignty and CLOUD Act access continues. CEO Karp’s warnings on predictive AI anticipating thoughts remain in discussion.

Palantir sovereign AI and business moves: Partnerships for sovereign AI (e.g., with Armada modular data centers, Ondas/Regna AI). Stock volatility after recent highs; strong commercial growth narrative continues alongside government contracts.

China AI export controls proposal: China proposing controls on certain AI technologies, adding to global AI race and technology transfer tensions.

Biotech: Nanoparticle gene editing for cystic fibrosis: UCLA researchers developed lipid nanoparticle delivery for full-length CFTR gene insertion into airway cells, restoring high levels of function in lab models (non-viral approach).

Biotech: Base editing for rare immunodeficiency: UCLA-led study used base editing to correct CD3 delta SCID mutation in blood stem cells, restoring T-cell production potential in lab/mouse models.

Biotech: Bacterial enzyme engineering: Researchers engineered a bacterial galactose oxidase (PsGalOx) as a greener biocatalyst tool for pharma and food ingredients, with major efficiency gains.

Biotech tools and delivery advances: New computational tool (moPepGen) for detecting hidden protein variants from genetic mutations (cancer research applications). Acoustic-wave method for efficient non-viral DNA delivery into cells for gene therapies.

Limited mainstream pickup.

Humanitarian costs in Yemen: Continued reports of civilian casualties, displacement, and shortages (food, fuel, medical) in areas like Taiz under pressure from fighting and siege-like conditions.

Iranian position on multi-front war: Deputy FM Saeed Khatibzadeh stressed that peace requires ending war on all fronts (including Lebanon), claiming the June MoU addressed this, while accusing the US/Israel of breaches.

text:
There is something revealing about the argument that keeping Nasir El-Rufai in detention could weaken the African Democratic Congress. It raises a fundamental question about the relationship between political power, individual liberty and the strength of democratic institutions.

Hon. Bello El-Rufai has offered a striking explanation of what he believes is driving the political controversy surrounding his father.

“There’s this fear about Mal. Nasir El-Rufai, because even his enemies will never say he’s not intelligent, he’s hardworking, he’s bold, he’s fearless.”

Bello further suggests that some political actors believe keeping El-Rufai detained would prevent the ADC from functioning effectively.

That is a serious allegation. It deserves examination, not automatic acceptance.

Nasir El-Rufai is an experienced political figure who served as Minister of the Federal Capital Territory and Governor of Kaduna State. His years in public office have made him a prominent and often controversial participant in Nigeria's political debates.

His supporters admire what they describe as his administrative discipline, willingness to take difficult decisions and readiness to confront powerful interests.

His critics have also raised important questions about aspects of his record in government. Both perspectives belong in any serious assessment of his political legacy.

But the immediate issue is bigger than whether Nigerians admire or oppose El-Rufai.

No political figure should be detained merely because of their influence, political associations or capacity to challenge an incumbent administration.

Equally, political prominence must never confer immunity from legitimate investigation or prosecution.

The distinction is essential.

Where criminal allegations exist, investigators must act within the law, disclose the applicable grounds for detention and respect judicial oversight. The accused must have a meaningful opportunity to challenge the allegations and defend themselves.

Where allegations of political interference arise, they should be examined through credible evidence rather than speculation.

The ADC, like every opposition party, must be free to organise, recruit members, develop policies and compete in elections without unlawful obstruction.

Its institutional strength should also depend on more than one personality.

Bello El-Rufai's remarks therefore raise questions worth asking: What are the legal grounds for his father's continued detention? Have applicable court orders been respected? And what evidence, if any, supports the allegation that detention is being used to undermine opposition activity?

These questions deserve clear, verifiable answers.

Nigeria's democracy is strengthened when political competition remains open, criminal justice remains independent and citizens can distinguish legitimate law enforcement from political persecution.

The test is not whether El-Rufai is feared, admired or criticised. It is whether the same constitutional protections apply to him as to every other Nigerian. https://t.co/B5SnNN7GkI

text:
Fall Weather Has Arrived! A Cool, Breezy Weekend Across Central Alabama

WeatherStation Morning Update | Saturday, October 17, 2026

Good Saturday morning, Central Alabama!

Fall weather has finally returned! After several days of unusually warm October temperatures, a cold front has brought much cooler and drier air into Alabama.

We're trading afternoon temperatures near 90° for highs in the 60s this weekend, with chilly mornings in the 40s. Some of our colder northern valleys could even dip into the upper 30s by Monday morning.

Saturday: Cool, Breezy, and Dry

Expect a mixture of sunshine and clouds today, with afternoon temperatures generally in the middle to upper 60s.

North winds around 10–20 mph could occasionally gust near 25 mph, making it feel a little cooler outside.

Rain chances are near zero, so outdoor plans should be fine. Just bring a jacket if you'll be spending time outside, especially during the morning.

Increased Fire Danger Today

One concern worth mentioning is the combination of gusty winds and low humidity.

Afternoon humidity could fall into the 30–40% range, allowing outdoor fires to spread more quickly.

I'd recommend avoiding outdoor burning today, especially leaves, brush, and yard debris.

Sunday: A Beautiful Fall Day

Sunday is shaping up to be a great day across Central Alabama!

We'll start with temperatures in the lower and middle 40s before warming into the upper 60s and lower 70s.

Expect plenty of sunshine, lighter winds, and dry conditions.

Whether you're heading to church, spending time with family, or enjoying the outdoors, Sunday should offer some very pleasant October weather.

Monday Morning: A Chilly Start

Clear skies and light winds Sunday night will allow temperatures to drop quickly.

Most communities will wake up Monday morning in the lower and middle 40s, but some colder northern valleys could dip into the upper 30s.

Widespread freezing temperatures aren't expected, but you'll definitely want a jacket heading out early.

Looking Ahead: Gradually Warmer Next Week

The cooler weather will stick around for a couple of days before temperatures begin climbing again.

Afternoon highs should return to the 70s Monday and Tuesday, with some lower 80s possible by Wednesday.

Dry weather will continue through much of next week, with no significant rainfall currently expected.

Final Thoughts

It's been quite a temperature turnaround across Central Alabama!

After several days of unusual October heat, we're finally enjoying some genuine fall weather.

Saturday will be cool and breezy, while Sunday looks especially nice with sunshine and lighter winds.

Just remember the increased fire danger today, and keep those jackets handy for our chilly mornings.

Enjoy the beautiful fall weather, Central Alabama, and have a wonderful weekend!

— Steve

𝐄𝐒𝐒𝐀𝐘𝐋𝐈 𝐓𝐎 𝐏𝐀𝐃𝐈𝐋𝐋𝐀: 𝐖𝐄 𝐆𝐀𝐕𝐄 𝐂𝐀𝐋𝐈𝐅𝐎𝐑𝐍𝐈𝐀 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐍𝐀𝐌𝐄𝐒, 𝐀𝐃𝐃𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐒𝐄𝐒 𝐀𝐍𝐃 𝐁𝐈𝐑𝐓𝐇𝐃𝐀𝐓𝐄𝐒 𝐎𝐅 𝟐𝟎,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐍𝐎𝐍𝐂𝐈𝐓𝐈𝐙𝐄𝐍𝐒

Sen. Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) said there is no evidence that 20,000 noncitizens received ballots in California, and accused the Trump administration of threatening election officials “𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐲 𝐥𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐥 𝐛𝐚𝐬𝐢𝐬.”

Bill Essayli, first assistant U.S. attorney for the Central District of California, answered on X: “𝘞𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘢𝘳𝘦 𝘺𝘰𝘶 𝘵𝘢𝘭𝘬𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢𝘣𝘰𝘶𝘵? 𝘞𝘦 𝘨𝘢𝘷𝘦 𝘊𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘧𝘰𝘳𝘯𝘪𝘢 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘢𝘮𝘦𝘴, 𝘢𝘥𝘥𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘦𝘴, 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘋𝘖𝘉𝘴 𝘰𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘰𝘯𝘤𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘻𝘦𝘯𝘴 𝘸𝘦'𝘷𝘦 𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘪𝘧𝘪𝘦𝘥.”

He said federal officials also hold the alien files at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, which contain each person's immigration status. His offer to the state: “𝘐𝘧 𝘊𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘧𝘰𝘳𝘯𝘪𝘢 𝘩𝘢𝘴 𝘦𝘷𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘴𝘩𝘰𝘸𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘺 𝘢𝘳𝘦 𝘪𝘯 𝘧𝘢𝘤𝘵 𝘤𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘻𝘦𝘯𝘴, 𝘸𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘭𝘰𝘷𝘦 𝘵𝘰 𝘴𝘦𝘦 𝘪𝘵.”

Essayli says the 20,000 figure comes from a review of federal databases confirmed by USCIS and HSI, and that the data has been handed over so California is “𝐟𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐜𝐤 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤.” Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Attorney General Rob Bonta have countered that DOJ has offered no proof, and that voting is already underway.

Essayli also warned that under 18 U.S.C. §§ 611 and 2, officials who knowingly tabulate unlawful ballots risk aiding and abetting a federal offense. DOJ has sued California over the ballots, and the case is now in court, where California's own records will matter.

text:
Your Home Is Watching You: The Smart Home Surveillance Trap

By PNW Staff October 15, 2026

For generations, Americans have viewed their homes as the one place where they could shut the door on the outside world. Private conversations remained private, family routines were nobody else's business, and corporations had no window into everyday life.

But that understanding of privacy is rapidly changing. And the remarkable part is that nobody has to force surveillance technology into our homes anymore. We're buying it ourselves.

Apple's new AI-powered smart home hub offers the latest glimpse into a future where microphones, cameras, facial recognition, door locks, thermostats, and artificial intelligence work together to manage our households.

The sales pitch is irresistible: greater convenience, better security, and a home that practically runs itself.

But behind that convenience lies a troubling question: How much information about your private life are you willing to surrender, and who ultimately controls it?

Apple Wants To Be At The Center Of Your Home

Apple's smart-home expansion represents something much bigger than another electronic gadget. Its new touchscreen hub is designed to coordinate household devices through an upgraded Siri assistant and Apple's connected-home ecosystem.

Imagine walking into your kitchen and having your home recognize you, display your schedule, adjust the temperature, turn on the lights, and tell you who is standing at the front door.

Now consider the information necessary to make that possible.

Security cameras monitor entrances and potentially interior rooms. Smart locks register when doors open and close. Motion sensors detect activity. Thermostats learn household schedules. Voice assistants respond to spoken commands.

Individually, each feature sounds useful. Together, they create the technological foundation for an extraordinarily detailed understanding of what happens inside a private residence.

Apple emphasizes privacy protections, including encryption and processing certain information directly on devices. Those safeguards matter. An assistant waiting for a wake phrase is not necessarily recording every conversation.

But the larger question remains: What happens when our homes become dependent on an expanding network of connected devices capable of collecting and interpreting information about our daily lives?

Your Home Is Becoming A Digital Profile

Most people understand that smartphones collect information about their location, internet activity, and purchasing habits. Far fewer recognize how much their homes can reveal.

A smart lock could establish when family members leave for work, when children return from school, and how frequently visitors arrive. A video doorbell could record deliveries and guests. Motion sensors could reveal which rooms are occupied, while a connected thermostat might indicate whether anyone is home.

None of these devices needs to record a private conversation to reveal intimate details about the people living there.

Combine their information, and patterns emerge.

When does the family wake up? When is the house empty? Who regularly visits? Have daily routines suddenly changed?

Not every manufacturer collects or retains all this information. Some devices process data locally, while others rely on cloud services. But the potential for collecting detailed behavioral information is expanding rapidly.

For decades, advertisers have constructed digital profiles based on browsing history, shopping behavior, and online interactions. Connected homes introduce another potential source of information: the physical routines of ordinary families.

Your house is no longer simply where you live. Increasingly, it can become another source of behavioral data.

Artificial Intelligence Changes Everything

Traditional smart-home technology was relatively simple. You issued a command, and a device responded. Turn on the lights. Lock the door. Adjust the thermostat.

Artificial intelligence introduces something far more sophisticated.

Instead of merely following instructions, AI systems can identify patterns, combine information from different sources, and predict what people are likely to do next.

A sufficiently integrated system might learn when homeowners leave, which visitors arrive regularly, or when household activity changes. It could distinguish between family members, recognize unusual behavior, and automatically adjust connected devices.

Some capabilities already exist in limited forms. Others remain emerging possibilities rather than features of any particular Apple product.

But the direction is clear: smart homes are evolving from devices that obey instructions into systems that interpret human behavior.

A camera recording may reveal little by itself. A smart lock's activity log might seem harmless. A thermostat's history appears unimportant.

But when AI connects information from all three, it may draw conclusions that none could establish independently.

That is the difference between collecting data and creating intelligence from data.

The technology doesn't necessarily need to hear every word you say to develop an intimate understanding of how you live.

What Happens When Someone Else Wants The Information?

Technology companies frequently assure consumers that their privacy is protected. Apple, in particular, has made privacy a central part of its identity.

Encryption, local processing, and strong security controls can genuinely reduce privacy risks. But connected systems are not automatically immune from outside access.

First, there is cybersecurity. Internet-connected cameras, locks, and household devices can become targets for hackers. Compromised passwords and software vulnerabilities have already exposed sensitive information in the broader smart-home industry.

Second, there is corporate access. Depending on the product, certain information may be stored on company servers, processed by outside providers, or retained for troubleshooting. Consumers rarely understand exactly what is collected, where it goes, or how long it remains available.

Third, there is government access.

Technology companies operate under laws that can require them to produce information in response to valid warrants, subpoenas, and court orders. Encryption may prevent access to certain records, but information companies possess and can access may also become available through legal demands.

Consider how dramatically this changes the privacy equation.

A generation ago, determining who entered a home, when its occupants left, or what happened inside might have required physical surveillance and considerable investigative resources.

Today, depending on the devices installed and records retained, portions of that information may already exist in digital form.

Surveillance has become potentially cheaper, more scalable, and less visible.

The Surveillance We Invited Inside

Smart-home technology offers genuine benefits. Cameras can deter crime, connected sensors can detect emergencies, and automated systems can make life easier.

But convenience should never eliminate basic questions about privacy and control.

Can homeowners determine what information is collected? Can they delete their records? Do they know whether their data stays inside their home or travels to distant servers?

The smart-home industry is selling Americans a future where every device anticipates their needs. What receives far less attention is the extraordinary amount of personal information that future could generate.

For generations, Americans feared outsiders placing listening devices and cameras inside their homes.

Now we install the technology ourselves, connect it to the internet, and celebrate when it becomes intelligent enough to learn our habits.

The greatest threat to household privacy may not be surveillance imposed upon us.

It may be the surveillance we willingly invite inside, one convenient device at a time.

text:
Why anyone can't work in silence? 🤔

Everyone wants success
Everyone knows it takes hard work

Hard work in complete silence

- No one is clapping when you lift weights
- No one is cheering when you send 100 cold emails
- No one is motivating you when you wake up early

We know this

But why can't we do this?

Because it's:

- Boring
- Repetitive
- No instant reward
- No progress bar over your head

So...

Solution? 🤔

Here's what you can do

1️⃣ Create an immediate reward

Don't wait 6 months to feel rewarded

Finished 10 cold emails?

Take a 5-minute break

Finished a difficult task?

Listen to your favourite song

Give your brain something to look forward to NOW

2️⃣ Make progress visible

Imagine writing 500 words every day

You might not see results today

But after 30 days, you've written 15,000 words

Track every day you show up

Now you can SEE your progress instead of just hoping for results

3️⃣ Break the work into smaller wins

Don't think about making $10,000 from freelancing

Think about:

- Finding 10 prospects
- Writing 5 personalised emails
- Improving one sales pitch
- Booking one call

You can't control when the money comes

But you can control today's target

4️⃣ Stop judging the work by today's results

You sent 100 cold emails and got no clients

Does that mean the work was useless?

Not necessarily

Maybe your targeting is wrong

Maybe your offer sucks

Maybe your emails land in spam

Track what you learn, not just what you earn

5️⃣ Separate the work from the reward

You don't need to enjoy writing every email

You need to understand why you're writing them

The email is boring

But learning how to acquire customers can change your business

Focus on what the boring task is building

So...

Stop expecting your brain to stay excited about a reward that's months away

Create small wins TODAY

Make progress visible

And keep working towards the bigger reward 🤏

text:
THE RAT RACE

Stop Participating. Wake Up With Grace.

The rat race doesn’t sound like much fun. So why do we get up every day and run?

My father used to say something along the lines of, “You gonna get out there and run with the rest of the rats?”

Well, Dad, I’ve got a better question.

Who said I had to?

We spend our lives chasing circumstances, competing with our neighbors, worrying about tomorrow, and trying to keep up with a society that never seems to slow down.

And then there’s they.

“They say this.”
“They say that.”
“You know what they say.”

But who the heck are they?

And who’s them?

We blame they for the way things are, then turn around and run with them like our lives depend on it. Maybe the joke is on us. We’ve given an invisible crowd the authority to dictate our reality, and we’re exhausting ourselves trying to keep up.

I’m not interested in figuring out who they are. I’m interested in figuring out why we keep listening.

I’m not participating in a societal race of mediocrity.

Consider the dog chasing a parked car—or even a moving one. What’s he going to do when he catches it? He has no plan for what comes next. He’s simply been conditioned to chase.

Sound familiar?

Then there’s the rat in the cage, raging against the very circumstances that keep him trapped. There’s a reason that lyric hits home:

“Despite all my rage, I’m still just a rat in the cage.”

The rage comes from the cage. The frustration comes from the race. And sometimes, the harder we struggle against the life we’ve been conditioned to live, the more tightly we grip the bars.

It’s like crabs in a bucket, each one trying to climb out while the others pull it back down.

Different expressions. Same lesson.

You cannot find freedom by blindly participating in the very thing that keeps you imprisoned.

But Scripture offers us another way.

Romans 12:2 tells us not to conform to this world, but to be transformed by the renewing of our minds.

Galatians 5:1 reminds us that Christ has set us free to live in freedom.

And Matthew 6:34 tells us not to borrow tomorrow’s troubles before tomorrow arrives.

That’s not permission to become complacent. It’s an invitation to stop wasting our lives on needless worry, meaningless competition, and the endless management of circumstances beyond our control.

I’m not waking up another day just to run with the rats.

I’m waking up to live.

To love. To grow. To create. To take care of my health, my peace, my faith, and the star player God entrusted to me.

Me.

Jesus said in John 10:10 that He came so we might have life, and have it more abundantly.

That’s the race worth running: the race of faith, love, truth, and purpose. Hebrews 12:1 tells us to run with endurance the race set before us—not somebody else’s race, not the race society invented, and certainly not a race built on fear and comparison.

And as my father used to say, if there was such a thing as luck, mine would be all good.

I’ll take that spirit with me, along with goodness and mercy, which Psalm 23:6 promises will follow us all the days of our lives.

So turn it up loud!

Let the rats run. Let the dogs chase cars. Let the crabs fight over the bucket.

I’m choosing a different way.

I don’t know who they are, and I don’t care to find out. I’m not here to chase every rumor, satisfy every expectation, or prove my worth by keeping pace with the crowd.

I’m Jack David.

I’m loved. I’m free to choose. I’m taking care of me, my star player, and I’m walking in the grace of my Father.

I’m not running with the rest of the rats. I’m running the race God set before me.

And if the world wants to call that crazy, that’s fine.

I’d rather be free than fit in.

Wake up with grace. Live with purpose. And remember:

You don’t have to participate in every race you’re invited to run.

— Jack David

#JackDavid #TheRatRace #WakeUpWithGrace #RenewYourMind #FreedomInChrist #TheAbundantLife #ChooseYourRace

text:
I thought I was getting married this year. My fiancée had already received her engagement ring, both our families were excited, and my mother had spent $10,000 on lace for our wedding celebration.

Then one of my female friends moved to Atlanta and decided to surprise my fiancée with lunch.

What she found in my fiancée's apartment made me realize I might not even be the man she intended to marry.

There was a pink blanket on her couch, a dog bowl with another man's dog's name on it, men's sneakers by the door, and a wedding Save the Date card on her fridge.

Lauren & Derek. November 3. Chateau Elan Winery.

The woman I was supposed to marry had another wedding planned.

And I wasn't the groom.

My fiancée and I met three years ago when she was visiting her cousin in Atlanta over the July 4th weekend. She told me I wasn't her usual type. I was quiet, tall, well put together, and didn't talk too much. I took her to Ponce City Market for tacos on our first date, then we walked along the BeltLine for almost three hours. She later told me that what attracted her most was how I listened whenever she spoke.

We did long distance for a year. Dallas to Atlanta was only a two-hour flight, so we made it work. Every other weekend, one of us would fly to see the other. I was consistent. I sent her Uber Eats during her twelve-hour clinical rotations, and she introduced me to her mother over FaceTime. Her mother loved me almost immediately.

After exactly one year and eight months together, I proposed over FaceTime. She had just returned from clinicals and was still wearing her scrubs when I said, "Maya, I'm tired of this FaceTime relationship. I want to wake up next to you. Will you marry me?"

Then I showed her the ring through the camera. I had already sent it to her by FedEx. It was a simple 1.2-carat oval diamond, exactly her style.

She screamed so loudly that her roommate thought something terrible had happened. She posted the engagement, and her mother called mine that same night. Both families were excited, and we started planning the wedding.

We agreed that she would finish her nursing program in Dallas in May, move to Atlanta in June, have a small courthouse wedding in July, and then celebrate with a big Nigerian-American wedding in December.

I offered to handle the courthouse arrangements because I was already living in Atlanta. She agreed and told me she couldn't wait to become my wife.

Looking back, there were warning signs I should have noticed.

She always had a reason not to visit me. Sometimes she blamed her clinical schedule, sometimes she said she needed to save money, and sometimes she told me she wanted us to save for our future house. I understood because nursing school was demanding, and I wanted her to finish without unnecessary stress.

Whenever I visited her in Dallas, she was affectionate and attentive. She knew how to make me feel loved, so I never imagined she could be hiding something this serious.

We FaceTimed almost every night. She knew my routines, my friends, and my plans for our future. I thought we were building a life together.

I had no idea she was building another one with someone else.

Last month, one of my female friends, Tasha, moved to Atlanta after matching for her residency at Emory. She knew about my engagement and offered to surprise Maya with lunch when she had some free time.

I gave her Maya's apartment details, thinking it would be a sweet gesture.

Tasha arrived on Tuesday at 1 p.m. At 1:17 p.m., she sent me a video.

I will never forget that time.

If a doctor asks you "where does it hurt?" for 20 minutes, you assume he's guessing off Google

If he looks at your hand for 3 seconds & says "you wake up at 3am with your left ring finger numb & your lower back tight," you will swallow whatever pill he puts on the table without asking what's inside it

The human brain has a permanent glitch: it automatically assumes whoever describes a problem in higher resolution than you can also owns the cure

Most people write marketing that brags about the cure. "We'll add $100k/mo to your business." Every founder with money has seen 4,000 ads promising that & his brain filters it out before he finishes the sentence

Describe his private Tuesday more accurately than he describes it to his own wife & he wires you $25,000 without asking for a case study

Here's how I engineer this across X content, DMs & sales calls:

1... Describe the Tuesday, never the dream

When I want to sign a founder doing $150k/mo, I write a paragraph about:
- the $8,000/mo agency retainer he keeps paying out of guilt because switching feels like a second job
- the Slack channel where the agency drops a weekly Loom every Friday that nobody on his team watches anymore
- the call he had with his partner in August where they both blamed a bad month on "seasonality" & both knew they were lying

95% of readers scroll right past that paragraph. Designed. The 5% living inside that exact week freeze mid-scroll because it feels like someone bugged their office

2... Predict his last failed fix before he admits he tried it

When a prospect lands in my X DMs or hops on a call, I never ask "what have you tried so far?"

I tell him what he already tried & where it broke:

"At your revenue you probably already hired a cold email agency for $4k/mo, got 15 calls with broke leads asking for a payment plan, & killed it after 60 days"

When you name a guy's last mistake before he tells you about it, every ounce of skepticism leaves his body. You just proved you've seen this movie 50 times

3... Put a clinical name on the thing hurting him

A symptom with no name feels like bad luck. A symptom with a name feels like a condition you've cured before

Tell a founder "your content isn't converting" & he argues with you

Tell him "your profile is failing the 2am hunger audit because you have comment-gate posts sitting right above a $15,000 offer" & he asks how fast your team can rebuild it

4... Why X is the only platform where you can run a 4-minute diagnosis for $0

You cannot fit a clinical diagnosis inside a 12-second reel or a cold email. On Instagram & TikTok people scroll to turn their brain off. On LinkedIn they perform for their boss

X is the only place on earth where a founder worth $10M+ sits still at 11pm & reads 1,000 words from a stranger in silence. By the time he finishes three of my long-form posts, he's spent 15 minutes watching me dissect his exact business down to the bolts

When the "what do you charge" DM finally lands, the sale is already over. Nobody haggles with the only doctor who knew which finger was numb

We run this exact X content + funnel machine for brands doing $50k-$500k/mo -> pulling webinar opt-ins at $0.25, booked calls at $5-50 & closing calls at 50-60%

text:
ROGER MARSHALL: SERVING KANSAS OR DEFENDING DONALD TRUMP?

The claim that Senator Roger Marshall has been a champion of the Constitution and an outstanding representative of Kansas deserves to be tested against his actual record.

The results are difficult to reconcile with that praise.

Constitutional government requires Congress to exercise its powers independently of the president. Those responsibilities include declaring war, overseeing federal spending, and regulating foreign commerce. Marshall, however, has repeatedly sided with Donald Trump's assertions of executive authority instead of demanding greater congressional accountability.

Consider the war with Iran.

On September 24, 2026, Marshall opposed a resolution calling for American troops to be withdrawn from hostilities that Congress had not authorized. It was not his first vote against such a measure. Regardless of whether someone considers Iran a serious threat, a prolonged war warrants congressional debate and authorization. Marshall's votes have helped Congress avoid confronting that obligation.

Kansas farmers are paying a substantial economic price for policies Marshall supports.

Trump's tariffs have unsettled agricultural trade, weakened export opportunities, and pushed China toward other suppliers of soybeans, sorghum, and additional farm commodities. In October, Reuters reported that China was substantially behind its commitments to purchase American soybeans, with Brazil capturing much of the lost business.

Marshall has continued defending Trump's trade strategy, despite conceding that tariffs inflicted economic hardship on farmers. And in February 2026, the Supreme Court determined that Trump lacked authority under emergency-powers legislation to impose his sweeping tariffs. A senator committed to congressional authority should recognize the significance of that ruling.

Then there is the Iran war's effect on production costs.

According to the Associated Press, by October gasoline prices had climbed approximately 45% and diesel prices 68% compared with their prewar levels. Earlier in the year, the American Farm Bureau Federation reported that urea fertilizer prices had jumped 55% and farm diesel prices 72% within a matter of months.

For Kansas agriculture, those increases are particularly damaging. Farmers need diesel to operate tractors and combines, while wheat and corn production depend on fertilizer. Rising expenses would be troublesome enough on their own. Combined with disrupted export markets and unpredictable crop prices, they put additional pressure on already narrow profit margins.

Marshall argues that Trump's approach will produce benefits in the future. But Kansans are entitled to judge their senator by what his policies have delivered, not merely what he hopes they eventually accomplish.

THE CONSTITUTION DOES NOT REQUIRE A SENATOR TO PROTECT THE PRESIDENT FROM SCRUTINY. IT REQUIRES HIM TO FULFILL HIS OWN CONSTITUTIONAL DUTIES

Roger Marshall was elected to represent Kansas, not to provide political cover for Donald Trump. His record offers substantial grounds to challenge the claim that he has served either responsibility well.

Catholicism  often dressed pagan gods up in new clothes, gave them Bible-friendly names, and put them back in the same spots they’d always been. In other words, it wasn’t a purge, it was a PR rebrand.

This isn’t wild conspiracy theory dude. Historians, archaeologists, and even some Catholic scholars will tell you the same thing. In order for the Roman government to spread its take over of Churches to the pagan masses of Rome, it had to absorb local customs and deities to make the religion more palatable to converts. People don’t like letting go of their old gods, festivals, and sacred sites. 

The Roman pagan government knew that. So instead of saying, “Your god is fake, burn his temple,” it often said, “This temple? Oh, it’s for Saint So-and-So now. Keep the temple, it’s fine”

They treated Saints exactly like the Roman pagans treated all of their different Gods. 

Examples…

Saint Barbara, the patron saint of miners.

Saint Hubertus, the patron saint of hunters and foresters.

Saint Leonhard, the protector of farmers and animals. 

Saint Nicholas, “venerated” as the patron saint of merchants and traders.

Brigid, the beloved Celtic goddess associated with fertility and healing, is perhaps the clearest example of the survival of an early goddess into Catholicism. Practitioners, mainly Ireland, pay tribute to Saint Brigid of Ireland who shares many of the early goddess’s attributes. Her feast day on the first of February falls around the same time as the pagan celebration of Imbolc.

We see the EXACT SAME thing at ancient pagan sites, where the gods and goddesses were believed to be in harmony with the landscape, embodying its qualities.

Ancient pagan beliefs survived into the Middle Ages.

This resulted through the centuries in Catholic saints replacing the old gods and goddesses.

It’s extremely clear to see former pagan gods and goddesses in Catholic saints and their attributes.

There are astonishing parallels between both belief systems, Roman paganism and aspects of Catholicism. 

The adoption of these pagan practices and symbols by the Catholic Church shows how the adoption of new institutions were difficult for pagan Romans and a blending of their pagan traditions was required for adoption of the masses after hundreds of years of the Roman government demonizing and slaughtering Christian’s. 

This all parallels the concept of diversity and multitude. In paganism, there were numerous gods and goddesses, each responsible for specific aspects of life or the world. In Catholicism, the “veneration” of saints offers a parallel system. Instead of many gods, there are hundreds of saints, each covering SPECIFIC attributes or domains. Similar to pagan gods, these saints can be both male and female.

text:
The Joyful Mysteries of the Rosary: Saturday October 17, 2026

A young woman stands in a quiet room. An angel waits for her answer. The world holds its breath, and so do we. What does God ask when he draws near? What joy follows a yes spoken in trust? The Joyful Mysteries hold that question in scenes of arrival, recognition, and return.

In these mysteries we stay with the coming of Jesus. Mary says yes, and the Word takes flesh. She visits Elizabeth, and joy leaps ahead of them. Jesus is born in poverty, offered in the temple, and found again among the teachers. God enters ordinary rooms, roads, and worries. This joy is not noise. It is the certainty that the Son has come to dwell with his people. We ask for grace to welcome him as Mary did, with trust and with room in our days. Come and pray the Joyful Mysteries with us today. Let each bead slow us down until we notice Christ already near.

I pray for you today 🙏 @RCatholicPrayer
