text:
In the future womanhood must take the lead, because she is given an enhanced and more delicate intuitive perception. Man will change through the nature of woman when he is forced to recognize in her the hint of what is more noble...

"For the sake of those few faithful ones, the earth-woman, through the nearness of God, shall be permitted to rise to that height which was already ordained for her from the very beginning. Blessed are you mankind, that you may receive this grace although you do not deserve it."

"In the future strictly observe the laws of God. The purity of earthly woman lies in her faithfulness. For faithfulness is purity. A woman without faithfulness is unworthy to be called woman. And unfaithful is every woman who playfully trifles with men, either in words or in thoughts. Unfaithful to herself and to her high task in this Creation therefore also on earth."

"Faithfulness alone calls forth all the virtues in woman. Not one of them will be lacking. Whatever she does is pure when it is done in faithfulness. Nor is it otherwise in man. Faithfulness is purity for every human being. Naturally faithfulness must be genuine; it must not merely spring from the imagination. And genuine faithfulness can only live in true love, never in passion or fantasy."

"Therefore faithfulness is the highest virtue of every woman; it also enables her fully to accomplish her high task in this Creation. Heed this well, ye men: The high, fine Substantiality that which is more perceptive and more gentle, leads the household in the great Creation. Woman is also appointed to her office, which she is completely capable of fulfilling: To lead the household in the earthly existence, to offer a home in the right sense."

"In the future, it is the task of the woman to make this earth homelike and harmonious and she can develop this task to artistic heights. Therein lies everything and upon this everything must be founded if it is to thrive and blossom forth. The home must become a sanctuary through the woman. It must become a Temple for the Will of God. This contains worship of God when you listen in to His Holy Volition in Creation and when you adjust your life and your activity on earth accordingly."

"And also man, whose profession in the past has proved to be based exclusively on slavish subjection to the intellect, will change through the nature of woman when he is forced to recognize in her the hint to what is more noble. Always look into the household of this Creation and you will know how you have to arrange your life one earth."

"However man must not disregard the order of a household in an inconsiderate way, no matter whether through neglectful non-observance or a craving for power; for the activity of the woman in the household is just as important as is that of the man in his profession. It is merely of a different nature, but it cannot be dispensed with."

"Woman's task in the home swings in the Law of God of which you are urgently reminded by the physical body, in that the latter seeks recreation, rest and nourishment and last but not least...harmony among the souls therein which refreshes and provides a new incentive and new strength for all man's activities. The balance in this must be absolutely harmonious."

"For this reason the woman too, must respect the work of the man and not think that her activity may alone be decisive. The activity of both parts shall be joined to each other in an even swinging. The one may not disturb the other. Thus man must not willfully upset or confuse the orders in the household, but through being punctual and showing a growing understanding, he must even help so that everything can keep its harmonious course."

"This is what you can and must learn from Creation. In the Millennium you will yet be compelled to do so, otherwise you could never exist therein. And whoever is then not able to continue to exist in it will be eliminated according to the Law of Creation for he no longer remains worthy of the blessings of Creation."

"Therefore pay heed to your home and learn to understand this Subsequent Creation. You must become familiar with it and now at last adjust yourselves to the order also here on earth; otherwise you will be lost and must perish."

Read "In the Light of Truth: The Grail Message" by the Son of Man Immanuel. As an act of Grace, He has opened the Book of Creation to mankind; a mission that had started with Jesus Christ.

text:
No, the Blessed Virgin Mary is the Ark of the New and Eternal Covenant.

I’ll prove it with Scriptural Typology and Patristics.

(1) Scriptural Typology

(A) Basic Citation 

Luke 1 (compares Mary with the Ark of the Covenant - verse 35 with Numbers 9:15, verse 44 with 2 Samuel 6:14, verse 43 with 2 Samuel 6:9, verse 56 with 2 Samuel 6:11)

(B) Substantive Typology 

(1) First 

Numbers 9:15 “On the day when the tabernacle was erected, the cloud[b] covered the tabernacle, the tent of the covenant; but from evening until morning it took on the appearance of fire over the tabernacle.”

Luke 1:35 “And the angel answering, said to her: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee. And therefore also the Holy which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.”

(2) Second

2 Samuel 6:14-15 “Then David came dancing before the Lord with abandon, girt with a linen ephod.[b] 15 David and all the house of Israel were bringing up the ark of the Lord with shouts of joy and sound of horn.”

Luke 1:44 “For behold as soon as the voice of thy salutation sounded in my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy.”

(3) Third

2 Samuel 6:9 “David became frightened of the Lordthat day, and he said, “How can the ark of the Lord come to me?”

Luke 1:43 “And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me.”

(4) Fourth

2 Samuel 6:11 “The ark of the Lord remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-edom and all his household.”

Luke 1:56 “And Mary abode with her about three months; and she returned to her own house.”

(2) Patristics

St. Cyril 

“The Ark would be the type and image of Christ : for if we look back to the way of the Incarnation of the Only-begotten, we shall see that it is in the temple of the Virgin, as in an ark that the Word of God took up His abode. For in Him dwelt all the fullness of the Godhead bodily, as the Scripture saith. But the testimonies in the ark were the word of God, and the wood of it was imperishable, and with pure and choicest gold was it beautified within and without” (St. Cyril, De ador. In Spir. Et Verit, p. 293, St. Maximus of Turin and other Fathers apply the Ark of the Covenant to the Blessed Virgin Mary) (Blessed Virgin, p. 76).

St. Athanasius 

“Be mindful of us, most holy virgin, who after childbirth didst remain virgin; and grant to us for these small words great gifts from the riches of they graces, O thou full of grace. Accept them as though they were true and adequate praises in they honor; and if there is in them any virtue and any praise, we offer them as a hymn from ourselves and from all creatures to thee, full of grace, Lady, Queen, Mistress, Mother of God, and Ark of sanctification” (Orat. In Deip. Annuntiat, nn. 13, 14. Int. Opp. S. Athanasii) (Blessed Virgin, p. 80).

          “O noble Virgin, truly you are greater than any other greatness. For who is your equal in greatness, O dwelling place of God the Word? To whom among all creatures shall I compare you, O Virgin? You are greater than them all O (Ark of the) Covenant, clothed with purity instead of gold! You are the Ark in which is found the golden vessel containing the true manna, that is, the flesh in which Divinity resides.” Homily of the Papyrus of Turin.

Yeshayahu: The Prophetic Name Across the Inhabited Earth
From the Farthest Reaches of Sinim to Beyond the Pillars of Hercules - 

An Extraordinary Global Philological Compilation of 252 Linguistic Entries, Ancient Sacred Scripts, Indigenous Orthographies, Historical Manuscript Traditions, and Rare Biblical Nomenclatures
Presented by DeepAncientThought and The New Alexandria Library of Texas -

A Global Announcement
From the ancient Hebrew manuscripts of Jerusalem to the Arctic settlements of Labrador, from the Euphratean world of Mesopotamia to the Ethiopian highlands, from the remotest linguistic communities of the Amazon to the scattered volcanic islands of Polynesia, one prophetic name has entered an astonishing multitude of human writing systems.

Yeshayahu. יְשַׁעְיָהוּ. Isaiah.
Its Hebrew theophoric composition preserves the declaration Yahweh is salvation, joining the Semitic root ישע, associated with salvation and deliverance, to the divine element יהו.

Across centuries of translation, manuscript transmission, missionary printing, indigenous literacy, ecclesiastical scholarship, and multilingual biblical interpretation, this name acquired a remarkable variety of written and spoken representations.

The present compilation brings together 252 comparative entries within seven geographical and historical divisions.

 The collection embraces the oldest biblical literary languages, medieval Christian manuscript cultures, Semitic and Iranian comparanda, endangered indigenous traditions, Arctic syllabics, African scripts, Austronesian languages, Amerindian orthographies, and the extraordinarily diverse linguistic environments of the Pacific.
Its central investigation concerns the survival and transformation of a sacred proper name across geographical distance, divergent writing systems, phonological adaptation, and successive generations of biblical translation.
Isaiah 49:12 supplies a particularly fitting geographical horizon, describing peoples approaching from afar, from the north, from the west, and from the land called Sinim in the Masoretic Hebrew. The precise location of Sinim remains disputed among historical commentators and ancient textual witnesses. Nevertheless, its literary association with distant peoples provides an evocative framework for this worldwide linguistic undertaking.

The classical Pillars of Hercules, guarding the western  Mediterranean passage toward the Atlantic, supply the corresponding geographical emblem of the farthest western horizon.

From the prophetic horizons of antiquity to the geographical extremities of the inhabited Earth, the history of Yeshayahu becomes a study of language, memory, revelation, and the extraordinary endurance of biblical nomenclature.

The Global Linguistic Register - 

The spellings below reproduce the submitted compilation in normalized form. They constitute a comparative working register. Individual vernacular spellings, historical reconstructions, and manuscript attributions require edition-level verification before being described as independently attested.

I. Ancient Biblical Languages, Sacred Manuscripts, and Historical Writing Systems

1. Hebrew: יְשַׁעְיָהוּ, Yeshayahu
2. Biblical Aramaic: יְשַׁעְיָה, Yeshayah
3. Classical Syriac: ܐܫܥܝܐ, Eshaʿya
4. Ancient Greek: Ἠσαΐας, Esaias
5. Latin: Isaias
6. Arabic: إشعياء, Ishʿiyāʾ
7. Coptic: Ⲏⲥⲁⲓⲁⲥ, Esaias
8. Geʿez: ኢሳይያስ, Isayyas
9. Gothic: Esaias, transliterated form
10. Old Church Slavonic: Исаїа, Isaia
11. Old Nubian: ⲓⲥⲁⲓⲁⲥ, proposed form
12. Sogdian: Isaya, proposed transcription
13. Phoenician: 𐤉𐤔𐤏𐤉𐤄𐤅, reconstructed consonantal transcription
14. Punic: YŠʿYHW, comparative reconstruction
15. Ugaritic: Proposed Northwest Semitic reconstruction
16. Akkadian: Proposed cuneiform adaptation
17. Elamite: Proposed cuneiform adaptation
The last five entries are historical linguistic comparisons, rather than established surviving attestations of Isaiah's name.
II. South Asia, East Asia, Southeast Asia, and Ancient Asian Minorities
1. Pashto: اشعیا
2. Dari: اشعیا
3. Chinese: 以赛亚, Yǐsàiyà; fuller Hebrew-oriented transliteration 耶沙亚胡

🔑 Extraordinary Philological and Phenomenological Features - 

Theophoric Name Conservation. The preservation of the original Hebrew divine element, particularly within the forms Yeshayahu and Yeshayah, supplies the linguistic foundation for examining how ancient Hebrew personal names express theological propositions.

Consonantal Metamorphosis. The succession Yeshayahu, Esaias, Isaias, Isaia, Yesaya, Izaya, and Itaia illustrates the transformations through which proper names may pass when transmitted into languages with different consonant inventories and orthographic conventions.

Scriptural Polygraphy. Hebrew, Syriac, Greek, Latin, Ethiopic, Coptic, Chinese, Devanagari, Tamil, Cherokee, Canadian Aboriginal syllabics, and numerous other scripts offer an unusually extensive comparative field for investigating the graphical representation of a single ancient name.

Arctic Biblical Typography. 

The historically documented 1837 Labrador Inuktitut edition, Prophetib Iesaiasib Aglangit, preserves an especially valuable example of nineteenth-century biblical translation and the integration of Isaiah's name into an indigenous grammatical structure.

Oceanic Phonological Adaptation. Proposed forms such as Isaia, Esaia, Aesea, and Itaia invite comparative examination of inherited biblical terminology across Polynesian, Micronesian, and Melanesian linguistic systems.
Indigenous Manuscript Historiography. The surviving histories of missionary printing, vernacular alphabet development, translation revision, and local reading communities offer substantial opportunities for recovering neglected bibliographical evidence.

Cross-Continental Onomastics. By bringing together European, African, American, Arctic, Asian, and Pacific forms, the compilation establishes a substantial working foundation for investigating the historical transmission of biblical personal names.

Prophetic Geographical Correspondence. Isaiah 11:12, 42:10, 49:6, 49:12, 60:1–9, and 66:18–20 furnish a remarkable biblical vocabulary concerning distant peoples, islands, nations, geographical extremities, and the international proclamation of divine glory.

The Larger Literary Contribution
This comparative undertaking opens a bibliographical and philological field considerably broader than a conventional multilingual word list. Each entry presents the possibility of recovering a particular history of translation, the date of a first printed Scripture, the contribution of an indigenous translator, the development of a local orthography, the transformation of a Semitic consonant sequence, or the survival of biblical nomenclature in a community whose literary records remain little known outside specialist archives.

The full scholarly edition can extend the present register into manuscript facsimiles, verified original-script transcriptions, historical printing censuses, grammatical comparisons, linguistic family classifications, geographical concordances, translation genealogies, and a chronological account of the diffusion of the Book of Isaiah.
Its ambition is to establish an enduring reference work for biblical philology, comparative onomastics, historical linguistics, indigenous literary history, manuscript bibliography, sacred geography, and the phenomenology of written language.

Yeshayahu, From Antiquity to the Ends of the Earth

One ancient Hebrew prophetic name. Seven great comparative divisions. 252 collected linguistic entries. A worldwide record of biblical language in remarkable historical and geographical diversity.

There is not one page or chapter in the bible that does not have 1. The holy spirit through the word and 2. Yeshayahu aka Isaiah” in Hebrew- Yeshayahu (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ) - God saves - God is our Salvation for the Entire Planet earth! This is the first time ever these languages have been compliled! 

Yeshayahu or Isaiah the prophet who bore this name carried its message into some of the darkest days of Judah’s history.

📜 Ancient & Biblical Languages

• Hebrew: יְשַׁעְיָהוּ (pronounced Ye-sha-ya-hu). This is the original, full theophoric name found in the Hebrew scriptures.

• Syriac (Classical Aramaic): ܐܫܥܝܐ (pronounced Esha'ya). In the Syriac Peshitta (the standard version of the Bible for churches in the Syriac tradition), the name matches the shorter Aramaic biblical form Yis'aya.

• Latin: Isaias 
(Classical/Ecclesiastical Latin). Latin dropped the original -yahu ending, adapting the name from the Ancient Greek Septuagint translation (Ēsaïas).

• Akkadian: Cuneiform records tracking Judean exiles in Mesopotamia transliterated Hebrew names using available syllable signs. The elements would be broken down as ia-a-shu-ú (for the Yesha / salvation element) paired with ia-a-hu-ú (the Yahu deity element).

• Elamite: As a linguistic isolate of ancient southwestern Iran, the Elamite language did not have a native equivalent for the name. In historical Achaemenid royal or administrative records, West Semitic names containing the Hebrew -yahu suffix were phonetically transliterated into Elamite cuneiform as -ya-u-[-u-a].
Modern Regional Languages

• Afghan (Pashto / Dari): اشعیا (pronounced Eshaya). As Afghanistan is predominantly Islamic, the name is shared via the Quranic/Arabic tradition of the prophet, spelled إشعياء.

• Chinese:

• 以赛亚 (Simplified: Yǐsàiyà) - Used in standard Chinese Christian Bibles (such as the Chinese Union Version).

• 耶沙亚胡 (Yēshāyàhú) -  Used in academic or Jewish contexts when strictly transliterating the exact phonetics of Yeshayahu.

• Indian Languages (South Asia): Because India has many major languages, the translation varies by script, though most derive from the English Isaiah or the Arabic Eshaya:

• Hindi: यशायाह (Yashāyāh) or इसायाह (Isāyāh)

• Tamil: ஏசாயா (Ēsāyā)

• Malayalam: യശയ്യാഹ് (Yashayyāh• Pitjantjatjara Bible: Adapted closely to the English sound as Aisaya.

• Kriol (The most widely spoken Aboriginal language today): Transliterated phonetically as Ayajaya

📝 Commentary This is one of the most extraordinary supernatural verses in " Yeshayahu " 

The Arm of YHWH is addressed almost personally:

Awake. Awake. Put on strength.

The people invoke the ancient manifestations of Divine power and ask that the same agency become active in their own age.

Then Isaiah enters archaic cosmic vocabulary:

רַהַב, Rahab
תַּנִּין, tannîn, dragon

Rahab here is not Rahab of Jericho. In Isaiah, Job and the Psalms, the name belongs to a complex poetic field associated with pride, Egypt, and the great defeated sea-opposition. 

The dragon, tannîn, belongs to the same scriptural world as the great sea-creatures and serpent powers appearing in Genesis 1, Psalm 74, Ezekiel 29 and Isaiah 27.

Ancient Jewish interpretation already read the language historically as well as cosmically. Ibn Ezra identifies Rahab with proud Egypt and the dragon with Pharaoh, appealing specifically to Ezekiel 29:3, where Pharaoh is called the great dragon lying among his rivers.  

Modern Jewish textual notes also preserve Rahab and Dragon explicitly as the names of primeval monster figures.

The crucial fact is that Isaiah immediately connects this dragon-language to the Exodus in verse 10. The text therefore overlays cosmic conflict vocabulary upon historical deliverance.

Psalm 74 follows a similar pattern: YHWH divides the sea and breaks the heads of dragons in the waters.

Psalm 89 joins mastery of raging sea with crushing Rahab.

Job 26 joins YHWH's power over the sea, Rahab and the fleeing serpent.

Isaiah 27 speaks of YHWH punishing Leviathan and slaying the dragon in the sea.

Revelation later retrieves dragon imagery on an explicitly eschatological scale.

Isaiah 51:9 therefore stands at a remarkable intersection of Angelomachick and dragon-combat imagery, Exodus historiography, sacred hydrology and the invocation of ancient Divine warfare.

text:
Hello, I am Palestinian. 🇵🇸 And since honesty is rare in my politics, allow me to confess a few things.

The UN offered me a state. Alongside Israel. Borders, independence, recognition. I said no. My leaders promised that the war would "drive the Jews into the sea." Instead, I lost everything, and they called it a catastrophe. Not because they didn't offer me a state, but because I rejected it.

1948–2025. Arab states could have integrated me, given me rights, passports, dignity. Instead, they locked me up in refugee camps for generations, so that I would remain a weapon against Israel. They built palaces for themselves and prisons for me. They used me as propaganda, not as people.

After another lost war, I could have built a state in the West Bank and Gaza. Instead, I insisted on "no peace, no recognition, no negotiations." Three no's. Fifty years later, I'm still stateless. Turns out rejection doesn't pay the rent.

Oslo, 1990s. Israel said, "Let's give it a try." It gave me autonomy. Guns for the police. Billions in aid. What did my leaders do? They stole the money, armed militias, and launched an intifada. Suicide bombings instead of schools. Rockets instead of factories.

Gaza, 2005. Israel left completely. No settlers, no soldiers. I had the chance to turn Gaza into a Mediterranean Singapore. I voted for Hamas. They turned it into Mogadishu by the sea. Billions in aid? Tunnels, rockets, and palaces for their leaders, while my people eat canned food in the dark.

Democracy? I haven't had elections in almost 20 years. Hamas kills dissidents in Gaza. Fatah imprisons them in the West Bank. My leaders cancel elections because they're too busy fighting for power.

Religion. Instead of building a future, I put clerics on television teaching children to hate Jews. I glorify "martyrs" who blow up buses. I raise my children on songs of blood and fire instead of books and science. I trade hope for holy war.
Arab world. Arab regimes call me "brother."

But ask them how many Palestinians can live freely in Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, or Kuwait. They exclude me, but they celebrate my death, because my death is their excuse.
Absurd. I keep saying I want to "build a state." And ironically, right next door is Israel: the neighbor that built a thriving democracy, a technological powerhouse, desert farms, dusty cities. No oil, no infinite wealth, just courage. I could have learned, copied, collaborated. Instead, I chose envy and rage.

Anti-Jewish obsession. I could have accepted Jews as neighbors. I could have said, "Two nations, two states." Instead, I repeat: "From the river to the sea." Instead of showcasing honor, hospitality, and the rich Arab culture, I displayed only the culture of the sword.Anger, extremism, and bloodshed. Instead of shouting salaam (peace) to the Israelis, I shouted death to the Jews. And then I feign surprise when the Israelis don't trust me, when they're angry, disappointed, and convinced that I don't want coexistence at all.

Accountability. I blame Israel for everything. Always. Do my leaders steal billions? Blame Israel. Does Hamas fire rockets from hospitals? Blame Israel. Do I glorify death more than life? Blame Israel. Accountability is not my strong suit.

I am Palestinian. I could have built a nation, many times over. I chose rejection, corruption, and endless war. I could have lived in peace with Israel, but I chose to live in the shadow of its destruction.
So yes, I am a victim. But all too often, I am a victim of my own leaders, my own choices, and my own refusal to let go of hatred. And that, dear reader, is the tragedy no one wants to admit.

text:
What about this?

Key Historical Episodes

1. The Umayyad Conquest of Hispania (711–718 AD)
The Context: Under the Visigothic Kingdom in Spain, Jews faced severe state-sponsored persecution, forced conversions, and restrictions on civil rights.   The Assistance: As Muslim troops under Tariq ibn Ziyad advanced across the Iberian Peninsula, several chroniclers record that local Jewish populations welcomed the invaders. In several captured cities—most notably Córdoba, Granada, Seville, and Toledo—Muslim commanders left captured garrisons under the administration and defense of local Jewish militias so the main Muslim army could continue advancing north.   Historical Debate: While medieval Christian chronicles (such as those by Lucas de Tuy or Rodrigo Jiménez de Rada) often framed this as "treason" or opening city gates to the invaders, modern historians treat these claims with nuance. Some scholars note that while Jews certainly aided the incoming forces due to Visigothic oppression, later Christian accounts exaggerated the degree of conspiracy to explain their own rapid military collapse.   

2. The Siege of Caesarea Maritima (c. 640 AD)
The Context: During the Muslim conquest of the Levant, the Byzantine fortress city of Caesarea held out against Arab forces for several years.The Assistance: According to early Islamic and Jewish historical accounts (such as those recorded by Al-Baladhuri and later Jewish chroniclers), a local Jewish resident named Yusef (Joseph) reportedly showed the Muslim army a secret subterranean passage or weak point in the city's fortifications, allowing the troops to breach the city defenses and end the Byzantine siege.   

3. Early Levant & Mesopotamian Campaigns (630s–640s AD)
The Context: The Jewish populations of Byzantine Syria and Palestine had experienced intense persecution, especially following the Byzantine-Sassanid War (602–628 AD), where Emperor Heraclius outlawed Judaism and executed many Jews after retaking Jerusalem.The Assistance: When Arab armies invaded Byzantine Syria, local Jewish communities frequently served as scouts, guides, or suppliers for the Arab forces. Because both Jews and local non-Chalcedonian Christians were treated as second-class citizens or heretics by Constantinople, many welcomed the incoming Arab forces, who offered dhimmi status—which guaranteed freedom of worship in exchange for paying a tax (jizya).

text:
The Things We Do to Each Other and Call It Love...

I still don’t fully understand why we forgive so much cruelty when someone says it was love. We condemn possessiveness in principle, then call it devotion when someone cannot bear to let us go. We talk about sacrifice as though it is always noble, without asking who is giving things up, what it costs them, or whether they ever felt free to refuse. And we are strangely reluctant to question someone who insists that everything they did came from love.

The word itself is part of the trouble. We use it for experiences that have very little in common. There is wanting someone to be happy for their own sake, and there is being unable to bear their happiness without us. There is tenderness that comes from understanding someone, and there is desperate attachment born of fear. Both can feel overwhelming. Perhaps that is why we confuse them so easily.

The old stories understood this. Paris desired Helen, and Troy burned, though wounded honour, political ambition, and the decisions of powerful men helped bring about its destruction. Orpheus descended into the underworld for Eurydice, only to lose her when he looked back. Medea, betrayed by Jason, murdered her own children. None of these were simple love stories. They showed that powerful feelings could exist alongside vanity, fear, revenge, and a terrible disregard for who else might suffer.

We have not changed very much.

What stays with me is not the dramatic cruelty of those stories. It is the ordinary damage people inflict while still thinking of themselves as decent human beings...Someone who knows exactly what frightens their partner and uses it during an argument. Someone who withholds affection because they want the other person to experience a little of the insecurity they have felt. Someone who repeatedly threatens to leave, not because they intend to go, but because they need to hear themselves being begged to stay.

These things often begin with fear rather than malice. That makes them harder to confront, particularly when both people genuinely care.Aristotle believed that real affection meant wishing another person well for their own sake. I have always found that idea persuasive. Living by it is another matter. We want the people we love to be happy. Then their happiness stops depending on us, and suddenly our generosity is tested in ways we never anticipated.

Letting someone go looks noble from a distance. When it is happening to you, the experience is rather different. Your mind understands the reasons. The rest of you refuses to cooperate.

We also bring far more of our past into relationships than we realise. Not necessarily the stories we tell over dinner, but the quieter things. The child who waited for affection that never arrived. The teenager who learned that being vulnerable invited ridicule. The adult who trusted someone completely and discovered too late that the trust was not mutual.

Those experiences do not disappear because we meet someone kind.

A delayed message can mean nothing to one person and feel like abandonment to another. An innocent remark can touch a humiliation that has survived for decades. Someone who has experienced repeated loss may need reassurance that another person finds difficult to understand.

We are all unfinished in places.

But our histories cannot remain permanent excuses. At some point, understanding why we behave as we do must lead to responsibility for how we treat others. Otherwise, the person who loves us becomes responsible for injuries they never caused, and their patience is treated as something they must continue giving.

Two people can become trapped in this without either being particularly unkind. One withdraws when distressed. The other experiences withdrawal as rejection and begins asking for reassurance. That makes the first person retreat further. Eventually both feel attacked, both believe they are trying to save the relationship, and neither understands why the other cannot see what seems so obvious.

I find something terribly sad about that. Especially when both people are intelligent, sensitive, and capable of remarkable kindness towards everyone except each other in those particular moments.

We admire suffering more than we probably should. We praise the person who waits for years, the lover who forgives everything, the one who abandons personal ambitions for someone else. Literature has made such devotion beautiful. I wonder what happens to the people who attempt to live according to those ideals.

What remains of someone who has spent years making themselves smaller to accommodate another person's needs? What happens when sacrifice becomes so habitual that they forget it was ever a choice?

Every serious relationship involves compromise. But there is a difference between making room for someone in your life and gradually removing yourself from it.

Fromm described love as a practice involving care, responsibility, respect, and knowledge. That makes more sense to me than the idea that love simply happens to us. Attraction happens. Longing happens. We do not always choose the person whose absence unsettles us or whose happiness begins to matter so much.

How we treat that person is another matter.

We can feel jealous without interrogating them. We can be frightened without threatening to leave. We can be angry without reaching for the one insecurity they trusted us never to use against them.

I am also uneasy with the way we have begun treating departure as though it is always evidence of strength. Sometimes leaving is necessary, especially when dignity or safety is at stake. But people also leave because they cannot apologise, cannot bear being questioned, or refuse to examine their own part in what went wrong.

Fear can sound remarkably like principle when our pride needs defending.

Staying can be just as dishonest. People remain together because they fear loneliness, social judgment, financial uncertainty, or the prospect of beginning again. They call it commitment, even when the relationship has ceased to nourish either of them.

I would want to know what happened before the decision, what was tried, what was ignored, and whether either person still had room to be themselves.

Two people can love each other deeply and still be unable to live together without causing harm. We prefer stories in which love is either genuine and ultimately victorious, or false and therefore destined to fail. Real relationships rarely oblige us with such tidy conclusions.

Two people may share a sense of humour, hold similar values, recognise something familiar in each other's loneliness, and experience a tenderness unlike anything they have known before. Yet they may disagree about trust, boundaries, reassurance, or what commitment actually requires.

They may hurt each other repeatedly while remaining completely sincere when they say, "I love you."

Meaning it does not repair the damage.

There is a particular loneliness in being misunderstood by someone who knows you intimately. A stranger's opinion seldom reaches the places where we are most vulnerable. But someone who has heard our private fears, who knows the childhood memories we rarely discuss, who has seen us cry without embarrassment, can wound us in ways that are difficult to explain.

Sometimes the injury is not even what they say. It is the sudden realisation that they could believe such a thing about us.

And the person who said it may be somewhere else, equally devastated, convinced that we have misunderstood them.

How many relationships have ended in that silence?

Two people waiting for the other to speak first. Both remembering what was said. Both rehearsing what they would say if the other finally called. Days pass. Then weeks. Pride becomes a habit, and the habit begins to resemble indifference.

By the time one finds the courage to reach out, the other may have learned to live without expecting it.

There is no great philosophical revelation here. It is simply sad.

We speak endlessly about communication, but listening becomes difficult the moment we feel accused. We begin preparing our defence before the other person has finished speaking. We correct details, bring up old injuries, challenge interpretations, and lose sight of the pain that started the conversation.

One of the hardest things to say is, "I understand why that hurt you, even though hurting you was not what I intended."

It requires us to accept that our intentions and another person's experience can both be real. An apology does not become meaningless because there was no malice. Forgiveness does not become compulsory because the apology was sincere.

People deserve the dignity of their own pain.

There is suffering in love that no amount of wisdom can prevent. We love people who are mortal, imperfect, and capable of changing in ways neither they nor we can fully control. Distance hurts. Illness hurts. Misunderstanding hurts. The thought of losing someone whose presence has become part of our ordinary days can be frightening beyond reason.

There are mornings when someone understands every argument for acceptance and still reaches instinctively for a person who is no longer there.

The body does not always obey what the mind has accepted.

But the pain that comes with loving another human being is not the same as the suffering we knowingly cause them. We cannot eliminate the first. We should be answerable for the second.

This is where love becomes a matter of conscience.

Not in the intensity of our declarations or the grandeur of our sacrifices, but in what we do when we are disappointed, frightened, or angry. Whether we can disagree without humiliating. Whether we can ask for reassurance without demanding submission. Whether we can acknowledge a mistake without immediately listing the other person's failures.

Suffering does not necessarily make us wiser. Sometimes it makes us compassionate. Sometimes it leaves us suspicious and unnecessarily harsh. Age offers no guarantee either. People can repeat the same mistakes for decades while becoming increasingly articulate about why they were right.

I find that last possibility particularly unsettling. We can spend years examining what others have done to us and remarkably little time considering what we have done to them.

We remember the evenings we waited for a call, but not always the mornings we withheld affection. We remember the accusations that wounded us, but forget the careless things we said when we were frightened. Our own suffering is vivid. The suffering we caused often survives in our memory as a misunderstanding.

Perhaps that is why we are so concerned with whether another person truly loved us, while neglecting a more revealing question:

What was it like for them to be loved by us?

Did they feel heard? Were they free to disagree? Could they speak about their fears without wondering whether those fears would later be used against them? Did our presence bring them some measure of peace, or did they gradually become anxious about saying the wrong thing?

These questions are uncomfortable because they do not allow us to hide behind the strength of our feelings.

I do not believe there is a universal rule for deciding when someone should stay, forgive, or walk away. Human relationships contain too much history, too many private injuries, and too many circumstances that outsiders never see. Some deserve another attempt. Others have already demanded more than anyone should have been expected to give.

But love should make us more careful with another person's humanity, not less.

If someone has trusted us enough to reveal the parts of themselves they conceal from most of the world, that trust ought to mean something even after affection has changed. Especially then.

We may not preserve the relationship. We may not even preserve the tenderness with which it began. But we can refuse to turn what we once knew about someone into a means of hurting them.

That matters more to me than most of the magnificent promises people make when they are happy.

I keep returning to the thought that the greatest wrong we commit in the name of love is believing that the strength of our feelings somehow excuses what those feelings have led us to do.

The real measure may not be how much we were prepared to suffer for someone, but how seriously we took the possibility of making them suffer.

And I cannot consider that question without thinking about my own conduct, not merely the behaviour of others.

After all, it is easy to remember how deeply we https://t.co/dEmyHc3R6k takes more honesty to remember how we behaved while we were loving.

text:
2026 WILL NOT BE DECIDED BY WHO HAS THE BIGGEST ONLINE AUDIENCE. IT WILL BE DECIDED BY WHO ACTUALLY SHOWS UP.

Whether you think we are winning or you feel like we are losing, put in one hundred percent.
This is not only about the scoreboard. This is a historical moment. In most cycles, one side is already written off. The race is not close, and the side that is down stops working. This is not that cycle. Control of Congress is still in play, and the margins that decide it are the kind a ground game can move. This is one of the closest midterms in a long time.
Do not lose motivation. Let that closeness push you harder. This is the cycle where showing up can make history.

We are in the final stretch.
Election Day is November 3. Twenty-seven days. Early voting is already open. Ballots are already out. Chasing a ballot that never gets cast is not the job anymore.
The job is getting the vote out of the house and into the booth.

New York already ran this play. In the 2025 mayor’s race, the other side did not win on posts. It won on a volunteer army: doors, a plan to vote, and someone willing to get the voter to the poll site before it closed. The campaign reported more than 100,000 volunteers, 3.1 million doors, 4.6 million calls, and 2.7 million texts.

Same tactic. Our voters. Our doors.
Knock. Motivate. Confirm the plan. If they need a ride, give them the ride. Walk them to the booth.
FREE TIME ≠ ORGANIZATION. FOLLOWERS ≠ VOLUNTEERS. SIGNUPS ≠ COMPLETED SHIFTS. A TEXT ≠ A VOTE CAST.

The decisive question in the last month is simple:
Which side gets its people out of the house and to the voting booth before November 3?

For people who have already decided to participate, the field work is already running:

@ScottPresler / Early Vote Action — calls, texts, letters, and grassroots field activity.

@TPAction / Turning Point Action — Chase the Vote: canvassing, calls, events, and getting voters to cast a ballot.

Commit 100 / Citizens Alliance — training and direct voter contact, including Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

@AFPAction / Americans for Prosperity Action — canvassing, phone outreach, and grassroots field organizing.

@Heritage_Action / Heritage Action Sentinels — grassroots organizing and activist development.

@LeadershipInst / Leadership Institute — campaign, volunteer, and grassroots-organizing training.
Christian and Catholic voter contact is the same job in a different room. A church foyer and a parish hall can move a voter to the booth as fast as a turf packet.

@FaithandFreedom / Faith & Freedom Coalition — home visits, calls, texts, and voter education among evangelicals and Catholics. Its 2026 plan calls for 6 million doors through the end of October.

@CatholicVote — local chapters, voter guides, calls, and texts. Call the people in your parish. Ask them when they are voting. Offer the ride.

@ivoterguide — biblical-values voter guides for church distribution before people leave for the polls.
Latino Republican field work:

@libre_action / LIBRE Action — door knocks and calls aimed at Hispanic voters in battleground states.
Republican National Hispanic Assembly — state chapters for registration where the window is still open, events, and volunteer recruitment.
And follow people who spend their time on actual field organization:

If you’ve already chosen to participate, the progression is the same on a porch, in a church foyer, or on a Spanish-language turf:

SHOW UP → KNOCK → MOTIVATE → CONFIRM THE PLAN → GET THEM TO THE BOOTH → RETURN → TRAIN OTHERS

A repost can spread information.
A donation can fund the ride.
A knock creates the conversation.
A ride creates the vote.
The final stretch will not be decided by which side was loudest online. It will be decided by who is still at the door, and who is still driving people to the booth, on November 3.
Win or lose the feeling. One hundred percent. This is the moment. Make history.

text:
Here's what happened to Michael Jordan's impact compared to his team's overall production for him to become a 6-time Champion:
🏀After his injury ridden 1985-86 season, Jordan came back with 3 straight regular seasons with over 0.42+ Win Shares per Team Win in games he played. The bigger role a player had in a RS, eventually leading to an NBA title, was 1971-Kareem at 0.338 WS per TMW. 
In 1989 Collins had Jordan doing everything on offense (shooting and passing) for the Bulls to win 3 less games than the year before.
🏀Jordan's first season with Phil Jackson as the head coach, even before his supporting cast was fully ready to compete for a title, led to a drop from 0.421 to 0.345 Win Shares per team Win, while the Bulls improved their record by 8 wins.
🏀A year after, Jordan came up with a ~0.333 WS/TMW season, the 2nd best title season I found behind Kareem's 1971 campaign.
🏀During the Bulls two 3-peat seasons, Jordan had the following seasons based on this evaluation:
1991-0.333
1992-0.265
1993-0.308
1996-0.284
1997-0.265
1998-0.255
🏀Players like Russell (4) Shaq (3) or Lebron (2) had multiple Championship seasons over the 0.25 plateau. Jordan leads all players with 6 of them and that's why for most people he continues to be the undisputed GOAT.
🏀The impact of Jackson getting the job as the head coach and implementing Tex Winters' Triangle Offense is clear. More players impacting the game while making sure, Jordan would have the ball when it was time to win the game. 
🏀If a team doesn't show, during the RS,  the ability to get some pressure off the star player or players, they won't manage to do it during the playoffs. Even high impact has its limit and based on this evaluation the high limit is around one third of a team's production in wins.
🏀Among RS Win Shares team leaders who ended up leading their team to a title, 7 of them managed to do it, a total of 9 times, after having a RS with over 0.3 WS per TMW. 
In only 3 of those 9 seasons the team wasn't a top seed in its conference:
➡️1993 Bulls (Jordan) 2nd
➡️2006 Heat (Wade) 2nd
➡️2012 Heat (Lebron) 2nd
All three of those teams had either a star and/or key contributors missing a number of games during the RS, but those players were available in the playoffs to offer enough decoys to their star player.

Conclusion: Phil Jackson was right.

text:
Phil Jackson says he told Michael Jordan he needed to score less if he wanted to win a championship because scoring titles and championships don’t go together

“When I was given the job as the head coach of the Chicago Bulls, I brought Michael Jordan in to speak with me, and I said, ‘You know, you’ve averaged 37, 38, 36 points a game the last three years. You know, you’ve been the scoring champion, but if you look back at the history of the NBA, there hasn’t been a scoring champion for almost 15 years who’s won the championship. They don’t go together.’”

“‘And we need to take the focus off you, which is what teams now tilt their whole defense towards, stopping Michael Jordan, and open it up for the rest of our team. And it means you taking less shots a game. That’s important.’ And he stopped me and he said, ‘Are you going to run an equal-opportunity offense like Tex Winter’s been talking about?’”

“I said, ‘Yeah, I guess you could call it an equal-opportunity offense, but I’m not going to be calling the plays from the sideline. You guys are going to be reading it on the floor. So if the 24-second clock is running down and it becomes red, which is the call everybody makes when it’s under five seconds, we’ll teach the team how to get the ball to you at the end of that clock because then you can score.’”

“He said, ‘Well, I don’t think that I have to give up a scoring championship. I could score 32 points a game and still win a scoring championship. That’s only eight points a quarter.’ I said, ‘Michael, I had trouble scoring eight points a game when I was a player.’”

“‘But rather than scoring eight points a quarter, why don’t you save that for the fourth quarter and score 14 points in the fourth quarter and take us home? And you can do what you want to do during the early part of the game and then put the onus and the nail in the coffin in the fourth quarter to seal the deal.’ He kind of liked that idea.”

“And, you know, I think we lost two or three of our first games that we played in my first year coaching, and everybody had to kind of figure out how to do it, how to play together when the ball was dictating the action, when the passes were dictating what people would do, rather than a specific number for a player being called from the sideline. And I gave the team a little bit of authority, which is exactly what a coach wants to happen.”

🇾🇪|Al-Yatmah in Northern Al-Jawf: Abandoned Vehicles Tell a More Telling Story Than Destroyed Ones

Ansar Allah’s military media has released footage from the Al-Yatmah front, showing strikes on positions held by Saudi-aligned forces. Vehicles were destroyed; others were captured.

Yet, the most significant aspect of the footage is not the vehicles reduced to wreckage, but rather those left entirely intact with fuel still in their tanks and keys still in the ignition.

💥 An Abandoned Vehicle Is a Confession

Destroying a vehicle requires a missile. Capturing an intact one, however, requires only a single decision by its owner: to flee.

Destroyed vehicles are a testament to raw firepower; captured vehicles are evidence of a collapse in will. A vehicle left behind at a position implies that its owner was not inside when the strike hit they had already departed. They chose survival over dying for a Saudi Arabian paycheck.

The footage from Al-Yatmah shows both destroyed and captured vehicles. This reveals that the nature of the battle was not simply a case of "overwhelming firepower obliterating everything in its path." Instead, it suggests a mixed scenario: some forces chose to resist and were destroyed, while others offered no resistance and simply left their vehicles behind.

🎯 Why Al-Yatmah?

Al-Yatmah is located in the northern part of Al-Jawf Governorate, which shares a border with Saudi Arabia. This border has been an active front since the very first day of the war in Yemen. It serves as a staging ground for Saudi-backed forces, a point from which they launch incursions into the Yemeni interior, and a hub where they receive supplies and salaries from Saudi Arabia.

The positions at Al-Yatmah do not constitute a "defense in depth"; rather, they are forward-deployed outposts. Their purpose is to project power into Yemen while acting as an outer buffer for Saudi Arabia’s own border defenses. When these positions are struck and seized, it is not Yemen’s interior defenses that are weakened, but the buffer zone protecting the Saudi border.  Losing ground in this location means the buffer zone along the Saudi border is narrowing.

📜 Who is driving these vehicles?

The composition of the Saudi-aligned mobilization forces is clear: local tribal militias, commanders who have been bought off, and fighters on the Saudi payroll. Their equipment is provided by Saudi Arabia; their vehicles are supplied by Saudi Arabia; their salaries are paid by Saudi Arabia.

Yet, they are not Saudi soldiers. They are Yemenis or mercenaries fighting for Saudi Arabia on the Yemeni battlefield. Their loyalty is contractual. When the contract can no longer be honored when Saudi Arabia fails to provide air cover, supplies, or an escape route the contract effectively expires.

The vehicles captured in Al-Yatmah serve as physical evidence that these contracts have failed.

⚔️ The Calculus of the Northern Front

The fighting in the northern part of Al-Jawf Governorate is not an isolated event. It is one node in a broader process, a process that includes the collapse in Taiz, the advances along the West Coast, and the missile strikes on the Ma'ashiq Palace in Aden.

Saudi Arabia’s war in Yemen relies on proxy forces; it has no ground troops of its own. Its air force can conduct bombardments, but it cannot hold territory. Its navy can enforce a blockade, but it cannot exert control over the land. These proxy forces constitute its only presence on the ground.

When these proxies begin to abandon their vehicles, desert their positions, and refuse to fight, the Saudi presence on the ground shrinks not because it has been destroyed, but because it has been abandoned.

Destroyed equipment can be replaced; abandoned loyalties cannot.

🔻 Beyond the Frame

The footage released by military media outlets is carefully edited. It shows destroyed vehicles, captured hardware, and overrun positions. What it does not show is where those who fled have gone, whether Saudi Arabia will punish them, or whether the next position will meet the same fate.

Yet, there is a reality beyond the frame that requires no visual proof: if the Saudi-aligned forces had managed to hold Al-Yatmah, this footage would not exist.

The sole reason these images exist is that they failed to hold their ground.  Long live Yemen. Long live Ansar Allah. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

text:
George Orwell published 1984 in 1949.

He imagined a society where surveillance was everywhere, technology watched the population continuously, information was centralized, and powerful institutions could track individuals while knowing more about their lives than the individuals knew about the system watching them.

Look at what exists now.

Palantir’s Maven Smart System uses artificial intelligence to combine massive amounts of information into a single operational picture.

Satellite imagery.

Drone feeds.

Computer vision.

Geospatial intelligence.

Radar and sensor data.

Object identification.

Location tracking.

Movement analysis.

Target identification.

Real-time data fusion.

CENTCOM was reportedly pulling information from 179 different data sources through Maven by 2024.

That's the important part.

The technology doesn’t need one magical camera watching everything.

It connects information that was previously scattered across separate systems and turns it into one searchable, actionable picture.

Now look outside the military.

Cameras cover cities.

License-plate readers record vehicle movement.

Phones continuously generate location data.

Facial-recognition systems can identify people.

Financial systems document purchases.

Biometric systems increasingly connect identity to the body.

Digital-ID infrastructure is expanding.

AI can correlate enormous datasets faster than human analysts ever could.

Connect those dots.

The architecture required for a surveillance society already exists.

Maven demonstrates what happens when AI becomes the layer connecting the sensors, databases and intelligence systems together.

That's what makes this bigger than one Palantir product.

This is the direction modern surveillance is moving.

Orwell imagined telescreens.

We carry networked cameras, microphones, GPS sensors and biometric devices ourselves.

He imagined centralized records.

We now generate enormous digital records of our locations, communications, purchases, relationships and behavior.

He imagined automated control over information.

AI now makes it possible to analyze those records at a scale no government in Orwell’s lifetime could have imagined.

Military systems are often where advanced surveillance capabilities mature first. Once the underlying technology exists, the question becomes where else it gets deployed and what limits society places on it.

Project Maven shows that AI can turn hundreds of separate information streams into one operational picture.

What happens when the same architecture incorporates facial recognition, digital identity, financial data and behavioral profiles?

How much anonymity survives when cameras and sensors become searchable through AI instead of requiring someone to manually watch them?

Who decides what behavior deserves attention?

Who controls the algorithm deciding who becomes a person of interest?

And what happens when surveillance becomes so integrated into everyday infrastructure that people stop noticing it?

1984 wasn’t really about cameras.

It was about centralized power made possible by information, surveillance and control.

The technology to build that kind of system is here now.

Bucket 5: The 911 and whistle assignment

To everyone in Clark County who uses emergency services: call 911 when there is a genuine emergency. Report specific facts. Don’t embellish. Don’t turn a personal disagreement into a claim of immediate danger unless the facts justify it.

To dispatch supervisors and relevant oversight personnel: review credible concerns about inaccurate or repeated reporting through the appropriate process.

I am maintaining a working timeline of calls and records involving my household. The count must be reconciled against duplicates and the distinction between 911 and 311 contacts before it is treated as final.

The assignment is to establish the facts for each incident individually.

Who called? What did the caller report? What did dispatch relay? What did the responding personnel observe? What outcome was documented?

If a complaint was legitimate, the record should reflect that. If a report was knowingly false or an emergency system was improperly used, the evidence should be referred for appropriate review.

We protect emergency services by treating them seriously, not by using them as weapons in a neighborhood dispute.

Bucket 6: CPS, family services, and every parent in Nevada

To child-welfare workers: follow the law, document the basis for decisions, protect confidential information, and keep the child’s actual welfare at the center of the process.

To supervisors: ensure that concerns are assessed fairly and that parents receive the notices, explanations, and review procedures they are legally entitled to.

To parents: preserve letters, record dates, keep copies of submissions, and seek qualified legal assistance when a decision could affect custody or parental rights.

My family has been affected by concerns involving neighborhood reports and child-welfare contacts. I want the facts and the applicable procedures to be clear. I am not asking strangers online to contact workers at my home, interfere with an investigation, or publish confidential information about children.

The assignment is to demand lawful, evidence-based process while protecting the privacy and safety of every child involved.

Children are not bargaining chips. Parents are not automatically guilty because somebody made a report. And legitimate safety concerns must never be ignored.

Bucket 7: The HOA — rules are not a license to punish

To HOA boards and property managers: enforce community rules consistently, explain decisions, document the evidence, and provide the process required by law and the governing documents.

My family has disputed HOA actions, including fines and restrictions affecting my daughter’s use of the community pool. Those are matters that should be examined against the governing documents, the notices, the hearing record, and the applicable Nevada law.

The assignment for residents is to request the relevant rules, meeting minutes, notices, enforcement records, and appeal procedures through lawful channels.

The assignment for the HOA is to explain the basis for its decisions and apply its rules fairly.

No neighbor should be encouraged to harass another household. No board should treat criticism as proof of a violation. And no resident should assume a rule was applied unlawfully without examining the actual record.

If the process was fair, document it. If it was not, correct it.

Bucket 8: A special assignment concerning prescription-medication concerns

I have a separate concern based on statements I say I heard from a neighbor about prescription medication. I have described being offered medication for sale and hearing claims about medication being shared with another person. I declined the offer.

I cannot independently establish everything about those statements, and I will not diagnose anyone or speculate about another person’s medical condition.

But prescription medication should be used only as prescribed and handled lawfully.

Talent spotting starts early, and Beijing has just asked for 100,000 young Americans.

🇮🇷🇮🇶| The Baghdad Resolution: A Shelved Condemnation and an Ignored Ledger

Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister stated two things in Baghdad. First, the meeting would adopt several documents, including a final report titled the "Baghdad Report." Second, these documents include a resolution by the foreign ministers condemning the Israeli regime and the United States for their attacks on Iran.

Taken together, these two points offer the most precise self-portrait of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).

💥 A Resolution Drafted a Year Ago

The Deputy Foreign Minister made it clear: these documents were finalized by experts about a year ago. A year ago. Back when the "third imposed war" was still raging, when schoolchildren in Minab were being killed in bombings, and when 87 hospitals and clinics had already been destroyed that was when the experts drafted this resolution. It was then left to gather dust for a year.

Now, it is being "re-adopted" in Baghdad.

The term "re-adopted" perfectly encapsulates the entire function of the OIC. It is not "adopted for the first time." It is not "adopted as an emergency measure." It is not "adopted and implemented." It is merely *re-adopted* just as it was adopted last year, and the year before that.

The substance of the resolution is "condemnation." Condemning Israel. Condemning the United States. Condemning the attacks on Iran. The language of this condemnation was carefully crafted by experts: strong enough for Iranian representatives to return home and claim, "We have the support of the Islamic world," yet vague enough for representatives from Saudi Arabia and the UAE to return home and insist, "We did not specify any particular military response."

🎯 What Has Changed Between Then and Now?

A year ago, hospitals in Iran were still smoldering. A year ago, Israeli bombs were falling on Gaza. Today, the death toll in Gaza has climbed from 20,000 to 74,000.

A year ago, the U.S. naval blockade was still in place in the Strait of Hormuz.  A year later, the blockade remains, but Iranian oil tankers have found ways to circumvent it; liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) is being transferred from ship to ship in the Gulf of Oman, bound for Malaysia and China.

The timing of the resolution’s adoption is more revealing than its actual content. It was not passed during the height of the conflict, but rather when the war had reached a stalemate, a moment when all parties were busy recalibrating their positions.

📜 Who Needs This Resolution?

Iran needs it not because it can alter the situation on the battlefield, but because it establishes a legal record within the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC): a majority of its 57 member states have formally condemned attacks on Iran by the United States and Israel. While this cannot stop bombs from falling, it serves as a reference point for future negotiations, international legal proceedings, and the eventual writing of history.

Saudi Arabia and the UAE need it. They require a public vote condemning Israel to maintain their standing within the Islamic world, even as they continue to engage in intelligence sharing and arms deals with Israel. The vote is public; the dealings are private. The resolution allows the public stance to stand, while the private arrangements continue undisturbed.

Türkiye needs it. Having just handed over the chairmanship to Iraq, Türkiye needed a "deliverable" to show that the OIC had not been entirely idle during its tenure.

Every nation that voted in favor needed this resolution, yet none of them required it to produce any tangible, real-world consequences.

⚔️ What Is the "Baghdad Report"?

The Deputy Foreign Minister mentioned the "Baghdad Report," a final document summarizing the discussions and decisions of the meeting. It includes a reaffirmation of the Palestinian cause, condemnation of the expansion of Israeli settlements, expressions of concern regarding the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, and calls for economic cooperation among Islamic nations.

It serves as the official record of the meeting. It will be archived, translated into multiple languages, and distributed to all member states. Ultimately, it will find its place on a shelf in some foreign ministry’s archives, sitting alongside the final reports of the previous fifty summits.

Its purpose is not to guide action; its purpose is to prove that the meeting took place.  In a system that requires demonstrating to a domestic public that "something is being done," a final report serves as evidence that "something has indeed been done."

🔻 The Real Decisions Are Not Made in Baghdad

Resolutions will be passed in Baghdad. Applause will fill the hall. Delegates will shake hands. Journalists will take photographs.

Yet, in that same week, a U.S. C-5M transport aircraft lands at Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, carrying missile components and radar systems. Saudi Arabian F-15 fighter jets equipped with Israeli-made helmets take off from Khamis Mushait. The Egyptian parliament prepares to authorize Sisi to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia. Turkish drones continue to flow toward Riyadh.

The real decisions are not drafted in the conference halls of Baghdad; they are forged in the situation rooms of Washington, Tel Aviv, and Riyadh. The resolutions in Baghdad are a response to these actual decisions not a substitute for them.

Nevertheless, such a response is not without value. It establishes a record: within the official annals of the Islamic world, the United States and Israel are cast as the aggressors, while Iran is identified as the party under attack. This record may not alter the situation today, but it will shift the starting point for future debates.

Long live Iran. Long live the Resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

text:
Rep. Jayapal told a health-policy crowd where her new slogan came from: "in our focus groups and in our polling is the idea of freedom."

So I read the bill. H.R. 3069, Section 107. It makes it UNLAWFUL for an insurer, or your employer, to offer coverage that duplicates the government plan.

Freedom.

Medicare for All is not freedom. It is enslavement. Once Washington is the only legal payer, the government literally holds your life, your kids' future, and the answer to whether your wife gets to fight her cancer or gets handed the paperwork for assisted suicide. Every one of those calls moves from your kitchen table to a federal budget office.

Pramila. You did not find freedom in the bill. You found it in a focus group and glued it to the cover. That is muddying the water to make it look deep.

Pencils out. Let's grade the speech.

"It has taken away people's freedom." People stay in jobs they don't love because of the benefits.

Since 2014, no insurer can turn you down for a pre-existing condition. Leaving a job does not cost you the right to buy coverage. An HSA already follows the worker, and since 2020 an employer can hand you tax-free money for an individual plan that goes with you when you quit. The cure for being chained to your boss's plan is letting you OWN your plan. Her cure is chaining you to a bigger boss you can never quit. You can change jobs. You cannot change countries. Well... Canadians do. More than 105,000 of them left Canada for treatment in a single year.

"Freedom to switch jobs."

In 2019 she told reporters her bill would push about one million private insurance employees out of work. Freedom to switch jobs, delivered by deleting a million of them. Slight oversight!

"Medium sized businesses... can't afford to compete with corporations."

Ask who pays. When Bernie released his own menu of ways to fund this in 2019, it included a 7.5 percent premium on employer payroll. Every worker, every paycheck, whether the shop made money that month or not. A small business does not compete better when Washington takes a cut of every wage before the owner sees a dime. That plan couldn't pour water out of a boot with instructions on the heel.

"Without worrying about losing your healthcare."

You won't lose your coverage. You'll lose the date. Fraser's 2025 survey puts Canada's median wait from GP referral to treatment at 28.6 weeks, triple what it was in 1993. Neurosurgery, 49.9 weeks. Canada's own Supreme Court wrote it down in Chaoulli: access to a waiting list is not access to health care. And under Section 107, there is no private door out of that line.

Let me get this straight, using your logic. Groceries for All. One federal grocery store, and it becomes unlawful for Kroger to sell any food the government store already stocks. Never again worry about losing your grocery budget when you switch jobs. The shelves get restocked on Washington's schedule, and you get the freedom of 28 weeks between milk deliveries. It's just common sense.

What's next, a state-run plan writes a grandmother with lung cancer to say it won't pay for her cancer pill, but physician aid in dying is covered... wait, I'm being told Oregon's state-run health plan already did that. 2008. Barbara Wagner, 64, a retired school bus driver. The drug company ended up giving her the medicine for free. The government had offered her the other prescription.

Canada took the same road further. Health Canada reports 16,499 assisted deaths in 2024, about one of every twenty deaths in the country. When the treatment line is long and the death line is short, some desperate people take the short one. Your own state legalized assisted suicide in 2008, Congresswoman. Put one payer in charge of the cancer list AND the shortcut, and you've handed Washington the pen that wrote the Oregon letter.

Funny thing about your bill... it leaves the VA alone. The VA is the government plan I was on when my shoulder surgery got pushed back three years. Apparently that line was already free enough.

Quinn's Law Number Nine: to a liberal, intentions matter more than outcomes. A focus group measures how a word FEELS. It never measures how long the wait is. You can lead a person to Congress, but you can't make them read Section 107.

When the list says 28 weeks, a free country lets you walk out the door and pay someone else. Your bill bolts that door shut and paints FREEDOM on it.

I laid out the full case, and the plan the right supposedly doesn't have, here: https://t.co/P5ktRdp2O8

But what do I know, I'm only a medic who already did three years in the government line, and a teacher who read Section 107 before clapping for the word freedom.

WASHINGTON BUILT A 100% TARIFF WEAPON AGAINST RUSSIAN OIL BUYERS—THEN SUSPENDED IT BEFORE IT TOOK EFFECT.

On September 18, President Trump signed a law designed to raise the cost of supporting Russia’s energy economy.

It authorized sweeping penalties:

• A 500% tariff on Russian goods.
• A 100% tariff on goods from the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas, subject to statutory conditions.
• A separate 100% tariff targeting the five largest facilitators of Russian oil sanctions evasion.

On October 16, just before the new measures were due to take effect, Trump waived these tariffs, citing U.S. national interests.

Why does this matter for China?

Beijing is one of Moscow’s most important energy customers. Russian oil sales help sustain Russia’s export revenues while its war against Ukraine continues.

The new law offered Washington a powerful potential source of leverage: countries maintaining major Russian energy purchases could face substantial costs in accessing the American market.

That pressure has now been suspended.

The waiver does not eliminate existing Russia sanctions, nor does it prove that China has violated sanctions. But it postpones a new financial deterrent that could have affected Beijing’s calculations.

There is another contradiction: the White House supported the legislation before it became law, yet has now declined to activate major provisions.

The deeper issue is the credibility of American economic pressure.

If Washington repeatedly threatens severe penalties but declines to enforce them, Beijing and Moscow may have less reason to treat future warnings as credible.

Whether that happens remains to be seen.

The question is no longer just how high U.S. tariffs can go.

It is whether America’s adversaries believe Washington will actually use them.

text:
HUMXN Offers Free Home Repairs to Collect AI Robot Training Data

What if the data needed to train future robots came from ordinary home repairs?

AI data company HUMXN has announced a program covering eligible home-service appointments in Minneapolis, Chicago, and Miami. The services include plumbing, electrical work, HVAC maintenance, air-duct cleaning, and carpet cleaning.

The unusual part is how the work becomes training data. Human technicians perform the repairs while wearable recording devices capture their activities from a first-person perspective. HUMXN intends to turn those recordings into datasets for AI and robotics development.

This approach highlights an important challenge for physical AI. Learning about a repair from written instructions is different from observing how a skilled worker examines a problem, selects tools, and responds to changing conditions.

The potential value lies in collecting examples of real work outside controlled laboratory environments.

But there are important limits. HUMXN has not publicly demonstrated that robots trained on this specific dataset can independently perform these repairs. The number of completed appointments, the amount of collected footage, and the effectiveness of the resulting training data remain unverified.

The broader question is whether everyday human work could become a scalable source of training data for future robots.

#Robotics #PhysicalAI
